In complete-case analyses (n = 89), each doubling of neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) was associated with higher hazards in the composite Cox model (HR, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.10–1.96), time-varying Fine-Gray model (sHR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.03–2.01), and cause-specific Cox model (HR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.14–2.19). CD4/CD8 ratio was associated with composite and cause-specific hazards but not with the Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard. The reduced static model had an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.703 and calibration slope of 0.838; calibration weakened at later horizons.ConclusionHigher baseline NLR showed the most consistent association with both general prognosis and documented intracranial progression after GKRS. The endpoint-dependent CD4/CD8 findings and the internally validated prediction model remain exploratory and require external multicenter validation before clinical use.

items.title: Case Report: Certolizumab pegol as a potential rescue option for severe erythema multiforme associated with pustular psoriasis during pregnancy
items.abstract: BackgroundSevere erythema multiforme (EM) and pustular psoriasis presenting during pregnancy (PPP) are rare inflammatory dermatoses that may adversely affect maternal and fetal outcomes. Their coexistence during pregnancy is exceptionally uncommon, and therapeutic decisions are challenging because of limited evidence and concerns regarding fetal safety.Case presentationA 37-year-old woman at 30 weeks of gestation presented with rapidly progressive targetoid erythema, papulovesicular lesions, blisters, pustules, acral edema, and mild oral mucosal erosion. Severe EM was initially suspected based on the presence of targetoid lesions and mucosal involvement. During hospitalization, the development of sterile pustules and pustular plaques suggested concomitant PPP. Histopathological examination demonstrated interface dermatitis with focal epidermal necrosis in the arm lesion, consistent with EM, and intraepidermal pustule formation with neutrophilic infiltration in the abdominal lesion, supporting PPP. Potential EM triggers were investigated. HSV-I/II IgM was positive, whereas Mycoplasma pneumoniae testing was negative; however, no definitive infectious trigger was identified. Hydroxychloroquine, initiated approximately 2 weeks before disease onset by an external obstetrician, was discontinued because drug-associated EM was considered possible, although causality could not be confirmed. Despite treatment with intravenous methylprednisolone, intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), and corticosteroid pulse therapy, the disease continued to progress. Histopathological examination supported the diagnoses of EM and PPP. Genetic analysis revealed wild-type IL36RN and a heterozygous IL36G c.404T > C variant of uncertain significance.Intervention and outcomeAfter infection was excluded and informed consent was obtained, a single dose of certolizumab pegol 400 mg was administered subcutaneously during the early corticosteroid tapering phase following methylprednisolone pulse therapy Cutaneous lesions showed marked improvement within 72 h after certolizumab administration. Corticosteroids were successfully tapered. The patient delivered a healthy male infant vaginally at 39 weeks and 1 day of gestation. No maternal or neonatal adverse events were observed, and remission was maintained during one year of postpartum follow-up.ConclusionThis case highlights the diagnostic complexity and therapeutic challenges of concurrent severe EM and PPP during pregnancy. Although the contribution of previous corticosteroid and IVIG therapy cannot be completely excluded, the temporal association between certolizumab pegol administration and clinical improvement suggests that TNF-α blockade may represent a potential option. Further clinical experience and registry-based studies are required to clarify its efficacy and optimal clinical application.

items.title: Perceived reporting-system function, reporting barriers, and formal near-miss reporting among operating room nurses in China: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: BackgroundNear-miss reporting provides an early signal of perioperative system failure, yet formal reporting remains limited in operating rooms. This study examined correlates of formal near-miss reporting among operating room (OR) nurses at a two-campus tertiary hospital in China.MethodsIn this cross-sectional study, 2,281 OR nurses returned a structured questionnaire and 2,200 were analyzed, covering self-reported 12-month near-miss observation and reporting, four safety-culture indices, workload, and professional characteristics. Exposures were purpose-built indices rather than validated scales. Multivariable logistic regression, with a prespecified parsimonious model as the principal specification, examined factors associated with formal reporting among observers (Model A) and, as an exploratory aim, near-miss observation in the full sample (Model B).ResultsOf 2,200 OR nurses, 1,551 (70.5%) observed at least one perioperative near-miss during the preceding 12 months, yet only 478 (30.8%) formally reported an event; the remaining 1,073 (69.2%) made no report, a nurse-level rather than event-level measure. Count discrepancies predominated (47.3%). In the principal model, perceived reporting-system function was the strongest correlate of formal reporting (aOR: 2.19 per 1-SD increase, 95% CI: 1.84–2.60), whereas greater barrier burden was inversely associated (0.67, 0.57–0.79); speaking-up and safety climate, which overlapped substantially, were not independently associated. The reporting-system association persisted after removal of the feedback item, which may reflect earlier reporting, and ordinal modeling of reported event volume reproduced both associations. Model A discrimination was acceptable (AUC 0.741). In the full sample, higher time pressure was associated with near-miss observation (1.14, 1.03–1.25), but this exploratory model discriminated poorly (AUC 0.600).ConclusionPerioperative near misses were commonly observed but seldom documented. These cross-sectional, self-reported associations cannot establish direction, but they are consistent with formal reporting depending on accessible, easy-to-use reporting systems and on reduced hierarchy-related and relational barriers, rather than on willingness to speak up alone.

items.title: Laboratory indicators combined with liver function scores for predicting suboptimal hepatobiliary phase imaging during gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI
items.abstract: BackgroundSuboptimal hepatobiliary-phase (HBP) enhancement may limit the diagnostic quality of gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI. We investigated whether routinely available laboratory indicators and liver function scores could identify patients at increased risk of suboptimal HBP imaging.MethodsThis retrospective study included 555 patients with focal liver lesions who underwent gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI, including 460 with good and 95 with suboptimal HBP image quality. Associations between laboratory indicators, liver function scores, and HBP image quality were evaluated using correlation and logistic regression analyses. Model discrimination, calibration, internal validation, and potential clinical utility were assessed using ROC analysis, bootstrap resampling, calibration analysis, and decision-curve analysis.ResultsThe ALBI score (OR=2.391, 95% CI: 1.364–4.190), GGT (OR=1.003, 95% CI: 1.001–1.004), TBA (OR=1.010, 95% CI: 1.003–1.017), and Hb (OR=0.982, 95% CI: 0.971–0.993) were independently associated with suboptimal HBP imaging. The combined model yielded an AUC of 0.758 (95% CI: 0.701–0.816), with 63.16% sensitivity and 78.70% specificity. Bootstrap internal validation that repeated the entire model-development procedure yielded a mean AUC optimism of 0.044 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.714, indicating that moderate discrimination was retained after correction for model-development optimism. The apparent and optimism-corrected Brier scores were 0.116 and 0.128, respectively.ConclusionsA model combining the ALBI score, GGT, TBA, and Hb showed moderate discrimination for suboptimal HBP imaging. These routinely available indicators may assist pre-MRI risk stratification, but external validation is required before clinical implementation.

items.title: KAT6B::KANSL1 fusion-positive uterine mesenchymal neoplasm with hybrid endometrial stromal and smooth muscle features: a case report
items.abstract: KAT6B/A::KANSL1 fusion-positive uterine mesenchymal neoplasms are rare and may show overlapping endometrial stromal and smooth muscle features. We report a 47-year-old woman with regular menses, no dysmenorrhea, and a 7-year history of a presumed uterine fibroid. She underwent laparoscopic myomectomy at an outside hospital in November 2024. The fragmented specimen was interpreted as an endometrial stromal tumor with smooth muscle differentiation, but the tumor–myometrium interface could not be assessed, and an endometrial stromal nodule could not be distinguished from low-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma. Subsequent pelvic magnetic resonance imaging showed postoperative changes, possible residual leiomyomas, and heterogeneous enhancement at the uterine fundus. Pelvic computed tomography showed heterogeneous uterine enhancement without definite extrauterine disease. Because the original specimen was fragmented and a potentially malignant uterine mesenchymal neoplasm could not be excluded, completion hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy was performed. The hysterectomy specimen contained multiple residual intramyometrial nodules with marked regional heterogeneity. One component showed fascicular smooth muscle morphology and diffuse desmin and h-caldesmon expression, whereas other nodules showed tongue-like myometrial infiltration, focal intravascular growth, spiral arteriole-like vessels, and diffuse ER, PR, CD10, and SMA expression. Whole-transcriptome sequencing identified an in-frame KAT6B::KANSL1 fusion involving KAT6B exon 3 and KANSL1 exon 11. Because the tumor expressed ER and PR, postoperative letrozole was administered for 30 days, after which surveillance was selected following review of the final pathologic and molecular findings. At 8 months after completion surgery, no clinical or radiologic recurrence was detected; this limited follow-up does not permit conclusions regarding long-term biological behavior or endocrine treatment benefit.

items.title: Primary umbilical endometriosis mimicking a urachal fistula: a case report
items.abstract: BackgroundUmbilical endometriosis is an uncommon form of extrapelvic endometriosis and may be misdiagnosed as other umbilical or urachal disorders. Cyclic umbilical bleeding or discharge is an important clinical clue, but the diagnosis is often confirmed only after surgical excision and histopathological examination.Case presentationA 31-year-old woman presented to the hospital with a history of umbilical discharge for more than one year. The symptom occurred predominantly during menstruation and was characterized by recurrent umbilical discharge with occasional bloody secretion. Physical examination revealed mild erythema and swelling of the umbilicus, without active discharge at the time of examination. Preoperative computed tomography of the lower abdomen and pelvis showed no obvious abnormality. The initial clinical diagnosis was urachal fistula with possible umbilical infection. The patient underwent surgical excision of the umbilical lesion under general anesthesia. Intraoperatively, purulent discharge was observed at the umbilicus, and complete excision of the umbilical lesion was performed. Histopathological examination revealed endometrial glands and stroma beneath the squamous epithelium with hemosiderin deposition, while immunohistochemistry showed CD10, CK7, and PR positivity with negative/weak ER expression, supporting the diagnosis of umbilical endometriosis.ConclusionThis case emphasizes the diagnostic challenge of primary umbilical endometriosis presenting with chronic umbilical discharge. Careful assessment of menstrual history, imaging findings, and pathological examination is essential for accurate diagnosis.

items.title: Machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with venous thromboembolism and acute kidney injury
items.abstract: BackgroundHypoalbuminemia is a prevalent and critical complication among intensive care unit (ICU) patients with venous thromboembolism (VTE) and acute kidney injury (AKI), significantly associated with increased mortality and prolonged hospitalization. However, reliable tools for early prediction of hypoalbuminemia in this high-risk population remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with coexisting VTE and AKI.MethodsIn this retrospective study, data from 585 ICU patients with VTE and AKI were analyzed. Patients were divided into a training cohort (n = 409) and a validation cohort (n = 176). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with standardization was applied for feature selection. Five machine learning models-logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), and support vector machine (SVM)-were developed and evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Decision curve analysis (DCA), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and feature importance were performed for the optimal model. The performance of the best machine learning model was compared with conventional ICU severity scores (APSIII, LODs, and OASIS).ResultsThe standardized LASSO regression identified ten optimal predictors: creatinine (cr), age, tumor/cancer, body mass index (BMI), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), urine output, D-dimer (D_D), Charlson comorbidity index, anticoagulant use, and alanine aminotransferase (ALT). Among the five models, XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance with a validation AUC of 0.882 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.832–0.924], followed by RF (AUC = 0.878), LightGBM (AUC = 0.870), LR (AUC = 0.838), and SVM (AUC = 0.662). The 5-fold cross-validation AUC for XGBoost was 0.901 ± 0.042, with minimal overfitting (CV-test difference = −0.019). Decision curve analysis demonstrated favorable clinical net benefit of the XGBoost model across a wide range of threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis and feature importance consistently identified urine output, age, LDL, BMI, and D-dimer as the top contributors. Compared with conventional ICU severity scores, the XGBoost model significantly outperformed APSIII (AUC = 0.661), LODs (AUC = 0.652), and OASIS (AUC = 0.647). The logistic regression-based nomogram achieved a C-index of 0.838, providing a user-friendly bedside tool for clinicians.ConclusionThe machine learning-based XGBoost model, incorporating ten readily available clinical variables, demonstrated excellent predictive performance for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with VTE and AKI. This model offers a practical and interpretable tool for early risk stratification and may guide proactive nutritional and therapeutic interventions in this vulnerable population.

items.title: Case Report: Paralytic rabies masquerading as traumatic spinal cord injury: a diagnostic pitfall in trauma surgery
items.abstract: Rabies is a uniformly fatal zoonotic encephalitis. Its paralytic form, which accounts for approximately 20% of cases, frequently resembles acute spinal cord injury (SCI). When there is a coincident history of trauma, diagnostic anchoring may wrongly attribute neurological decline to the injury, thereby delaying the correct diagnosis. We describe the case of a 26-year-old man who developed progressive, ascending paralysis of the lower limbs 10 days after a 3-m fall. At a secondary hospital, he was clinically diagnosed with traumatic SCI without spinal MRI. On transfer, reassessment revealed a fox bite 4 months earlier and features of the hydrophobia variant (a sensation of water “entering the brain” during swallowing). Cerebrospinal fluid metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) detected Rabies lyssavirus within 48 h, showing 100% sequence identity to Chinese isolates spanning the N and L genes. This finding was subsequently confirmed by the Sichuan Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) using standard reference testing on peripheral blood. The patient subsequently died of autonomic and respiratory failure. This case highlights how recent trauma can obscure a fatal infectious cause. A clinical diagnosis of SCI made without neuroimaging should be regarded as provisional, and mNGS can provide an unbiased, rapid means of resolving diagnostically challenging neurological presentations.

items.title: Research trends and hotspots of liposomal bupivacaine: a bibliometric analysis from 2000 to 2025
items.abstract: BackgroundPostoperative pain remains a persistent challenge in perioperative care, frequently contributing to delayed patient mobilization, hindered functional recovery, and increased opioid consumption. Liposomal bupivacaine was developed to extend the release duration of local anesthetics following a single-dose administration; however, its clinical utility exhibits considerable variability across surgical procedures, block techniques, and comparator regimens. From a bibliometric perspective, this study aims to systematically investigate the overall developmental trajectory, intellectual structure, and emerging research frontiers of liposomal bupivacaine.MethodsA comprehensive literature search was performed in the Web of Science and Scopus databases for studies on liposomal bupivacaine published between 2000 and 2025. After deduplicating and merging records from both databases using a custom script, the consolidated dataset was analyzed using VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and the Bibliometrix R package.ResultsA total of 3,552 publications were included in this study. The annual publication volume increased markedly between 2020 and 2025, reaching its peak in 2025. In terms of geographical and institutional distribution, the United States dominated the field, ranking first with 2,075 publications and 63,218 total citations; China ranked second with 565 publications, though its international co-authorship rate was only 13.23%. Major contributions were made by leading institutions such as the Mayo Clinic. At the author level, De Paula demonstrated the highest publication output and network betweenness centrality, Urman recorded the highest average citations per paper, and Onel accumulated the highest total citations; collectively, these three scholars constituted the intellectual core of the field with the most prominent contributions. Regarding journal distribution, The Journal of Arthroplasty ranked first in productivity, whereas Advanced Drug Delivery Reviews garnered the highest cumulative citations, reflecting distinct emphases on clinical translation and basic pharmaceutical dissemination, respectively. Co-citation clustering identified five major thematic domains: arthroplasty, liposomal bupivacaine, fascial plane blocks, breast reconstruction, and local anesthetic delivery. “Extended-release bupivacaine” emerged as a core keyword characterized by high occurrence and high centrality. Concurrently, “erector spinae plane block” and “autologous breast reconstruction” have surged rapidly in recent years, demonstrating an ongoing thematic shift toward procedure-specific applications.ConclusionThis study represents the first quantitative bibliometric analysis of liposomal bupivacaine, revealing an evolutionary shift in research focus from early investigations centered on pharmacokinetics and formulation to diversified, procedure-specific clinical applications. Future studies should prioritize expanding international collaborative networks and further exploring emerging techniques, such as fascial plane blocks, across understudied surgical populations. This research roadmap provides directional guidance for investigators, clinicians, and funding agencies alike.

items.title: Correction: Comparative effectiveness of daytime versus nighttime paravertebral block analgesia on intraoperative hemodynamics in older lung cancer patients: a target trial emulation study
Exploratory predictive value of novel inflammatory biomarkers for microvascular obstruction after emergency revascularization in STEMI patients
items.abstract: PurposeTo assess the associations of blood cell-derived inflammatory markers with the formation of microvascular obstruction (MVO) and their exploratory predictive performance in STEMI patients after PCI.Patients and methodsA retrospective analysis was conducted based on a prospective cohort, which included the patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) who underwent emergency percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) at Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital. All patients underwent cardiac magnetic resonance imaging within 7 days post-surgery, and were classified into MVO and non-MVO groups based on the examination results. Emergency and first post-PCI routine blood test and other clinical data were collected from patients, and various cell ratios were calculated, including the monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), systemic inflammatory response index (SIRI), and aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI). The risk factors for MVO were evaluated by univariate and multivariate logistic regression analysis.ResultsA total of 311 patients with STEMI were included. Among them, 198 developed MVO and the other 113 were MVO free. After adjustment for clinical covariates, higher post-PCI WBC, NEU, SIRI and NLR and greater peri-PCI eosinophil decline were associated with MVO. In the correlation-reduced joint analysis, post-PCI SIRI retained the most robust association.ConclusionPostoperative WBC, NEU, SIRI, NLR, ΔEOS, ΔEOS% showed exploratory predictive performance for the formation of MVO after PCI in STEMI patients, and post-PCI SIRI showed the most robust association after accounting for biomarker intercorrelation.

items.title: Systemic inflammatory response index as an independent predictor of all-cause mortality in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis: a retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: PurposeChronic kidney disease (CKD) represents a major global public health burden, with affected individuals facing substantially elevated risks of morbidity, mortality, and healthcare resource utilization. In this context, the present study was undertaken to evaluate the prognostic value of the systemic inflammatory response index (SIRI) in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis.Patients and methodsA total of 534 maintenance hemodialysis patients were included in the study. The median follow-up duration was 26.0 months. The primary endpoint of this study was all-cause mortality. We compared a comprehensive panel of laboratory parameters between the survival and non-survival groups, including metabolic markers (serum triglycerides, total cholesterol, uric acid, calcium, sodium, and potassium), renal function indices (serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen), hematological parameters (hemoglobin, hematocrit, white blood cell, platelet, neutrophil, lymphocyte, and monocyte counts), and inflammatory markers (albumin and C-reactive protein). Furthermore, we derived five composite inflammatory indices from the complete blood count: NLR, PLR, MLR, SIRI, and SII.ResultsDuring a median follow-up period, 105 of 534 patients (19.7%) died. Compared with survivors, non-survivors were significantly older and exhibited higher levels of inflammatory markers, including CRP and SIRI, along with lower hemoglobin and albumin levels. In multivariate analysis, age, serum potassium, hemoglobin, and SIRI (OR: 1.072, 95% CI: 1.009–1.139, p = 0.025) emerged as independent predictors of all-cause mortality. ROC analysis demonstrated that SIRI had acceptable discriminative ability (AUC: 0.724), with an optimal cut-off value of 2.3, and patients with SIRI ≥2.3 had significantly shorter survival than those with lower values (log-rank p < 0.001).ConclusionSIRI demonstrated clinical utility as a novel, readily available biomarker for predicting all-cause mortality in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis.

items.title: Benchmarking the performance of large language models on medical genetics questions: a comparative evaluation of GPT-5.1, Gemini Pro 3, and Claude Opus 4.5
items.abstract: ObjectiveThis study benchmarks the performance of three state of the art large reasoning models comprising GPT 5.1, Gemini Pro 3, and Claude Opus 4.5 by evaluating their accuracy, response consistency, processing speed, and output length on medical genetics questions from the Turkish Medical Specialty Examination (TUS).MethodsA total of 233 medical genetics questions were selected based on predefined inclusion criteria covering molecular mechanisms, inheritance patterns, genetic disorders, and diagnostic techniques. Each question was independently submitted to GPT 5.1, Gemini Pro 3, and Claude Opus 4.5 using a standardized prompt. Model accuracy was compared using McNemar's test. Response consistency was assessed using Cohen's Kappa. Response time and word count were analyzed using the Friedman test with Dunn Bonferroni post hoc comparisons.ResultsNo statistically significant differences were observed in overall accuracy among the models (p > 0.05). GPT 5.1 achieved the highest accuracy at 97.9 percent followed by Claude Opus 4.5 at 96.6 percent and Gemini Pro 3 at 96.1 percent. Cohen's Kappa indicated moderate qualitative divergence between Gemini Pro 3 and Claude Opus 4.5 with kappa equal to 0.451. Significant differences were found in response time and output length (p < 0.001).ConclusionAlthough all models demonstrate similarly high accuracy, they differ in operational behavior, suggesting distinct internal knowledge representations and response strategies.

items.title: Neuronal FICD shapes motivated behavior through modulation of dopamine receptor dynamics
items.abstract: Motivated behaviors rely on dopaminergic signaling, which in turn depends on the correct folding and trafficking of receptors through the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). Within the ER, the AMPylase enzyme FICD acts as a molecular rheostat through its modification of the chaperone BiP, dynamically tuning the organelle's responsiveness to folding perturbations and cellular stress. While the biochemistry of FICD is well-established, its role in complex animal behavior remains poorly understood. Here, we identify FICD as a conserved contributor to the generation of motivated behavior. In Drosophila, pan-neuronal knockdown of dFic significantly reduces feeding, spontaneous locomotion, and reward-seeking behavior. These alterations occur without disrupting circadian architecture, motor capacity, or homeostatic hunger, indicating a specific loss of motivational drive. Depleting dFic within subsets of dopamine receptor-expressing (Dop1R1) neurons recapitulates these behavioral alterations. Transcriptomic profiling reveals that dFic depletion does not induce a canonical unfolded protein response, pointing to a specific post-transcriptional alteration rather than global ER stress. At the molecular level, dysregulated dFic alters the localization and abundance of Dop1R1. Finally, we demonstrate that this regulatory axis is evolutionarily conserved, as loss of FICD similarly diminishes motivated behaviors in C. elegans and mice. Together, these findings implicate FICD in the generation of motivated behavior and link dynamic control of ER proteostasis to dopamine-receptor maturation.
items.authors: Weaver, K. J.; Abdon, B.; Toth, B.; Jack, A.; Giblin, W.; Burgess, C. R.; Pletcher, S. D.; truttmann, m. c.
items.title_zh: FICD通过调节多巴胺受体动态影响动机行为
items.summary_zh: 动机行为依赖于多巴胺信号传导，而这一过程又依赖于受体在内质网中的正确折叠和运输。AMP酰化酶FICD在内质网中通过修饰伴侣蛋白BiP，动态调节细胞器对折叠扰动和细胞压力的响应。我们发现FICD是产生动机行为的重要保守因子。在果蝇中，广泛敲低dFic显著减少了进食、自发运动和寻求奖励的行为，而不影响昼夜节律、运动能力或内稳态饥饿，表明动机驱动的特异性丧失。对表达多巴胺受体(Dop1R1)神经元中dFic的耗竭重现了这些行为变化。转录组分析显示，dFic耗竭未引发经典的未折叠蛋白反应，指向特定的转录后改变而非全局内质网压力。在分子水平上，失调的dFic改变了Dop1R1的定位和丰度。最后，我们证明这一调节轴在进化上是保守的，FICD的缺失同样减少了动机行为。

items.title: Viral dispersal drives changes in population composition
items.abstract: In an acute viral infection, a small seeding population expands rapidly over several orders of magnitude, then declines. This vast population growth is accompanied by spatial expansion as infection spreads to new anatomical sites within the host. Evolutionary theory predicts that spatially expanding populations experience more extreme stochastic losses of genetic diversity than spatially unstructured populations. To test this prediction in the context of viral dynamics, we evaluated the impact of spatial expansion on viral population genetic structure and assessed how modulators of viral dispersal affected this structure. To this end, we developed a means of implementing the spatial expansion of influenza A virus in cell culture and applied it to a viral population carrying a diverse genetic barcode. Across this simplified cellular landscape, we found that spatial expansion produces a patchwork of distinct viral subpopulations. We then evaluated the consequences for population structure of two modulators of viral dispersal: extracellular viscosity and a common polymorphism in the viral attachment protein. Both physical constraint and viral phenotype altered the extent of genetic bottlenecking and spatial heterogeneity that developed during expansion, indicating that environmental features and viral traits that modulate dispersal also modulate viral population composition, diversity and evolution.
items.authors: Holmes, K. E.; Sims, A.; Ferreri, L. M.; Ortiz, L.; Elie, B.; Koelle, K.; VanInsberghe, D.; Lowen, A. C.

items.title: Reversible fixation of microbial cells for targeted genomics
items.abstract: Phylogeny- or activity-based fluorescent labelling of microorganisms coupled with fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) is a powerful approach to rapidly isolate cells of interest from complex communities for targeted genomics. However, the method has not been widely adopted because standard paraformaldehyde or ethanol fixation procedures hamper nucleic acid recovery and/or long-term sample storage. Here, we present dithiobis(succinimidyl propionate) (DSP) as a reversible fixative for microbial cells that enables fluorescence imaging and DNA extraction and amplification for sequencing. DSP fixation is compatible with widely used fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) approaches and bioorthogonal non-canonical amino acid tagging, and can be applied to diverse sample types, where it consistently performed as well as paraformaldehyde. Furthermore, high-quality genomes were obtained from individual and multiple bacterial cells selectively extracted from complex samples using FISH-FACS. Thus, DSP is a dual-use fixative for microbiome imaging and sequencing, improving targeted microbial genomics.
items.authors: Engelberts, J. P.; Wasmund, K.; Mussmann, M.; Solntseva, N.; Pereira, F. C.; Rinke, C.; Prabhu, A.; Volmer, J. G.; Hanson, B. T.; Hausmann, B.; Osvatic, J.; Tyson, G. W.; McIlroy, S. J.; Loy, A.
items.title_zh: 可逆固定微生物细胞以实现靶向基因组学
items.summary_zh: 基于系统发育或活性标记的微生物荧光标记结合荧光激活细胞分选（FACS）是一种强有力的方法，可快速从复杂群落中分离感兴趣的细胞以进行靶向基因组学。然而，传统的多聚甲醛或乙醇固定程序限制了核酸的回收和长期样本存储。本文提出了二硫代双（琥珀酰亚胺丙酸酯）（DSP）作为微生物细胞的可逆固定剂，能够进行荧光成像及DNA提取和扩增以进行测序。DSP固定与广泛使用的原位荧光杂交（FISH）方法和生物正交非典型氨基酸标记兼容，适用于多种样本类型，其性能与多聚甲醛相当。此外，通过FISH-FACS从复杂样本中选择性提取的单个和多个细菌细胞获得了高质量基因组。因此，DSP是一种双重用途的固定剂，适用于微生物组成像和测序，提升了靶向微生物基因组学的研究。

items.title: Birth synchronisation increases allonursing opportunities in free-ranging dogs
items.abstract: Over 50 years ago, the hypothesis emerged that co-resident women synchronise menstruation through pheromonal cues. This idea has persisted as a widespread narrative and has subsequently been extrapolated to other animals as well. Indeed, reproductive synchrony has many potential benefits, including creating allonursing opportunities and facilitating female mate choice. Nevertheless, little evidence exists of female vertebrates synchronising their oestrus beyond seasonal effects, through socially mediated cues. We analysed reproductive synchrony in free-ranging dogs, which combine weak, population-dependent reproductive seasonality with facultative cooperative breeding. Controlling for seasonality, we show that birth synchrony was higher among co-resident, maternally related females, suggesting synchronisation among individuals who are likely to cooperate. This was supported by our finding that birth synchrony and maternal kinship independently increased the probability and frequency of allonursing. Finally, preliminary evidence shows that oestrus synchrony decreased male monopolisation. These findings contribute to the debate on socially mediated reproductive synchronisation, suggesting that it may have mainly evolved because it facilitates cooperative breeding.
items.authors: Vanderheyden, M.; Truffaz, N.; Chaignon, B.; Car, C.; Pilot, M.; Cimarelli, G.; Marshall-Pescini, S.; Range, F.; Berghaenel, A.

items.title: Do LLM Proposers Improve Budgeted Search for Ionizable Lipids?
items.abstract: Efficient lipid design under limited experimental budgets is a central challenge in computational chemistry and drug discovery. We introduce LEAF (Lipid Evolutionary Adaptive Framework), a matched-budget protocol for testing whether language-model proposers improve combinatorial molecular search relative to classical baselines. The study uses a 30,044-candidate ionizable-lipid space, a frozen Gaussian-process oracle fitted to experimental potency labels, and a separate active-learning surrogate. Four language models evaluated over eight seeds and three splits show no significant improvement over genetic-algorithm or random-search baselines. For Llama 8B, 79.1% of acquisition-selected queries repeat previously evaluated archive members. Removing duplicates reduces the performance gap on some splits but increases proposal cost and can prevent budget exhaustion. Larger models reduce duplication without establishing superiority or equivalence. Exploratory scored prompts and stricter novelty controls yield positive median differences against the genetic algorithm, yet wide intervals and shared-seed dependence preclude stronger conclusions. A validated single-assay reanalysis preserves the chemotype-cold deficit at a smaller numerical scale, and exploratory expected hypervolume improvement does not reverse the result. Follow-up checks address whether proposers genuinely use injected evidence. These checks include a zero-shot leakage probe, rank-only and chain-of-thought-rationale prompts, a score-shuffle perturbation, an evidence-conflict probe, and a genuine reasoning-mode proposer. They show measurable engagement with supplied information without a corresponding performance gain. LEAF isolates proposal quality as the experimental variable and documents a concrete failure mode of zero-shot LLM proposers under controlled budgets.
items.authors: Singh, H.; SINGH, R. K.; Krishna, C. S.; Srivastava, S. P.; Gorantla, R.

items.title: BioMod: Biological Module Tokenization for Single-Cell Foundation Modeling
items.abstract: Single-cell foundation models typically represent cells as flat sequences of individual genes, requiring higher-order biological organization to be inferred implicitly from sparse expression profiles. Similar to the evolution from character-level to semantic tokenization in natural language processing,we hypothesize that cellular states can be more efficiently represented using biologically meaningful intermediate units. Here we present BioMod, a 50-million-parameter single-cell foundation model that introduces biological modules as representation units between genes and cells. BioMod constructs an overlapping vocabulary of 660 biological modules derived from curated pathways and data-driven gene programs, replacing thousands of gene-level inputs with compact module representations. Pretrained on approximately 73 million human cells using high-ratio module masking with an asymmetric decoder, BioMod achieves state-of-the-art performance across cell-type annotation, zero-shot batch integration, perturbation-response prediction and drug-response forecasting while maintaining a compact architecture that enables efficient inference on a single GPU. Module-level analyses further demonstrate that BioMod captures biologically meaningful cellular programs and preserves pathway-level organization.
items.authors: Meng, L.; Zhu, J.; Han, B.; Zang, Y.; Li, W.; Zong, K.; Zhong, J.; Yang, Y.; Liu, J.; Jia, J.; Sun, R.; Yu, G.; Han, J.; Chen, Y.; Zhang, L.; Xu, J.
items.title_zh: BioMod：单细胞基础建模的生物模块标记化
items.summary_zh: 单细胞基础模型通常将细胞表示为单个基因的平面序列，需要从稀疏表达谱中隐式推断更高阶的生物组织。我们假设细胞状态可以通过生物学上有意义的中间单位更有效地表示。本文提出BioMod，一个拥有5000万个参数的单细胞基础模型，引入生物模块作为基因与细胞之间的表示单位。BioMod构建了一个由660个生物模块组成的重叠词汇，这些模块源自经过整理的通路和数据驱动的基因程序，替代了数千个基因级输入。BioMod在约7300万个人体细胞上进行预训练，采用高比例模块掩蔽和非对称解码器，在细胞类型注释、零样本批次整合、干扰响应预测和药物响应预测等任务中实现了最先进的性能，同时保持紧凑的架构，支持在单个GPU上高效推理。模块级分析进一步表明，BioMod捕捉了生物学上有意义的细胞程序，并保持了通路级组织。

items.title: HERO: A hierarchy-aware analysis pipeline for reducing and refining whole-brain atlas-mapped cellular datasets
items.abstract: Advances in high-throughput mesoscale microscopy and machine learning-based image analysis pipelines have made unbiased whole-brain imaging widely accessible. However, translating the resulting atlas-mapped datasets into biologically meaningful results remains a substantial barrier owing to their sheer magnitude and complex hierarchical organization. Consequently, reporting structure and analysis methods vary widely across studies, undermining rigor and reproducibility. To address this, we developed a user-friendly data reduction workflow, HERO (Hierarchy-aware Expression Region Organization), designed to perform hierarchy-aware selection, refinement, ranking, and visualization of whole-brain cell detection datasets. The workflow is customizable to specific needs, requires minimal coding experience, and outputs transparent, curated results. HERO functions as a seamless plug-in within larger-scale whole-brain cell detection analysis pipelines, providing efficient, unbiased region selection to streamline subsequent statistical analyses and comparative evaluations. Although HERO is developed with mouse cell-detection datasets, it can be applied to any atlas-mapped dataset that contains hierarchical information. Here, we applied the HERO pipeline to example cell detection datasets containing afferent cells from the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BST) and the insular cortex (insula). HERO provided top projecting regions consistent with historical tracing studies for the BST (e.g., amygdalar and hypothalamic regions) and the insula (e.g., somatosensory, autonomic, and interoceptive regions). Furthermore, the refinement step of HERO provides additional enriched regions originally obscured in the primary ranked outputs, such as memory- and emotion-associated structures. With HEROs dynamic processing, we were able to identify top-projecting regions consistent with the literature and, additionally, find regions often obscured in these large datasets. In sum, HERO offers a standardized analysis workflow to reduce whole-brain cell-detection datasets, transforming raw regional cell counts into curated results and advancing the effectiveness, interpretability, and accessibility of whole-brain imaging in neuroscience.
items.authors: Shipman, A. L.; Centanni, S. W.
items.title_zh: HERO：一种层次感知的全脑细胞数据集分析管道
items.summary_zh: 随着高通量中尺度显微镜和基于机器学习的图像分析管道的发展，无偏见的全脑成像变得广泛可及。然而，将这些地图化的数据集转化为生物学上有意义的结果仍然面临重大障碍，主要由于数据量庞大和复杂的层次组织。因此，研究报告的结构和分析方法差异很大，影响了研究的严谨性和可重复性。为此，我们开发了用户友好的数据减少工作流程HERO（层次感知表达区域组织），旨在对全脑细胞检测数据集进行层次感知的选择、精炼、排序和可视化。该工作流程可根据特定需求定制，需最少编码经验，并输出透明、经过整理的结果。HERO作为更大规模全脑细胞检测分析管道的无缝插件，提供高效、公正的区域选择，以简化后续的统计分析和比较评估。虽然HERO是针对小鼠细胞检测数据集开发的，但也可应用于任何包含层次信息的地图化数据集。

items.title: Criticality-related dynamics accompany long-term functional decline in primary cortical MEA cultures
items.abstract: Primary cortical neuron cultures are widely used to study network development and decline, but their long-term electrophysiological trajectories are poorly characterized. We used multi-electrode arrays to longitudinally monitor Wistar rat cortical cultures for up to ~730 days in vitro (DIV), combining activity measures with survival analysis and criticality metrics. Wells shared an early developmental phase, with mean firing rate peaking at 12-14 Hz around DIV 100-150, before diverging into two phenotypes: early-death wells, showing progressive loss of burst organization, longer inter-burst intervals, shorter bursts, and steep declines in active-electrode recruitment; and long-survival wells, which sustained organized bursting and measurable activity well beyond DIV 400, in some cases past DIV 700. Cox proportional-hazards modeling with FDR correction across thirteen candidate features identified burst duration, inter-burst interval, synchrony, mean firing rate, branching ratio, and Kappa index as significant predictors of time to network failure. Criticality metrics offered the most mechanistic insight: in early-death wells, branching ratio declined toward zero and Kappa index rose toward its upper bound as networks approached silencing. Beyond their average levels, the rate of change of branching ratio and Kappa index over recordings was the strongest correlate of survival time among all criticality metrics. Neuronal avalanche size and duration exponents and their scaling relation, remained consistent with scale-free dynamics in both phenotypes while networks were active, though avalanche occurrence rate declined progressively in early-death wells without reaching significance as an independent predictor. These results show that long-term network survival is not determined by firing rate alone, but by preserved burst organization, sustained electrode recruitment and near-critical propagation dynamics. This work offers one of the longest electrophysiological characterizations of rodent cortical cultures to date and identifies criticality-based metrics as promising tools for predicting network decline and evaluating interventions to preserve long-term neuronal function.
items.authors: Escobar, A.; Gil-Bea, F. J.; Rodriguez-Gomez, L.

items.title: Deciphering auditory neuroprogenitor stemness for large-scale neuronal screening
items.abstract: Sensorineural hearing loss can arise from damage to sensory hair cells, auditory neurons or their synaptic connections, with auditory neuropathy and cochlear synaptopathy highlighting the importance of neural integrity for hearing. The mammalian cochlea has limited capacity to regenerate lost auditory neurons. Understanding the molecular programs that sustain cochlear progenitor expansion and neurogenic competence could support neuronal regeneration and provide renewable models for auditory drug discovery. We previously established that WNT activation combined with dual SMAD inhibition (CHIR-DS) supports scalable expansion and neuronal differentiation of mouse auditory neuroprogenitors (ANPGs). Here, we characterize the transcriptional, chromatin and metabolic changes associated with the induced state. RNA-seq and ATAC-seq identified reduced Id1 and Id2 expression and increased accessibility at proneural basic helix-loop-helix motifs, alongside transcriptional enrichment of translation, mTOR and glucose-metabolism programs. Compared with growth-factor controls, CHIR-DS-treated ANPGs showed slight increase in glycolysis at early passage. However, after long-term expansion, both glycolysis and mitochondrial respiration were markedly enhanced. Human fetal ANPGs also responded to CHIR-DS with increased sphere growth and retained neural differentiation capacity, providing proof of concept beyond the mouse system. Finally, neurons derived from stemness-induced ANPGs (siANs) supported a 384-well reporter assay and a 2,560-compound pilot screen that nominated candidate neurite-outgrowth enhancers. Together, these findings validate the pathway basis of ANPG stemness induction, characterize the resulting molecular and metabolic state, and demonstrate human feasibility and a neuronal screening application.
items.authors: Rousset, F.; Pepe, L.; Sarhadi, M.; Lemeille, S.; Sgroi, S.; Oberhauser, L.; Daskalou, D.; Ilmjarv, S.; Braun, S.; Senn, P.
items.title_zh: 解码听觉神经祖细胞的干性以进行大规模神经元筛选
items.summary_zh: 感音神经性听力损失可由感觉毛细胞、听觉神经元或其突触连接的损伤引起，听觉神经病和耳蜗突触病凸显了神经完整性对听力的重要性。哺乳动物耳蜗再生失去的听觉神经元的能力有限。理解维持耳蜗祖细胞扩展和神经发生能力的分子程序可能支持神经元再生，并为听觉药物发现提供可再生模型。我们之前建立了WNT激活与双SMAD抑制（CHIR-DS）结合可以支持小鼠听觉神经祖细胞（ANPGs）的可扩展性和神经分化。在此，我们表征了与诱导状态相关的转录、染色质和代谢变化。RNA-seq和ATAC-seq显示Id1和Id2表达降低，神经前体基本螺旋-环-螺旋基序的可及性增加，同时翻译、mTOR和葡萄糖代谢程序的转录富集。与生长因子对照组相比，CHIR-DS处理的ANPGs在早期传代中糖酵解略有增加，但经过长期扩展后，糖酵解和线粒体呼吸显著增强。人类胎儿ANPGs也对CHIR-DS作出反应，表现出球体生长增加和保持神经分化能力。

items.title: A foundation model for brain organoid network dynamics uncovers intrinsic computation and convergent disease phenotypes
items.abstract: Brain organoids develop self-organizing neural networks that can be used to model neurodevelopment and disease. Here we introduce PULSE, a foundation model developed using over 900 hours of high-density microelectrode array recordings of in vitro and ex vivo neural tissue. We show that this single model can address two open questions: how disease-associated variants alter network development, and how naive circuits encode information. PULSE revealed accelerated network maturation in held-out human 16p11.2-deletion organoids. It also revealed a change in network coordination shared with SHANK3 deficiency. Because organoids develop without sensory input, they let us ask how circuits encode information before any representation is learned. Closed-loop control of a virtual inverted pendulum engaged existing spontaneous activity patterns rather than creating new ones. PULSE provides a common reference frame for neural circuits across genotypes, protocols and tasks.
items.authors: Schweiger, H. E.; Robbins, A.; Hernandez, S.; Moreno-Ochando, A.; Cline, I.; Doganyigit, K.; Mouzaya, M.; Hussain, K.; Pang, Z. P.; Duan, J.; Salama, S. R.; Pollen, A. A.; Bhaduri, A.; Haussler, D.; Teodorescu, M.; Mostajo-Radji, M. A.

items.title: Reuse of learned subtask representations during human planning
items.abstract: The notion of a compositional reuse of previously learned problem solutions predicts that the human brain should reinstate such learned subtask representations during planning. Here, we test this in a value-ranking task implemented in an online and a magnetoencephalography (MEG) experiment, respectively. Participants first learned pairwise rankings and subsequently solved problems where these learned rankings could either be reused or required reordering. Behaviourally, in the online experiment, we show the availability of a reusable subtask structure improved accuracy, with computational modelling indicating a greater weighting of subtask-level value when participants could avail of this learnt structure. In MEG, during planning, we show enhanced reactivation of task-relevant subtask representations in the reusable condition, and particularly so early in the experiment. In a subsequent probe task, we show subtask-identity representations generalised to a novel context and that stimuli belonging to the same learned subtask manifest an increase in their neural similarity. Temporally delayed linear modelling (TDLM) revealed forward and backward sequential reactivation at a subtask level, alongside backward stimulus-level replay, with subtask sequenceness varying according to task context. The findings provide convergent behavioural, computational and neural evidence for reactivation and reuse of learnt relational structures for novel problem solving.
items.authors: Seak, L. C. U.; Luettgau, L.; Eckstein, M. K.; Moran, R.; Dolan, R. J.

items.title: Linking anterior cingulate sulcal variability to attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder behavior
items.abstract: Background: The anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) is consistently implicated in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). ACC variability, including its most variable structure, the paracingulate sulcus (PCGS), has been known since the late 1800s, and since then, has been linked to cognitive control, impulsivity, and psychiatric conditions comorbid with ADHD, including autism spectrum disorder and schizophrenia. Yet, the role of the PCGS in ADHD remains unexamined at the individual level. Methods: We characterized PCGS incidence, asymmetry, and morphology in 247 children and adolescents (144 ADHD: 10.9 +/- 2.73 years old, 75% male; 103 neurotypical: 12.2 +/- 3.17 years old, 50% male) from the ADHD-200 dataset. The PCGS was manually identified in FreeSurfer cortical surface reconstructions. Morphometric measures, including sulcal length, depth, and cortical thickness, were extracted and normalized to hemisphere-wide variables. Between-group analyses tested whether PCGS presence, asymmetry, and quantitative morphology differed by diagnosis, while behavioral analyses examined associations with inattention, hyperactivity-impulsivity, and cognitive measures. Age and gender were included as covariates. Results: Analyses revealed that, in both NT and ADHD individuals, there was significant leftward asymmetry in PCGS presence. Between groups, the PCGS was less likely to be present in individuals with ADHD in the left hemisphere. Leftward PCGS absence was also associated with significantly higher ADHD index and hyperactivity-impulsivity scores. Conclusions: These findings advance understanding of how early neurodevelopmental variation in cortical folding may serve as a structural intermediary between genetic liability and the behavioral expression of ADHD.
items.authors: Hadveck, R. F.; Paras, A.; Anctil, M.; Martinez, E.; Gallardo, C. M.; Maboudian, S. A.; Willbrand, E. H.; Weiner, K. S.

items.title: Lysosomal Glycosaminoglycan Catabolism Regulates Microglial Cell State in the Developing CNS
items.abstract: Remodeling of the extracellular matrix (ECM), a complex structural and signaling network of the nervous system, is essential for CNS development, plasticity, and injury responses, yet how individual neural cell types contribute to this process remains poorly understood. Here, we show that phagocytic clearance of glycosaminoglycans (GAGs), major components of the ECM, is an intrinsic function of microglia in the developing CNS. Our studies reveal an unexpected finding that impaired GAG clearance shifts microglia toward a non-homeostatic cell state seen in immature and disease-associated microglia (DAM), supporting a reciprocal relationship between the ECM and microglia. Using mouse models of Mucopolysaccharidosis VII, we examined the consequences of deleting {beta}-glucuronidase (GUSB), a lysosomal enzyme required for GAG degradation. Loss of GUSB causes early accumulation of undegraded chondroitin sulfate within microglial lysosomes, as confirmed by LC-MS analysis of intracellular GAGs isolated from cortical microglia. Single-cell RNA sequencing identified Gusb-null microglia as a distinct transcriptional population enriched for a core transcriptome shared by immature and disease-associated microglia. Together, these findings establish lysosomal GAG catabolism as a pathway that links ECM remodeling to the acquisition of adult homeostatic microglial identity during CNS development.
items.authors: Hope, K. T.; Zhang, Y.; Basu, A.; Luo, B.; Chassie, K.; Weiss, R. J.; Yellajoshyula, D.
items.title_zh: 溶酶体糖胺聚糖降解调控发育中CNS小胶质细胞状态
items.summary_zh: 本研究探讨了糖胺聚糖（GAGs）在发育中中枢神经系统（CNS）中的清除作用，发现其为小胶质细胞的内在功能。研究表明，GAG清除受损会使小胶质细胞转变为非稳态状态，与未成熟和疾病相关小胶质细胞（DAM）相似，支持了细胞外基质（ECM）与小胶质细胞之间的相互关系。通过小鼠粘多糖贮积症VII模型，研究了缺失β-葡萄糖醛酸酶（GUSB）的后果，发现GUSB缺失导致小胶质细胞内未降解的硫酸软骨素早期积累。单细胞RNA测序显示，Gusb-null小胶质细胞为一种独特的转录群体，富含未成熟和疾病相关小胶质细胞共享的核心转录组。这些发现确立了溶酶体GAG降解作为连接ECM重塑与获得成年稳态小胶质细胞身份的途径。

items.title: Oligodendrocyte stress response as a driver of vascular dementia
items.abstract: Vascular dementia (VaD) is a prevalent and devastating neurocognitive disorder characterized by profound white matter damage, yet the precise cellular mechanisms linking cerebrovascular stress to demyelination remain poorly understood. Here, we characterize the impact of a chronic cardiometabolic stress regimen combining a high-fat diet and hypertension (HF/HBP) on central nervous system structure and function. Adult HF/HBP mice exhibit progressive oligodendroglial cell loss and myelin thinning, followed by cognitive impairments, anxiety-like behavior, and memory deficits that recapitulate clinical features of VaD. Mechanistically, we identify the integrated stress response (ISR) as a central driver of this pathology; pharmacological inhibition of the ISR restores myelination, while cell-specific genetic deletion of the ISR-activating kinase PERK from oligodendrocytes fully protects mice from HF/HBP-induced pathological and behavioral defects. Furthermore, we provide translational evidence that the ISR is activated in oligodendrocytes in human cases of cerebrovascular disease. Together, these findings reveal a critical, cell-autonomous role for oligodendroglial ISR activation during cerebrovascular stress and position this pathway as a viable therapeutic target to mitigate VaD pathogenesis.
items.authors: Merour, E.; Ghatage, T.; Corbett, C.; DeBerge, M.; Kunjamma, R.; Ian Steckler, I. S.; Heidari, M.; Sorond, F. A.; Flanagan, M. E.; Thorp, E. B.; Popko, B.

items.title: High-throughput light-sheet 3D microscopy of whole rodent brain microstructure for integration with MRI
items.abstract: Whole-brain cellular mapping is essential for understanding how differences in cellular architecture shape brain organisation and function. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) provides whole-brain coverage in humans and animal models but is only indirectly sensitive to cellular features. Integrating MRI with whole-brain microscopy is therefore critical for interpreting existing microstructural MRI metrics and developing new, more specific ones. Here, we present a scalable cross-resolution framework that integrates 3D light-sheet microscopy (LSM) of intact rodent brains with diffusion MRI (dMRI) to bridge cellular and macroscopic brain imaging. By combining active electrotransport-based tissue clearing and immunolabelling with accelerated LSM acquisitions, we achieve whole-brain multiplexed mapping of neuronal and glial populations in intact rodent brains on timescales comparable to conventional histology and 2D microscopy. This throughput enables LSM and MRI integration at scale, linking macroscopic MRI contrasts to microscopic cellular features within the same tissue. We apply this framework across eight genetically diverse mouse strains to develop predictive models of 3D microscopy-derived cellular features from multi-shell dMRI-derived contrasts. We demonstrate that data-driven combinations of state-of-the-art dMRI contrasts predict neuronal and astrocytic features better than individual contrasts, across all animals. Our novel approach enables 3D microscopy to guide the development and interpretation of microstructural MRI measures that are ultimately translatable to the living human brain.
items.authors: Hanmer, J. M.; D'Antonio, F.; Manzano-Patron, J.-P.; Assimopoulos, S.; Wood, S. C.; Tachrount, M.; Shen, Q.; Craig, M.; Lai, C.; Hickman, G. J.; Radfar, E.; Chisholm, K. I.; Farr, T. D.; Jasanoff, A.; Hoerder-Suabedissen, A.; Molnar, Z.; Ligneul, C.; Tisca, C.; Jbabdi, S.; Howard, A. F. D.; Miller, K. L.; de Guzman, E.; Lerch, J. P.; Sotiropoulos, S. N.

items.title: Apoptotic Cells Promote Tim4+ Macrophage Differentiation Through Direct and Indirect Signaling Pathways
items.abstract: Tissue macrophages are the primary cells responsible for efficiently clearing apoptotic cells, yet how professional efferocyte populations are established remains unclear. Tim4 marks a subset of macrophages across multiple tissues that are highly efferocytic, but the mechanisms governing Tim4 acquisition are poorly understood. Here, we show that monocyte-derived macrophages progressively differentiate into Tim4 macrophages in homeostatic and pathological settings. We identify a cell-autonomous pathway in which efficient apoptotic cell clearance promotes Tim4 acquisition in macrophages, as combined deficiency of CD11b and MerTK impairs both efferocytosis and Tim4 acquisition. Surprisingly, excessive apoptotic cell burden enhanced Tim4 acquisition independently of these receptors. We demonstrate that serial exposure to apoptotic cells induces a type 2 immune response characterized by expansion of IL-4-producing populations and that IL-4R-STAT6 signaling is sufficient and required to drive Tim4 acquisition. These findings support a model in which Tim4 acquisition in macrophages integrates direct signals associated with apoptotic cell clearance and indirect signals generated by apoptotic cell burden. We propose that these complementary mechanisms enable tissues to dynamically adjust the size and function of the professional efferocyte compartment to meet changing demands for apoptotic cell clearance.
items.authors: Manning, B. S.; Zhu, L.; Murphy, B.; Soliman, M. M.; Shao, C.; Param, N.; Miyamoto, T.; Shinde, R.; Carroll, M.; Zhang, N.

items.title: Anti-inflammatory macrophages limit endothelial inflammation and restrict neutrophil recruitment through Gas6/AXL signaling
items.abstract: Neutrophil extravasation requires coordinated interactions between the endothelium and surrounding cells, including tissue resident macrophages. Macrophages adopt distinct polarization states in the tissue environment, positioning them as regulators of vascular inflammation. However, how these states influence barrier function and neutrophil extravasation remains unclear. Here, we polarized macrophages in the matrix surrounding an endothelial vessel, in a three-dimensional inflammation-on-a-chip model developed only from primary human cells. We found anti-inflammatory macrophages limited endothelial inflammation, reducing ICAM-1 upregulation, maintaining VE-Cadherin expression, halving permeability relative to pro-inflammatory devices, and reducing neutrophil extravasation and migration relative to macrophage-free devices. Secretome profiling identified Gas6, an AXL ligand, as a potential regulator of these effects. Inhibiting AXL increased extravasation in devices with anti-inflammatory macrophages, and soluble Gas6 reduced extravasation in macrophage-free devices, implicating Gas6 as a mediator of this regulation. This indicates macrophages regulate endothelial inflammation and the neutrophil response via Gas6 signaling.
items.authors: Ignes-Romeu, A.; Sood, R.; Hind, L. E.

items.title: BCR repertoire analysis and cloning of antibody candidates targeting native and Asp7-isomerized β-amyloid
items.abstract: Computational approaches are increasingly used to prioritize monoclonal antibody (mAB) candidates from BCR-seq datasets. However, the reliable identification of B cells encoding antibodies against rare antigenic epitopes remains challenging. We employed a repertoire-guided workflow combining antigen-tetramer sorting of B cells from immunized mice, followed by low-input bulk BCR-seq, which yielded informative clonal repertoires. Clustering analysis allowed us to prioritize IGH and IGK clonotypes potentially targeting {beta}-amyloid and the isoAsp7 proteoform (isoD7-A{beta}1-16), implicated in Alzheimer's disease. We observed recurrent IGHV8-12 and IGKV1-117 usage, consistent with canonical mouse anti-A{beta} responses. Focusing on isoD7-A{beta} -associated candidates, we selected fourteen candidate IGH--IGK combinations for recombinant expression including variants containing IGKV8-21, IGKV8-19, IGKV2-112 together with IGHV1-75, IGHV10-1 or IGHV8-12. Several recombinant mABs showed detectable binding activity to isoD7-A{beta}, including a candidate with preferential recognition of isoD7-A{beta}, supporting the feasibility of the approach but underscoring the challenge of accurate chain pairing. These results provide proof of principle that repertoire-guided analysis can prioritize candidate IGH and IGK chains and propose possible heavy-light chain combinations based on their co-representation across samples while experimental testing remains necessary to identify antibodies with preferential recognition of isoD7-A{beta}.
items.authors: Nikolaev, N. A.; Kolobova, E. A.; Myshkin, M. Y.; Shagina, I. A.; Barsova, E. V.; Kechko, O. I.; Grogoreva, T. V.; Mitkevich, V. A.; Merzlyak, E. M.; Kozin, S.; Makarov, A. A.; Chudakov, D. M.; Lukyanov, S. A.; Grigorova, I. L.; Britanova, O. V.

items.title: Fever-range temperature enhances B cells in vitro but is dispensable for the germinal center in vivo
items.abstract: Fever is a conserved physiological response to immune activation characterized by elevated body temperature. While hyperthermia enhances innate and T cell immunity, its role in shaping the B cell compartment remains poorly defined, despite B cells' role in long-term protection. Understanding how temperature modulates B cell physiology is relevant to vaccine strategies, particularly fever management around immunization. Therefore, we investigated the influence of fever-range thermal changes on humoral immunity. To decipher the direct effects, primary B cells from C57BL/6 mice were stimulated in vitro under mild hyperthermic conditions (~1.5{degrees}C increase). Fever-range temperature enhanced B cell activation, facilitated entry into cell division, and increased antigen presentation to CD4+ T cells, while transcriptomic analysis revealed enrichment of pathways involved in protein synthesis and mitochondrial respiration. To determine whether these intrinsic effects translated into altered humoral immunity in vivo, we developed a novel tunable implant-based system to induce localized, 48-hour hyperthermia around a draining lymph node in awake mice without altering core body temperature. Following subcutaneous NP-OVA/alum immunization, localized hyperthermia localized hyperthermia did not enhance antigen-specific germinal center B cell expansion, antibody titers or IgG affinity on day 9. Moreover, heating during priming did not affect the recall humoral response after a booster on day 21. Thus, fever-range temperature directly modulates murine B cell function in vitro but does not enhance humoral immunity in vivo, indicating that the biological consequences of intrinsic B cell thermosensitivity depend on its integration within the multicellular and inflammatory signals shaping germinal center responses.
items.authors: Mohammed, S.; Sbihi, Z.; Laignel, P.; Houtia, I.; Haddou, S.; Procopio, E.; Morales, O.; Franck, G.; Caligiuri, G.; Nicoletti, A.; Le Borgne, M.
items.title_zh: 发热温度增强体外B细胞活性但对体内生发中心无影响
items.summary_zh: 发热是免疫激活的生理反应，表现为体温升高。尽管高温可增强先天免疫和T细胞免疫，但其对B细胞的影响尚不明确。我们研究了发热范围内的温度变化对体液免疫的影响。通过在轻度高温条件下（约升高1.5°C）刺激C57BL/6小鼠的初级B细胞，发现发热温度增强了B细胞活化、促进细胞分裂并增加了对CD4+ T细胞的抗原呈递，同时转录组分析显示与蛋白质合成和线粒体呼吸相关的通路富集。为了验证这些内在效应是否影响体内的体液免疫，我们开发了一种新型可调植入系统，在不改变核心体温的情况下，在清醒小鼠的引流淋巴结周围诱导局部48小时高温。结果显示，局部高温并未增强抗原特异性生发中心B细胞扩增、抗体滴度或IgG亲和力。

items.title: Spatiotemporal analysis of sporozoite maturation and infectivity
items.abstract: Plasmodium sporozoites must undergo tightly regulated developmental transitions to become infectious and be successfully transmitted from the mosquito vector to a mammalian host. While transcriptomic studies have revealed stage-specific changes across sporozoite populations, the functional consequences of these transitions remain unclear. Here, using P. berghei, we characterised over time the infectivity of sporozoite forms collected from the midgut, haemolymph, salivary glands and saliva. We show that salivary gland invasion is required but not sufficient for sporozoite optimal infectivity, with the acquisition of hepatocyte cell traversal and invasion progressively increasing until a plateau from 18 days post-infection onwards. Using a stage-specific fluorescent reporter to track maturation, we found that fluorescence increased over time and correlated with infectivity within each compartment, yet maximal infectivity was reached only in salivary gland sporozoites. Notably, our data suggest that salivated sporozoites, the natural transmission form, exhibit enhanced infectivity relative to gland-resident forms both in vitro and in vivo early after salivary gland invasion. This difference decreases following optimal maturation inside the glands over time. These observations show a crescent gradient of sporozoite maturation and infectiveness from the midgut to the saliva, in which pre-salivary gland forms retain limited infectivity but do not reach the competence of mature salivary gland-associated parasites.
items.authors: Verzier, L. H. H.; Thiberge, J.-M.; Aliprandini, E.; Lagal, V.; Formaglio, P.; Silvie, O.; Amino, R.

items.title: Supplementation with a Limosilactobacillus fermentum K73 synbiotic modulates gut microbiota function and behavior in gnotobiotic mice transplanted with microbiota from children diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder
items.abstract: Gut dysbiosis has been implicated in numerous pathological conditions, including neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorders. Recently, dietary interventions targeted at restoring microbial balance have therefore gained attention as potential therapeutic strategies. We recently demonstrated that an encapsulated synbiotic containing high-oleic palm oil and Limosilactobacillus fermentum K73 can modulate the metabolic activity and composition of human-derived gut microbiota in an in vitro batch bioreactor. Here, we extended this work through an in vivo supplementation pilot study using gnotobiotic mice colonized with gut microbiota from Colombian pediatric patients diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or age-matched neurotypical (NT) donors. Behavioral assessments and analyses of gut microbiota composition and function were performed before and after synbiotic supplementation. First, we found that the gut microbiota from Colombian ASD patients exhibited significantly reduced richness relative to NT donors, consistent with reports from other geographical regions, and displayed distinct compositional features unique to this population. Humanization of the gnotobiotic mice with this donor microbiota was successful, with murine gut communities reflecting features of their corresponding donor microbiota. Notably, synbiotic supplementation induced significant increases in the abundance of beneficial taxa and the production of short chain fatty acids that were more pronounced in mice colonized with ASD-derived microbiota, with concurrent behavioral changes associated with beneficial modulation of gut microbiota. Overall, we provide evidence that supports synbiotic supplementation as a viable strategy to positively modulate gut microbiome in conditions of dysbiosis. Our study also expands the body of knowledge of gut microbiome to understudied populations such as Latin America.
items.authors: Bauer-Estrada, K.; Azamar, K. M. M.; Wang, C.; Sudi, S.; Friday-Saunders, K.; Marquez, V.; Quintanilla-Carvajal, M. X.; Acosta-Gonzalez, A.; Conde-Martinez, N.; Porras, A. M.; Alvina, K.
items.title_zh: Limosilactobacillus fermentum K73益生元调节自闭症小鼠肠道微生物功能
items.summary_zh: 肠道微生物失调与多种病理状况相关，包括神经发育和神经退行性疾病。本文通过在体内补充Limosilactobacillus fermentum K73益生元，研究了来自哥伦比亚自闭症谱系障碍（ASD）儿童的微生物群对无菌小鼠的影响。研究发现，ASD患者的肠道微生物群相较于年龄匹配的神经典型（NT）供体，丰富度显著降低，并展现出该人群特有的组成特征。通过供体微生物群成功人源化无菌小鼠，结果显示小鼠肠道微生物群反映了供体的特征。补充益生元后，观察到肠道微生物功能和行为的显著变化。

items.title: VPS34 regulation in pulmonary arterial vascular smooth muscle cells in pulmonary hypertension
items.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is characterized by the hyperproliferative phenotype of pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PAVSMCs) and extensive extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. Vacuolar protein sorting 34 (VPS34), a Class III Phosphatidylinositol-3 Kinase (PI3K), regulates cell proliferation, but its specific function in pulmonary vascular remodeling remains poorly understood. We aim to determine the role of VPS34 activation and regulation in PAVSMC proliferation, matrix deposition, and the progression of PAH. First, we found a marked decrease in the inhibitory phosphorylation of VPS34 at Ser164 (P-S164-VPS34), indicative of constitutive VPS34 activation, in remodeled pulmonary arteries (PAs) from human PAH patients and male mice exposed to Sugen/Hypoxia (SuHx). In human PAH PAVSMCs, siRNA-mediated knockdown of VPS34 or pharmacological inhibition via the selective inhibitor SAR405 significantly blunted cell proliferation and reduced the production of fibronectin, a major component of the remodeled ECM. Mechanistically, we found that Akt activation in PAH PAVSMCs promotes VPS34 activation; Protein Phosphatase 1 Catalytic Subunit Alpha is a potential effector in VPS34 activation; and active VPS34 led to the activation of the mTOR/S6 signaling pathway with tuberous sclerosis complex 2 downregulation. Finally, in vivo treatment with SAR405 attenuated right ventricular systolic pressure, right ventricular hypertrophy, and pulmonary vascular remodeling in SuHx mice, while concurrently decreasing vascular fibronectin deposition. Our study demonstrates that VPS34 activation, driven by an Akt-mediated loss of the inhibitory P-S164, is crucial in PAVSMC proliferation and fibrotic vascular remodeling in PAH. Targeting the VPS34 axis represents a promising anti-remodeling therapeutic strategy for the treatment of PAH. Keywords: Pulmonary arterial hypertension, vacuolar protein sorting 34, pulmonary vascular remodeling, pulmonary arterial vascular smooth muscle
items.authors: Natoli, A.; Reinhard, B.; Hallee, L.; Zhang, H.; Piza-Taylor, K.; Aung, F.; Poznahovska, A.; Gleghorn, J. P.; Lucas, R.; DiVita, M.; Shen, Y.

items.title: A single epigenetic repressor controls opposing developmental tempos in human neural and cranial neural crest lineages
items.abstract: The precise timing of lineage specification is essential for embryonic development, yet the epigenetic mechanisms enforcing human developmental tempo remain poorly understood. Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in ZNF462 cause Weiss-Kruszka syndrome (WKS), a pleiotropic disorder characterized by neurodevelopmental delays and craniofacial dysmorphisms. Here, we show that ZNF462 acts as an epigenetic gatekeeper that coordinates human developmental tempo across divergent lineages by repressing cell lineage-specific gene enhancers. In human embryonic stem cells (hESCs), ZNF462 maintains self-renewal by recruiting the G9A/GLP histone methyltransferase complex to silence primate-specific retrotransposon-derived enhancers. Upon neural lineage commitment, ZNF462 redirects to hominoid-specific LTR5_Hs elements and divergent lineage-specific enhancer programs, where its loss produces opposing kinetics. In neural progenitor cells (NPCs), ZNF462 enforces G9A/GLP-dependent repression of ZIC-driven neural enhancers, and loss of this repression traps NPCs in a progenitor state, slowing cortical neurogenesis without impairing terminal neurogenic capacity. In neural crest cells (NCCs), ZNF462 targets repressive chromatin to silence SOX9 family-driven enhancers. Here, ZNF462 haploinsufficiency triggers premature activation of definitive NCC specifiers, accelerating differentiation. These findings establish that a single repressor can simultaneously decelerate and accelerate developmental tempo by gating lineage-specific enhancers, placing Weiss-Kruszka syndrome into the emerging class of human developmental timing disorders.
items.authors: Bell, O.; Atmaca Duran, Z. E.; Birtele, M.; Quadrato, G.; Mendiratta, S.; Yelagandula, R.; Stevens, C.; Rhie, S.

items.title: Single-cell variant landscape of the human mitochondrial genome reveals cell type-specific functions and disease mechanisms
items.abstract: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) heteroplasmy is a significant source of cellular genetic diversity and can cause disease yet its distribution and functional importance across different human cell types are poorly understood. Here we present scMOCHA (Single-Cell Mitochondrial Omics for Cellular Heteroplasmy Analysis), a scalable computational framework that resolves highconfidence, single-cell resolution mtDNA heteroplasmy directly from standard single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. Using this tool to interrogate publicly available scRNA-seq datasets from human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) and bone marrow (BM) uncovered the single-cell landscape of mtDNA single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) and heteroplasmy across ages in human hematopoietic cell types. PBMCs and BM share many inherited homoplasmic and highly heteroplasmic SNVs, whereas somatic SNVs are tissue- and cell type-specific and distributed across the mtDNA genome, suggesting that they arise largely stochastically. mtDNA replication error is a dominant force shaping homoplasmic variants, while oxidative stress potentially drives a significant portion of heteroplasmic and somatic mutations. Importantly, we discover previously unknown cell type-specific and human disease-associated mtDNA SNVs. By coupling mtDNA genotypes with matched single-cell nuclear transcriptomes and structural modeling, we uncover potential molecular mechanisms by which disease-associated mtDNA SNVs impact cellular processes such as inflammation and contribute to disease. Together, these findings define the single-cell variant landscape of the human mitochondrial genome and reveal previously unrecognized lineage- and disease-associated patterns of mtDNA variation in the human hematopoietic system.
items.authors: Liu, C.; Peng, T.; Cen, Z.; Lu, P.; Potluri, P.; Hu, P.; Zhang, S.; Lott, M. T.; Widjaja, G.; Wallace, D. C.; Xing, Y.; Pei, L.
items.title_zh: 人类线粒体基因组单细胞变异图谱揭示细胞类型特异功能与疾病机制
items.summary_zh: 线粒体DNA（mtDNA）异质性是细胞遗传多样性的一个重要来源，并可能导致疾病，但其在不同人类细胞类型中的分布和功能重要性尚不清楚。本文提出了scMOCHA（单细胞线粒体组学用于细胞异质性分析），这是一个可扩展的计算框架，能够直接从标准单细胞RNA测序（scRNA-seq）数据中解析高置信度的单细胞mtDNA异质性。利用该工具分析人类外周血单核细胞（PBMC）和骨髓（BM）的公开scRNA-seq数据集，揭示了人类造血细胞类型中mtDNA单核苷酸变异（SNVs）和异质性的单细胞图谱。PBMC和BM共享许多遗传的均质性和高度异质性的SNVs，而体细胞SNVs则是组织和细胞类型特异的，且在mtDNA基因组中分布，表明它们主要是随机产生的。mtDNA复制错误是塑造均质性变异的主导力量，而氧化应激可能驱动相当一部分异质性和体细胞突变。重要的是，我们发现了之前未知的细胞类型特异性和与人类疾病相关的mtDNA SNVs。通过将mtDNA基因型与匹配的单细胞核转录组和结构建模结合，我们揭示了潜在的功能。

items.title: Convergent genome evolution reveals shared routes to salt tolerance in flowering plants
items.abstract: Transitions to saline environments pose formidable challenges to plants, yet halophytism has evolved independently across many flowering plant lineages. We assembled a comparative angiosperm gene catalog of ~10 million protein-coding genes from 232 genomes spanning 55 families, with similar representation of halophytes and salt-sensitive relatives, to identify convergent genomic signatures of halophytism. Halophytes show remarkable convergence with recurrent genomic trends in salt-response genes, including lower copy numbers, higher basal expression, more constrained expression variation, distinct evolutionary rates, and independent positive selection on select genes at the same amino acid sites across multiple halophyte lineages. Crops and their wild halophytic relatives differ in gene family evolution, particularly in stress-response pathways. These findings reveal repeatedly tested evolutionary routes to halophytism and establish a genomic foundation for translating convergent adaptations into salt-tolerant crops.
items.authors: Wimalagunasekara, S.; Dassanayake, M.
items.title_zh: 趋同基因组进化揭示开花植物盐耐受性的共同途径
items.summary_zh: 植物向盐碱环境的转变面临巨大挑战，但盐生植物在多个开花植物谱系中独立进化。我们组建了一个比较的被子植物基因目录，涵盖232个基因组，约1000万个编码蛋白质的基因，涵盖55个科，盐生植物与盐敏感亲缘种的代表性相似，以识别盐生植物的趋同基因组特征。盐生植物在盐响应基因上表现出显著的趋同，包括较低的拷贝数、更高的基础表达、更受限的表达变异、不同的进化速率，以及在多个盐生植物谱系中对特定基因的独立正选择。这些发现揭示了反复验证的盐生植物进化途径，并为将趋同适应转化为耐盐作物奠定了基因组基础。

items.title: Mid-Infrared Photothermal Imaging Unveils Altered Stearoyl-CoA desaturase (SCD) Activity in Ovarian Cancer Cells
items.abstract: Stearoyl-CoA desaturase (SCD)-catalyzed fatty acid desaturation plays a key role in cancer metabolism reprogramming. While existing approaches enable quantification of SCD expression, directly monitoring in situ SCD enzymatic activity alterations remains challenging. Here, we report a strategy to measure intracellular SCD activity alterations and SCD product distributions by mid-infrared photothermal (MIP) imaging. Fully deuterated palmitic acid (PA-d31) is repurposed here as a chemical probe to report the SCD activity via a new peak at 2246 cm-1, corresponding to the stretching of D-C=C-D bonds in the SCD product. The MIP intensity ratio between the product-associated signal and the total C-D signal defines the apparent SCD activity index. By visualization of SCD-catalyzed metabolic conversion, our approach reveals altered SCD activity in cisplatin-treated ovarian cancer cells, ovarian cancer stem cells and cells fed with oleic acid. Non-uniform distributions of the SCD product are also observed. These results establish bio-orthogonal MIP microscopy as a platform for studying intracellular enzymatic reactions in living systems.
items.authors: Teng, X.; Xia, T.; Yin, J.; Li, M.; Ao, J.; Ding, G.; Prabhu Dessai, C. V.; Isac, A. M.; Matei, D.; He, H.; Cheng, J.-X.

items.title: LOCALE: Local-Alignment Embeddings for Noise-Robust DNA Search at Scale
items.abstract: Searching petabase-scale repositories of raw sequencing data such as the NIH Sequence Read Archive (SRA) could unlock biological insights that remain inaccessible. Existing sequence-search methods either do not scale well or rely on exact $k$-mer matching that is brittle to genomic variation, which is high both within and across species and is further compounded by sequencing error. We recast sequence search as dense retrieval: we learn sequence embeddings whose inner-product similarity ranks locally aligned sequences above unaligned ones. We introduce LOCALE, an encoder trained with an InfoNCE objective on biologically informed augmentations: overlapping crops of parent sequences corrupted with substitutions, insertions, and deletions. This training recipe, rather than a specialized architecture, consistently induces variation-robust representations across four encoders spanning three tokenization schemes, improving Recall@$R_q$ by 7--39 points at 10% genomic variation. On a 50-accession SRA benchmark LOCALE retains 63.2% Recall@$R_q$ at 10% variation while existing k-mer indexes and DNA embedding methods fall below 35%, and on the full 4,571-accession MetaGraph benchmark (296 Gbp, 2.06 billion vectors) it achieves 4.5x the AUPRC of MetaGraph, the state-of-the-art k-mer index, with a single-node GPU IVF-PQ index retaining a 3.6x advantage at MetaGraph's query latency. Our encoder and training strategy generalize to real biological variance: on a cross-genotype Hepatitis B task, querying reads from one genotype against accessions of another with >8% natural divergence, LOCALE reaches 0.813 Recall@R_q versus 0.518 for MetaGraph.
items.authors: Synk, R.; Pandey, P.; Sahinalp, C.; Duraiswami, R.

items.title: AlphaFold3 and Intrinsically Disordered Proteins: Reliable Monomer Prediction, Unpredictable Multimer Performance
items.abstract: AlphaFold3 represents a major advance in protein structure prediction, yet its performance on intrinsically disordered proteins remains uncharacterized.
