This work presents a systematic overview of the evolution of global CAA guidelines and provides an in-depth analysis of recent research advances in assessment methodologies across three core domains, including hazard characterization, exposure assessment, and life cycle assessment (LCA). We highlight that modern CAA is undergoing a profound paradigm shift. Hazard characterization is transitioning from traditional in vivo experiments to predictive toxicology, anchored in new approach methodologies; exposure assessment is evolving from static, conservative assumptions to refined, dynamic coupled multi-media models; and LCA is expanding from end-of-pipe environmental impact auditing to source-level interventions that integrate prospective prediction and green design. By connecting insights across scales, from microscopic molecular mechanisms to macroscopic ecosystem-level outcomes, this study aims to provide relatively comprehensive methodological guidance for chemical alternative assessments. In turn, this work provides both the theoretical foundation for “Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD)” chemical development and the practical reference for establishing robust scientific toolkits for prospective chemical classification and regulatory decision-making.
items.authors: Yipeng Lu, Xiaoqian Chen, Pin Gao

items.title: Early Diagnostic Classification of Alzheimer’s Disease Using Structural and Resting-State Functional MRI
items.abstract: Background: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is an irreversible neurodegenerative disorder where early diagnosis at the mild cognitive impairment (MCI) stage is critical for timely intervention. While structural MRI (sMRI) and resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) provide complementary pathological information, clinical translation is limited by high feature heterogeneity and the heavy computational burden of 3D deep learning networks. This study aims to propose a lightweight, hybrid multimodal fusion model to overcome these limitations and improve diagnostic efficiency. Methods: A lightweight MobileViT-XS network was utilized to extract global and local pathological features from gray-matter sMRI images to reduce computational costs. Concurrently, graph theory was applied to rs-fMRI data to construct brain functional networks and calculate global topological properties. Following pretraining, feature-level fusion was performed to integrate sMRI features, rs-fMRI properties, demographic information, and two clinical neuropsychological examinations. Results: The validation results show that the proposed hybrid model achieved high diagnostic performance in the three-class classification task, yielding an accuracy of 0.928 ± 0.010, sensitivity of 0.901 ± 0.014, precision of 0.933 ± 0.014, and an F1 score of 0.911 ± 0.012. On the held-out testing subset of the independently collected dataset after dataset-specific fine-tuning, the proposed model achieved an accuracy of 0.857, with a sensitivity of 0.867, a precision of 0.867, and an F1 score of 0.859. Conclusions: The proposed framework successfully minimizes computational overhead while maintaining high classification accuracy. These findings suggest that the hybrid multimodal fusion model provides a promising computer-aided approach for three-class classification of AD, MCI, and NC.
items.authors: Junhu Liu, Bing Zhu, Miao Yu, Shichao Du
items.title_zh: 利用结构和静息态功能MRI早期诊断阿尔茨海默病
items.summary_zh: 背景：阿尔茨海默病（AD）是一种不可逆的神经退行性疾病，早期在轻度认知障碍（MCI）阶段的诊断对及时干预至关重要。结构MRI（sMRI）和静息态功能MRI（rs-fMRI）提供互补的病理信息，但由于特征异质性高和3D深度学习网络的计算负担重，临床转化受到限制。本研究旨在提出一种轻量级的混合多模态融合模型，以克服这些限制并提高诊断效率。方法：采用轻量级MobileViT-XS网络从灰质sMRI图像中提取全局和局部病理特征，以降低计算成本。同时，应用图论对rs-fMRI数据构建脑功能网络并计算全局拓扑特性。在预训练后，进行特征级融合，整合sMRI特征、rs-fMRI属性、人口统计信息和两项临床神经心理检查。结果：验证结果表明，所提混合模型在三类分类任务中实现了高诊断性能，准确率为0.928 ± 0.010，灵敏度为0.901 ± 0.014，精确度为0.933 ± 0.014，F1分数为0.911 ± 0.012。

items.title: Actions of Pharmaceutical Lactones and Lactams on the Enzymes with Lactonase Activity: In Silico Prediction and In Vitro Study
items.abstract: Pharmaceutical pollutants that contain lactone or lactam rings in their structure are frequently detected in wastewater. Enzymes with lactonase activity, synthesized by the microorganisms in aerobic activated sludge, are expected to be able to participate in the hydrolysis of these pharmaceutical pollutants, but the actual activity of many lactonases towards such compounds remains poorly characterized. In this work, a systematic molecular docking study of 12 enzymes and 39 pharmaceutical pollutants (β-lactam antibiotics, macrolides, coumarins, statins) was undertaken. The binding affinity, active-site occupancy, total enzyme surface occupancy and geometric characteristics of the molecules (the distance from the catalytic nucleophile to the carbonyl carbon of the lactone ring, and the attack angle formed between the nucleophilic atom of the enzyme and the C–N/C–O bond of the substrate) were evaluated in silico for a set of hydrolases displaying lactonase activity (AidC, AaL, hexahistidine-tagged organophosphate hydrolase (His6-OPH), etc.) and metallo-β-lactamases (MβLs) (NDM-1, MIM-1, SAM-1). Lactamases exhibited favorable intermolecular interaction geometry for the majority of β-lactams. No enzyme was found that satisfied the geometric criteria corresponding to the biodegradation of macrolides. With coumarins, only Paraoxonase PON2 provided an optimal geometry of biocatalysis; however, this enzyme is absent from activated sludge but may be of interest for in vivo applications. For several statins widely used in practice, combinations with enzymes having virtually ideal geometry for biocatalysis were identified: AidC/rosuvastatin lactone, AaL/lovastatin, His6-OPH/mevastatin, and PON2/simvastatin. For the first time, several pharmaceutical lactones were identified in silico and confirmed in vitro as inhibitors of MβL and His6-OPH. Competitive inhibition of NDM-1 by lactone-containing signaling molecules of Gram-negative bacteria present in activated sludge was revealed for the first time both in silico and in vitro. The obtained results‘ may be taken into account when implementing monitoring of biological stages at water treatment stations and improve the efficiency of water purification. The revealed characteristics of MβL inhibition by macrolides may be taken into account as one of possible explanations for the effective application of β-lactams in combinations with macrolides known from multiple paratactical investigations.
items.authors: Elena Efremenko, Maksim Domnin, Anastasia Sarapina, Aigul Zagidulina

items.title: CrossCheck: Evidence-Based Compliance Verification for OT Network Segmentation
items.abstract: Checking whether an operational technology (OT) network satisfies a segmentation standard takes four to six weeks by hand: passive monitoring for an asset inventory, then a manual check against firewall rules. The gap is sharpest in water and wastewater, facing a December 31, 2026 deadline for Emergency Response Plans under the America #039;s Water Infrastructure Act (AWIA), where the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) finds inadequate boundary protection is its most common weakness. We built CrossCheck, a tool that answers it from evidence an operator already has: flow data and whatever policy governs it, inline rules or an access list. From those inputs it checks three of the four elements in CISA #039;s Cross-Sector Cybersecurity Performance Goal 3.I, Network Segmentation: boundary devices between segments, inter-segment traffic tight enough to contain a breach, and physical isolation where required. On a small, hand-built set, CrossCheck caught every planted violation and correctly flagged insufficient evidence; a keyword baseline for manual practice missed a real violation and guessed rather than admit it didn #039;t know. Asset classification and the standard #039;s contextual exception clause are out of scope; the design generalizes beyond water and wastewater to any OT sector built around VLAN segments behind a boundary device.
items.authors: Amit Aneja

items.title: Ornamental Fish as a One-Health Hotspot for Dual eRNA Biosurveillance
items.abstract: Ornamental fish keeping has been positioned at a busy One Health interface, where global trade, retail handling, and home aquaria create repeated opportunities for microbial exchange under uneven biosecurity and intermittent antimicrobial pressures. In this review, dual eRNA biosurveillance is proposed as a practical way to move beyond agent lists by pairing environmental pathogen signals with host-state transcripts that reflect stress, barrier disruption, and immune activation. Pathogen eRNA recovered from tank or shipment water, biofilms, and filter media is considered alongside fish-derived eRNA markers to distinguish incidental detection from biologically meaningful risk, and to prioritize confirmatory testing. Evidence is synthesized for zoonotic hazards linked to ornamental systems and for exposure routes relevant to routine husbandry, including tank cleaning, splash/aerosol contact, and skin injuries from spines or abrasions; implications of antimicrobial resistance are treated as a risk amplifier where supported. Sampling points across breeder–export–transport–wholesale–retail–home pathways are mapped, and test-to-action options are aligned with signal patterns, including quarantine, hygiene and disinfection, customer risk communication, and referral to veterinary or clinical services. Minimum operational standards and reporting elements are outlined to support field validation and comparable datasets.
items.authors: Mehran Khordshid, Abtin Tavakoli, Ehsan Pashay Ahi

items.title: Electron Beam Terminal Sterilization of a Thermolabile Retatrutide Injectable in a Multidose Cartridge
items.abstract: Background: Terminal sterilization is generally preferred for parenteral products when the formulation and container can tolerate the process. Retatrutide is a thermolabile peptide, making conventional moist heat unsuitable and creating a need to evaluate a nonthermal terminal modality. Objective: To establish an in silico decision framework for electron beam terminal sterilization of a 10 mg/mL retatrutide multidose cartridge and to define a stability indicating reversed phase high performance liquid chromatography method for post irradiation control. Methods: Moist heat, dry heat, ethylene oxide, sterile filtration with aseptic processing, and electron beam irradiation were compared by product specific criteria. A model electron accelerator configuration used a UELR-10-15-S-1 unit No. 128170401 at 9.5 MeV, 1.19 mA, 50 cm scan width, and 1.75 m/min conveyor speed. Three virtual batches were assigned dose maps, bioburden distributions, verification tests, sterility outcomes, and RP HPLC results. A Monte Carlo survivor model estimated the probability of a nonsterile unit. Results: The model selected electron beam irradiation as a candidate terminal method, subject to experimental qualification. Simulated minimum and maximum absorbed doses were 15.1 to 15.4 kGy and 18.1 to 18.4 kGy, respectively. All three virtual batches met the model criterion of a probability of a nonsterile unit not greater than 10 to the power of minus 6. Post irradiation retatrutide assay was 97.2 to 97.8 percent, while total related substances were 2.10 to 2.39 percent. Conclusions: The simulated dataset supports a bounded development hypothesis but does not demonstrate sterility, peptide integrity, process validation, or suitability for human use. Accelerator electrical settings do not define absorbed dose. Confirmatory work requires calibrated dose mapping, microbiological dose substantiation, validated RP HPLC and orthogonal structural and biological methods.
items.authors: Ilyan Kan, Oksana Chizhova

items.title: Beyond the Vehicle-to-Parts Ratio: A Four-Dimensional Value-Carrier Framework for Diagnosing OEM–Supplier Coordination in China’s Electric Vehicle Clusters
items.abstract: The concept of automotive components, centred on manufacturing output, no longer captures the software, data and computing-power assets that determine advantage in software-defined electric vehicles. Taking China as its setting, this paper asks what a component is once value is generated jointly by parts, code, information and computation. It argues that the vehicle-to-parts ratio has become unusable: the 2025 revision of sub-national vehicle production accounting broke the comparability of city-level data, and components are accounted for as a single manufacturing aggregate in which intangible value is invisible. The ratio therefore remains valid as a measure of localisation but fails as a diagnostic of technological autonomy. The paper develops a four-dimensional framework reclassifying automotive value into hardware, software, data and computing-power carriers, specifies their dependency relations, and operationalises a collaboration ecosystem index with disclosed proxy indicators and an explicit coding rubric. Applied to four Chinese clusters and to Guangzhou, it identifies four coordination modes whose profiles exhibit asymmetric complementarity rather than convergence on one optimum. OEM–supplier coordination shifts from buyer–seller transactions to symbiotic partnership, from local sourcing to network coordination, from hardware to capability procurement and from cost to innovation orientation, with Tier 0.5 integrators as the most consequential structural change.
items.authors: Xibo Wu, Jian Qin, Zhizhuan Ge, Xiangyu Wang

items.title: Unsupervised Acoustic Stimulation at Home in Users with Self-Reported Maintenance Insomnia Symptoms
items.abstract: Closed-loop acoustic stimulation can enhance slow-wave sleep and sleep spindle activity, but evidence has largely been obtained under controlled laboratory conditions. Translat-ing this approach to the home environment is important for developing scalable interven-tions for the myriad of disorders featuring deep sleep reduction, including insomnia. We evaluated the feasibility and electrophysiological effects of modeling-based closed-loop neurostimulation (M-CLNS) using a self-applied wireless EEG headband (ZMax) during unsupervised home use in adults with self-reported maintenance insomnia symptoms. Sixty-two participants completed two habituation nights followed by two counterbalanced five-night periods of stimulation or sham. Forty-nine participants contributed 330 record-ings that met signal-quality criteria. Acoustic stimuli were phase-locked to the onset of the positive slow oscillation deflection (0°). Across 230,139 phase-targeting events, stimula-tion was delivered close to the intended phase for both stimulation (mean −10.2° ± 74.5°) and sham (−4.1° ± 72.4°). Compared with sham, stimulation elicited a significant stimu-lus-locked SO response and increased spectral power in both the SO (0.5–4 Hz) and sleep-spindle (9–14 Hz) bands. Sleep architecture was not measurably altered. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of phase-targeted acoustic stimulation using wearable EEG during repeated unsupervised home use. This scalable approach provides a founda-tion for longitudinal studies investigating whether sustained enhancement of SO activity can improve sleep and daytime functioning or alleviate insomnia symptoms.
items.authors: Filip Cerny, Stefan L. Jongejan, Roy Cox, Anna C. van der Heijden, Lucia M. Talamini

items.title: Diet Quality and Co-Occurrence of Arteriosclerosis and Knee Osteoarthritis: A Cross-Sectional Survey Among Chinese Iron Workers from Shougang Group
items.abstract: Background: Arteriosclerosis (AS) and knee osteoarthritis (KOA) pose a major public health challenge, yet evidence linking diet quality to the risk of comorbidity among Chinese occupational groups remains limited. This cross-sectional occupational study examined the association between diet quality indicators and the co-occurrence of AS and KOA among 1538 iron workers from Shougang Group. Methods: Dietary data were collected using the Diet Quality Questionnaire (DQQ) for China. Multivariable logistic regression models were performed with adjustment for relevant covariates. Results: Overall, 627 workers had co-occurrence of AS and KOA, including 579 men and 48 women. Among women, a higher continuous Global Dietary Recommendations (GDR) score was inversely associated with the odds of co-occurrence (OR = 0.75; 95% CI = 0.62–0.91). Compared with a GDR score ≤ −3, a GDR score ≥ 1 was also inversely associated with co-occurrence among women (OR = 0.13; 95% CI = 0.02–0.77); however, no statistically significant associations were observed among men or in the age- and BMI-stratified analyses. Conclusion: These findings provide preliminary evidence of an inverse association between diet quality and AS–KOA co-occurrence among female workers but should be considered exploratory, requiring confirmation in larger prospective studies.
items.authors: Ping Yuan, Xin Yuan, Zihao Li, Zhenpeng Guan, Zhiyong Zou, Jing Li

items.title: Validation of Satellite-Derived and Reanalysis Solar Irradiance Databases Across Indonesia’s Tropical Climate Zones
items.abstract: Accurate solar irradiance data are essential for photovoltaic (PV) resource assessment in Indonesia, yet no hourly-resolution multi-database validation exists across the archipelago scale. This study evaluates four gridded solar irradiance databases, CAMS, JAXA Himawari-9, NASA POWER, and ERA5, against quality-controlled ground measurements from 26 BMKG stations spanning all three major Köppen climate zones (Af, Am, Aw) during 2023–2024. CAMS achieved the highest hourly correspondence (median R2 = 0.855, rRMSE = 28.1%), and JAXA was close behind (R2 = 0.848), while NASA POWER showed the lowest systematic bias (rMBE = +3.6%). ERA5 showed the largest hourly errors (R2 = 0.617, rRMSE = 41.2%) consistent with its model-generated cloud fields that are unable to reproduce the localized convective-cloud variability. Because CAMS and JAXA infer cloud from the same Himawari-9 AHI observations on a common 0.05° grid, their comparison reduced sensor and resolution-related differences and focused on the retrieval design. Both showed closely comparable performance (clear-sky R2 = 0.925 vs. 0.913), and this gap widens as cloud frequency increases across the three climate zones. All four databases showed substantially larger relative errors under overcast conditions (Kt 0.35); the temporal aggregation reduced relative error substantially, with CAMS showing the lowest error at hourly and daily scales and NASA POWER the lowest monthly rRMSE. These results provide an archipelago-scale hourly-resolution validation of four structurally distinct databases across Indonesia’s three tropical climate zones, supporting product selection and bias-correction strategies for solar resource application in Indonesia.
items.authors: Suharti Hajar, Chang Ki Kim, Hyun-Goo Kim, Myeongchan Oh, Chang-Yeol Yun, Boyoung Kim

items.title: Temporary Shift from Net CO2 Uptake to Net CO2 Release During the Southwest Monsoon in a Tropical Mangrove Forest
items.abstract: Mangrove forests are important blue-carbon ecosystems, but their atmosphere-surface CO2 exchange can vary over short time scales in response to environmental conditions. This study examined CO2 exchange in the Del Carmen Mangrove Reserve, Siargao Island, Philippines, using PhilFlux eddy covariance and micrometeorological observations from March 2025 to February 2026. We analyzed diurnal, daily, and monsoon-season patterns of gross primary productivity (GPP), ecosystem respiration (RE), and net ecosystem exchange (NEE). The tower footprint showed net CO2 uptake during most of the observation period. August 2025 was the only month with positive aggregated NEE (19 g C m−2 month−1; 95% CI: −22 g C m−2 month−1 to 62 g C m−2 month−1). During August, monthly GPP was 158 g C m−2 month−1; 95% CI: 130–189 g C m−2 month−1 and monthly RE was 177 g C m−2 month−1; 95% CI: 135–226 g C m−2 month−1. Sixteen of 31 days showed positive NEE, mainly from 8 to 24 August. We therefore interpret this as a temporary positive-NEE episode rather than a month-wide or lasting reversal of CO2 uptake. The episode coincided with dry conditions during the Southwest Monsoon. Environmental analyses identified several variables associated with variation in NEE, GPP, and RE, but these relationships are interpreted as statistical associations rather than causal effects. Since the study covers only one annual cycle, longer-term observations are needed to determine whether similar events recur. Continued flux monitoring is needed to better understand the stability of mangrove CO2 exchange through time.
items.authors: Maricar Aguilos, Renato Bacsal, Rustum Aguilos, Manuel Anthony P. Jondonero, Michael Angelo Valete, Romell A. Seronay

items.title: Research on the Impact of Logistics Operations on the Business Performance of Airlines from the Perspective of Sustainable Development—Based on the Entropy Weight TOPSIS Combined Method
items.abstract: As one of the major auxiliary businesses of airlines, air cargo transportation is profoundly reshaping their profit-making models and development landscape. Considering the high liquidity and high-risk characteristics of the air transport industry, this paper constructs a multi-dimensional evaluation indicator system covering financial and logistics operation dimensions. Taking the panel data of China Eastern Airlines from 2012 to 2024 as research samples, this paper conducts an empirical analysis of financial performance evaluation using the entropy-weighted TOPSIS combined method to verify the feasibility of the adopted approach. On this basis, with cargo indicators reflecting logistics capabilities and operational strategies as independent variables, and the comprehensive business performance index formed by coupling key financial indicators and logistics operation indicators as the dependent variable, multiple groups of experiments are designed to systematically explore the influence mechanism of changes in logistics capabilities and operational strategies on airlines’ business performance. Meanwhile, scenario experiments with varying weight coefficients are performed to observe the relevant sensitivity. The research results indicate that changes in logistics capabilities and operational strategies exert significant impacts on airlines’ business performance. This study not only reveals that enterprise operational factors can exert far-reaching influences on overall corporate performance due to varying degrees of attention they receive, but also highlights the value of air cargo, making up for deficiencies in existing research that integrates airline performance evaluation with cargo logistics. Against the backdrop of growing global economic uncertainty, this research provides decision-making references and theoretical support for airlines’ business operations and sustainable development strategic planning.
items.authors: Jingwen Liu, Hua-An Lu

items.title: Programmable Axial–Radial Multichannel Nickel Microtubes Fabricated by Core-Filament Jet Electrodeposition
items.abstract: Programmable hollow metallic microdevices with lateral outlets are attractive for distributed fluid handling, but integrating an axial lumen, side channels, and a sealed distal tip remains fabrication-intensive. Here, a core-filament jet electrodeposition (CF-JED) strategy combines segmented electrolyte-jet operation with sacrificial nylon-fiber templating to fabricate multichannel nickel microtubes. An 80 μm nylon core defines the axial lumen, whereas 50 μm transverse and helical fibers prescribe lateral channels. Interrupting the jet creates the in situ assembly interval for template placement; resumed localized electrodeposition encapsulates the fibers and can close the distal tip, and physical pull-out releases the channels without chemical dissolution or drilling. Stable growth was obtained at 2.5 mA with an axial growth rate of approximately 15 μm·min−1. Micro-computed tomography revealed a 50 ± 5 μm radial channel and a 76 ± 6 μm axial lumen interconnected within the sealed-tip structure. SEM/EDS confirmed open lateral apertures and nickel-rich walls, while water-immersion gas testing provided qualitative evidence of channel interconnectivity. CF-JED therefore provides a template-defined route to programmable multichannel hollow-metal microstructures; direct liquid-flow, mechanical, and biological validation remain necessary for application-specific use.
items.authors: Wei Wang, Hongtao Qian, Pengju Liu, Zhonghe Li, Yulong Li, Xiaohong Yang

items.title: Legal Regulation of Forest Therapy in Healthcare: Implications for Professional Practice in Lithuania and the Republic of Korea
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: This article examines legal and professional challenges related to legal regulation of forest therapy. It explores the legal and institutional frameworks governing professional forest therapy and their implications for professional qualifications, access to practice, and the organization of professional activities in Lithuania and the Republic of Korea. It also illustrates regulatory models and examples of certification practices for forest therapy professionals in the European Union (EU) and third countries, provided by public and private bodies. This study identifies similarities and differences in professional forest therapy training and qualification requirements, and considers their potential implications for professional responsibility and protecting service users. Methods: A structured comparative legal analysis of legal and documentary sources was conducted, complemented by a structured analysis of scientific literature. Results: Forest therapy is regulated through diverse, often non-harmonized legal and professional frameworks. Differences exist in the legal definition of the practice, practitioner qualifications and training, and certification and accreditation procedures. These differences may affect access to professional practice, professional accountability, and safeguards for users, especially where professional forest therapy is provided in a healthcare context. Conclusions: The lack of harmonized regulation may have relevance for legal uncertainty among practitioners and service users. Greater clarity on professional forest therapy standards, methodology, qualifications, and the relationship between forest therapy and healthcare regulation can be relevant to professional mobility, forest therapy service quality and consistency, and the protection of patients’ and users’ rights.
items.authors: Gintarė Tamašauskaitė-Janickė, Daiva Petruševičienė

items.title: From Numerical Schemes to Neural Network Architectures: A Physics-Informed Framework for Differential Equations
items.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks usually incorporate differential equations primarily through the loss function, while the neural architecture itself is selected independently of the underlying numerical structure. This work develops a scheme-induced approach in which an analytically modified numerical method defines the computational architecture, while selected elements of the numerical scheme are made trainable and refined using physics-informed loss functions. The specific contribution is the formulation and systematic investigation of a class of scheme-parameterized low-fidelity physics-informed neural networks (LF-PINNs) for evolutionary PDEs. In the implementation studied here, a compact parameter network directly controls the coefficient of a generalized θ-scheme, while the implicit update is represented by a fixed number of Picard iterations. The approach is evaluated on six one-dimensional PDE benchmark configurations against conventional, hard-constrained, and adaptively weighted PINNs. The nine-parameter LF-PINN achieves competitive accuracy on several benchmark problems, while its trainable parameter remains explicitly connected to a coefficient of the underlying numerical scheme. The results also show that performance is problem-dependent and that a small number of trainable parameters does not necessarily imply lower computational cost. Stability, ablation, computational-cost, and generalization analyses further characterize the properties and limitations of the scheme-induced construction.
items.authors: Tatiana Lazovskaya, Dmitriy Tarkhov, Igor Velikorechanin, Galina Malykhina

items.title: Rethinking the Postmortem Pupil: Biological Insights Through the Standardization of Miosis and Mydriasis
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Postmortem pupillary assessment remains qualitative and lacks standardized quantitative criteria. The Pupil-to-Iris Ratio (PIR), a described photographic morphometric measure, enables objective postmortem pupil characterization independent of image magnification. This study aimed to establish a standardized PIR framework, characterize baseline postmortem pupillary morphology, and investigate its biological determinants. Methods: Retrospective study of 83 forensic cases (166 eyes) with postmortem intervals of 3–288 h. Digital photographs were analyzed using a semi-automated workflow. A predefined proposed operational PIR classification was applied. Associations with age, sex, postmortem interval, cause of death, and toxicology were evaluated using mixed-effects models and generalized estimating equations. Results: Quantitative PIR assessment was successful in all eyes. Neutral morphology predominated (119/166 eyes, 71.7%), while miotic and mydriatic phenotypes, including their extreme categories, accounted for 17/166 (10.2%) and 30/166 eyes (18.1%), respectively. Age showed a significant inverse association (ρ = −0.352, p = 0.001). Toxicological analyses showed poor discriminatory performance (direction-normalized AUCs, defined as max [AUC, 1 − AUC], of 0.553–0.606). Intra-observer repeatability across a randomly selected subset of 62 eyes was excellent (ICC(2, 1) = 0.919), with no statistically significant systematic difference between the two measurement sessions (p = 0.052). Conclusions: Standardized PIR assessment provides an objective framework for postmortem pupillary characterization. This study establishes a reproducible methodological foundation for future postmortem pupillometry research.
items.authors: Matteo Nioi, Pietro Emanuele Napoli, Djordje Alempijevic, Aleksandar Stankov, Domenico Nieddu, Alberto Chighine

items.title: Reassessment of Horstia and Related Mites Reveals Multiple Origins of Bee Association and Supports Recognition of Two Families, Horstiidae and Cerophagidae (Acari: Astigmata), with Establishment of Phloeohorstia gen. nov.
items.abstract: This study re-evaluates the evolutionary relationships of Horstia and allied bee-associated astigmatid mites using an integrative framework combining morphological reassessment and previously generated molecular phylogenetic evidence. Our results fundamentally challenge the long-standing hypothesis that bee associations in these mites and related mites, formerly placed in “Horstiinae”, originated once from a common bee-associated ancestor. Instead, the data support multiple independent origins of bee-associated lifestyles and justify the recognition of two distinct families, Horstiidae and Cerophagidae. These findings further demonstrate the limitations of relying on host association as a primary taxonomic character in Astigmata. In the present case, bee-associated taxa are distributed among multiple unrelated lineages, consistent with repeated host colonization and ecological fitting rather than inheritance from a single bee-associated ancestor. Bee nests represent nutrient-rich and spatially discrete habitats that were repeatedly invaded by preadapted mite lineages capable of exploiting stored organic materials. At the same time, both Horstiidae and Cerophagidae exhibit strong host conservatism once established, suggesting that transitions into bee nests are evolutionarily rare but stable over long timescales. The presence of free-living species retaining plesiomorphic morphological traits further supports a free-living ancestral condition in Horstia, with bee association representing a secondary ecological transition. For the free-living species formerly placed in Horstia we propose a new genus, Phloeohorstia gen. nov. and describe Phloeohorstia corticalis sp. nov. based on both adults and heteromorphic deutonymphs. Together, our results provide a more natural classification framework for these mites and highlight the need to re-evaluate other host-associated groups within Astigmata using integrative phylogenetic approaches.
items.authors: Pavel B. Klimov, Vasiliy B. Kolesnikov, Edward Mwangi, Jonas Merckx, Marcus Duarte, Felix Wäckers

items.title: Temperature Compensation of Embedded Fiber Bragg Gratings in Deep-Sea Syntactic Foam Error Bounds and Strain Identifiability
items.abstract: Fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs) embedded in deep-sea syntactic foam are attractive for in situ structural monitoring, but their wavelength response conflates mechanical strain, temperature, and hydrostatic pressure, and the foam remains thermally unequilibrated during deployment. This study develops a quantitative framework for separating these contributions and for allocating the errors that limit mechanical strain interpretation. We report sea-trial measurements from a specimen instrumented with two strain-sensing channels (S1, S2) and two temperature-reference channels (T1, T2), deployed to approximately 4.6 km depth in the Philippine Sea. A two-channel observation model links finite-grating strain transfer, reference-channel mechanical leakage, and spatial temperature mismatch to the compensation error, and is complemented by a coupled thermomechanical–optical validation against the field data. During descent the optical strain indication reached approximately −4.4 × 103 με, and after a four-hour station keeping hold the internal temperature still exceeded the 1.6 °C seawater by 7.7 °C, confirming that thermal transients dominate the residual signal. Nominal thermal correction accounted for 76.7% of the channel-summed station keeping increment and 88.0% of the deck recovery increment—single-deployment, channel-summed point estimates rather than independent replicates. For a 10 με error allocation, the temperature mismatch limit is 0.228 °C under ideal transfer and isolation, tightening to 0.164 °C at a transfer efficiency of 0.8 and weighted leakage of 0.10, and to 0.127 °C with an additional 20 με spatial strain mismatch. The framework converts these observations into quantitative requirements for sensor pairing, calibration stability, and mechanical strain interpretation, and shows that independent thermal information improves mechanical-amplitude identifiability even when the augmented condition number increases.
items.authors: Kun Wang, Qinbo Zhang, Xie Zhao, Wei Zhang

items.title: OneBoot GRU: Validation-Locked Polynomial Calibration for Level-Invariant Encrypted Inference
items.abstract: Encrypted recurrent inference must preserve both ciphertext depth and the numerical behavior of a feedback model. We develop OneBoot GRU, which couples the validation-locked selection of degree-three Sigmoid and degree-seven Tanh domains with a CKKS GRU cell that refreshes one hidden-state ciphertext after each step. On TwoPatterns, the locked polynomial model completed finite official-test trajectories with 92.431% macro accuracy, versus 98.114% for exact activations, and 0.830% mean domain violations. On SyntheticControl, polynomial and exact macro accuracies were 89.067% and 90.133%. Direct state-error comparisons show that improved domain coverage does not always reduce recurrent error; in a separate exploratory domain extension, screening reduced qualification tail error by 74.1% and 94.6% on ECG200 and ItalyPowerDemand. A parameter profile audited against pinned 128-bit sparse-secret references completed four encrypted recurrent steps, prefix pooling, and the trained head with maximum logit error 2.91 × 10−6 relative to the plaintext polynomial circuit. In three matched four-step runs, GRU median circuit latency was 226.343 s versus 336.981 s for an implemented polynomial LSTM. Twelve additional distinct 128-step inputs were completed under an intentionally insecure structural profile, with 12/12 prediction agreement against the plaintext polynomial reference. These experiments provide measured calibration, arithmetic-fidelity, and system-cost operating points within their stated parameter and sampling scopes.
items.authors: Xinxia Song, Zhigang Chen, Liqun Chen

items.title: Search-Trajectory Patterns as Feedback for Adaptive Metaheuristic Configuration Control
items.abstract: Adaptive decisions are often based on algorithm-specific feedback or simple indicators that provide limited information about the evolving search dynamics. This work investigates explicit pattern-based analysis of the search trajectory as a source of feedback for adaptive configuration control. A trajectory-driven framework is proposed in which Derivative Dynamic Time Warping (DDTW) analyzes the recent best-so-far fitness trajectory against reference patterns representing sustained progress and lack of progress. The resulting information regulates switching between predefined exploration- and exploitation-oriented parameter configurations. Two control strategies are introduced: Binary-Simple, which reacts directly to trajectory evidence associated with a plateau, and Binary-Complex, which incorporates multiple search conditions, temporal persistence, and asymmetric switching. The framework is evaluated on 27 Multidimensional Knapsack Problem instances using BPSO, GA, BGWO, and BDE, with 31 independent runs per condition. Results show that no fixed configuration consistently dominates across metaheuristics and instances, while the effects of trajectory-driven adaptation depend on the underlying algorithm. Across 108 metaheuristic–instance conditions, Binary-Complex achieves the best mean rank (2.13). The Friedman test detects an overall difference among strategies (p=7.73×10−5); Bonferroni-Dunn post-hoc comparisons favor Binary-Complex over both fixed configurations, but do not establish a difference from Binary-Simple. Moreover, a common trajectory-analysis parameterization produces different switching behaviors across the evaluated metaheuristics. These findings support explicit search-trajectory pattern analysis as a viable feedback mechanism for adaptive configuration control across different population-based metaheuristics.
items.authors: José Villamayor, Lucas Erazo, Ricardo Soto, José Garcia, Emanuel Vega

items.title: Former Foodstuff-Based Diets on the Quality and Sensory Properties of Eggs from Laying Hens
items.abstract: In recent years, former food products (FFPs) have been gaining attention as alternative feed ingredients for more sustainable production systems. This study evaluated the impact of including FFPs on the quality of eggs produced by laying hens. A total of 180 Lohmann Brown® hens were divided into three groups and fed a control diet (CON), a diet containing 20% FFPs (T20), and a diet containing 40% FFPs (T40). Eggs, collected between 31 and 33 weeks of age, were evaluated for physical, chemical, and sensory characteristics. Egg weight, shape index, yolk and albumen weight, and edible portion were comparable (p 0.05) among the groups. Moreover, shell thickness, shell weight, and shell proportion were unaffected (p 0.05) by dietary treatments. Yolk color was affected by FFP inclusion, with reduced (p 0.05) yellowness in the supplemented groups, likely due to the lower dietary xanthophyll content resulting from the partial replacement of corn. The inclusion of FFPs had limited effects on the sensory quality of the eggs, with differences (p 0.05) in yolk color and albumen texture. These findings highlight the potential of FFPs as a viable feed ingredient in laying hen diets. Further research is needed to confirm their applicability in different diets and farming conditions.
items.authors: Luisa Zaniboni, Niko Gioacchino Zeni, Cristina Tognoli, Sabrina Ratti, Edda Mainardi, Raffaella Rossi

items.title: A Variational Neural-Field Interpretation of the Stereo-CeNN Architecture in Light of Disparity-Tuned Cortical Organization
items.abstract: Stereoscopic vision relies on the ability of the visual system to estimate binocular disparity across the visual field. In computational models, stereo matching can be represented through multiple candidate disparity hypotheses defined over retinotopic position. In this work, we reinterpret the Stereo Cellular Neural Network, here referred to as Stereo-CeNN, within a continuous variational framework and introduce a neural-field representation defined over the joint domain of retinotopic position and disparity. In this interpretation, the discrete activities of the Stereo-CeNN are regarded as samples of a continuous activity field r(x,d,t), where different disparity layers correspond to populations tuned to different disparity preferences. The binocular input drives these populations according to local matching evidence, while spatial interactions within each disparity channel promote coherent activity across neighboring retinotopic locations. The final disparity estimate is obtained, consistently with the original Stereo-CeNN architecture, by selecting the disparity channel with the largest steady-state response at each retinotopic position. We show that the layer-wise organization and local spatial dynamics of the Stereo-CeNN admit a continuous neural-field counterpart, establishing an explicit structural and variational correspondence between the discrete retinotopy–disparity lattice and a population-level representation of stereopsis. This formulation provides a conceptual bridge between the independently developed Stereo-CeNN architecture and the mesoscale organization of disparity-selective populations observed in visual cortex, without implying a one-to-one anatomical or physiological correspondence. Because Cellular Neural Networks are locally connected dynamical systems originally conceived for analog and mixed-signal VLSI implementation, the same organization is also compatible with general neuromorphic principles of local, parallel, and distributed computation.
items.authors: Andrea Zanela

items.title: WiPure: Structurally Symmetric Cross-Attention with Fixed-Wavelet, Trainable Band Processing for Interference-Robust WiFi Activity Recognition
items.abstract: WiFi channel state information (CSI)-based human activity recognition remains challenging in dynamic indoor environments because water flow and non-target motion perturb the same multipath channel as target activities. We present WiPure, a dual-stream model that combines CSI amplitude and adjacent-antenna phase difference through fixed Symlet-4 decomposition, trainable per-band filtering, multi-scale temporal pooling, and structurally symmetric bidirectional cross-attention. WiPure was evaluated on 2000 samples covering five activities, five volunteers, two rooms, and paired interference states. It achieved 95.4±0.7% accuracy under bathroom water flow interference and 91.8±1.1% under laboratory non-target person interference, outperforming the strongest comparator by 1.1 and 2.4 percentage points, respectively. Five-fold leave-one-subject-out evaluation yielded 82.6±1.7% accuracy with a 95% confidence interval of 80.4–84.8%, demonstrating transfer to unseen participants. Fusion architecture comparisons and complete factorial ablations further confirmed the advantages of reciprocal cross-modal interaction and the combined WTM–MPM–BCM design. Without fine-tuning, WiPure achieved 78.5±1.8% and 76.0±2.3% accuracy in the two cross-environment directions. These results support multi-resolution amplitude–phase modeling as an effective approach to interference-robust and privacy-preserving indoor WiFi sensing.
items.authors: Min Lou, Junhao Lai, Qingyang Kong, Jiyuan Zhang, Ruiji Xu, Keji Mao

items.title: IMTOP, IMage-TO-Print Wound Dressings: From a Single Calibrated RGB Photograph to a Patient-Specific Patch
items.abstract: Patient-specific dressings for diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) must follow the individual lesion, yet image-to-fabrication pipelines rely on depth sensing and seldom report the accuracy of the fabricated object. We present IMTOP, a low-cost pipeline that turns a single calibrated RGB photograph into a printable patient-specific patch, and we budget its area error stage by stage. Two terms were measured: on 18 polylactic acid phantoms printed by fused deposition modelling, geometry was reconstructed to 0.32% area error and printing deviated by 0.69%; on 149 public clinical DFU images (uncalibrated, single-operator reference), three reference-seeded segmenters gave median patch area errors of 3.9% to 6.0%. The scale term was simulated (assumed 3 px placement noise on a 117 px reference; standard deviation 7.3%). Monte Carlo propagation of the terms gave an estimated median absolute total error of 7.3% to 8.0%; segmentation and scale were comparable, and printing contributed under 0.1% of the variance. Mask overlap correlated with, but did not determine, the patch error. A normal perilesional offset of 14% to 21% of the wound equivalent diameter covered the wound in about 94% of cross-validated cases. The results support the feasibility of the approach as a proof of concept.
items.authors: Federico Salerno, Luca Ulrich, Jacopo Secco, Gabriele Azzena, Rossella Laurano, Sandro Moos

items.title: Functional PDMS-Based Photocurable Resins for LCD-MSLA Additive Manufacturing of Maxillofacial Prostheses: Formulation–Structure–Property and Biological Relationships
items.abstract: Maxillofacial prosthetic rehabilitation requires elastomeric materials that combine mechanical performance, dimensional stability, aesthetic reproducibility, and biological safety with compatibility with digital manufacturing. This study developed three photocurable polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)-based formulations for liquid crystal display masked stereolithography (LCD-MSLA) and evaluated formulation- and pigmentation-related differences in their physicochemical, mechanical, dimensional, chemical, and biological behaviors. Formulations with different PDMS/copolymer/silica ratios were assessed under unpigmented, natural-pigment, and synthetic-pigment conditions and compared with a commercial silicone reference. Mechanical behavior, thermal stability, color, solvent degradation, apparent porosity, dimensional stability during accelerated aging, fibroblast viability, Candida albicans biofilm metabolic activity, and ATR-FTIR functional-group conversion were evaluated. Conversion increased from 63%–77% after printing to 74%–89% after 80 °C/2 h post-curing, indicating further consumption of reactive functionalities. M1 showed the most favorable tear-resistance and elongation profile, whereas M2 exhibited the lowest apparent porosity and lowest numerical RMSE among experimental formulations during aging. Natural-pigment conditions generally showed higher fibroblast viability than synthetic-pigment counterparts; however, all material-exposed groups remained below the 70% viability threshold in the indirect-contact assay; pigment type did not significantly affect C. albicans biofilm metabolic activity within formulations. Overall, formulation composition strongly influenced material performance, with M1 and M2 showing complementary mechanical and dimensional/microstructural advantages, supporting further optimization for personalized maxillofacial prosthetic applications.
items.authors: Rogelio Danovan Venegas-Lancón, Ma Concepción Arenas-Arrocena, Rosa Elvira Nuñez-Anita, Laura Susana Acosta-Torres

items.title: Wildlife as a Potential Reservoir of Paratuberculosis: Molecular Evidence of Mycobacterium avium Subspecies paratuberculosis in a Biosphere Reserve, the Sudan
items.abstract: Mycobacterium avium subspecies paratuberculosis (MAP) causes paratuberculosis (PTB), a chronic wasting enteritis of domestic and wild ruminants. Although the disease and/or its aetiology have been reported in livestock in the Sudan, they have not been investigated in wild animals. This study investigated MAP DNA prevalence in the Dinder National Park (DNP) to provide baseline data on PTB in wildlife. Fresh faecal samples (n = 274) of wild ruminants were collected from the ground around the six major water ponds of the DNP (44–48 samples/pond). Faecal DNA was extracted using a rapid extraction protocol and tested for MAP DNA using a real-time recombinase-aided amplification (RAA) assay. The vegetation structure around the ponds was observed and described. MAP DNA detection rates around the ponds ranged between 64.4% and 22.9%, with an overall apparent prevalence of 37.9% and a sensitivity/specificity-adjusted sample positivity of 42.4%. The faecal samples belonged to Reedbuck (Redunca redunca), Warthog (Phacochoerus aethiopicus), Waterbuck (Kobus defasa), African Buffalo (Syncerus caffer), Oribi (Ourebia ourebia), and among which MAP DNA detection rates were 39.4% (28/71), 39.1% (18/46), 38.0% (27/71), 37.5% (12/32) and 35.2% (19/54), respectively. The vegetation pattern around the ponds showed a notable difference that was consistent with MAP DNA detection. These results are consistent with the potential role of wildlife in paratuberculosis maintenance and transmission. Future investigations, including genotyping, would identify possible cross-transmission of the pathogen at the wildlife-domestic animal interface.
items.authors: Enass M. Abdalla, Omer M. Meina, Sanaa M. Idris, Wisal A. Elmagzoub, ElSagad Eltayeb, Julius B. Okuni

items.title: Understanding Organic Adlayer Formation on CoOx-Terminated PtCoO2
items.abstract: PtCoO2 is an attractive candidate for next-generation interconnects due to its exceptionally low in-plane resistivity, but its susceptibility to degradation under reducing conditions necessitates effective surface passivation strategies. In this work, the deposition of organic adlayers on PtCoO2 was systematically investigated using octadecylphosphonic acid (ODPA), octylphosphonic acid (OPA), 1-octadecanethiol (ODT), and trifluoroacetic acid (TFA). The influence of immersion time (0.5–48 h) and surface pre-treatment (untreated, ethanol-cleaned, and UV-ozone-treated surfaces) was evaluated using water contact angle (WCA), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and atomic force microscopy (AFM). Low-energy ion scattering (LEIS) confirmed a CoOx-rich surface termination, which strongly influenced adsorption behaviour. Among the molecules studied, phosphonic acids exhibited the strongest interaction with the surface, with ODPA producing the highest WCAs (97–99°) and clear evidence of phosphonate bonding. Comparison with OPA revealed the importance of alkyl chain length in promoting hydrophobicity and molecular organisation, yielding values of 77–88°. In contrast, ODT exhibited heterogeneous adsorption, sulphur oxidation, and aggregate formation, while TFA showed limited surface retention. Overall, ODPA was identified as the most effective adsorbate, establishing phosphonic acid-based self-assembled monolayers as promising candidates for the passivation of PtCoO2 and related conductive oxide materials.
items.authors: Kerry Hazeldine, Jean-Philippe Soulié, Marko Vehkamäki, Mikko Ritala, Christoph Adelmann, Silvia Armini

items.title: Cryptococcal Infection in Advanced HIV-Associated Immunosuppression—Case Series
items.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Cryptococcal meningitis remains a life-threatening complication of advanced HIV infection. Its recognition can be challenging when neurological manifestations are nonspecific or cerebrospinal fluid inflammation is limited. This case series illustrates the diagnostic variability and therapeutic challenges encountered in five patients managed at a regional HIV/AIDS center in northeastern Romania. Case Presentation: Five men aged 26–69 years were hospitalized between November 2022 and March 2025 with HIV-associated cryptococcal disease involving the central nervous system. All had profound immunosuppression, with CD4+ T-cell counts of 6–31 cells/mm3. Clinical manifestations included headache, confusion, altered consciousness, and focal neurological deficits. Cerebrospinal fluid opening pressures were elevated, while inflammatory findings ranged from lymphocytic pleocytosis to an almost acellular profile. Microbiological investigations included direct microscopy, fungal culture, and molecular testing, according to availability. In one patient, culture confirmed Cryptococcus neoformans despite negative India ink microscopy and absent documented pleocytosis. Antifungal treatment included liposomal amphotericin B and fluconazole-based regimens, with treatment selection constrained by drug availability and organ dysfunction. Three cases had fatal outcomes during hospitalization. Conclusions: Cryptococcal meningitis should remain a diagnostic consideration in profoundly immunosuppressed patients with neurological symptoms, even when initial microscopy is negative or cerebrospinal fluid inflammation is minimal. These cases emphasize the importance of complementary microbiological investigations, assessment and management of intracranial pressure, reliable access to recommended antifungal regimens, and appropriate timing of antiretroviral therapy.
items.authors: Isabela Ioana Loghin, Ion Cecan, Andrei Vâţă, Anton Knieling, Otilia-Elena Frăsinariu, Victor Daniel Dorobăţ
items.title_zh: 晚期HIV相关免疫抑制中的隐球菌感染病例系列
items.summary_zh: 背景与临床意义：隐球菌性脑膜炎仍是晚期HIV感染的致命并发症。当神经系统表现不具特异性或脑脊液炎症有限时，识别可能具有挑战性。本病例系列展示了在罗马尼亚东北部一地区HIV/AIDS中心管理的五名患者所遇到的诊断差异和治疗挑战。病例介绍：五名年龄在26至69岁之间的男性于2022年11月至2025年3月期间因HIV相关隐球菌病住院，涉及中枢神经系统。所有患者均有严重免疫抑制，CD4+ T细胞计数为6-31细胞/mm3。临床表现包括头痛、混乱、意识改变和局灶性神经功能缺损。脑脊液开压升高，炎症表现从淋巴细胞增多到几乎无细胞特征不等。微生物学检查包括直接显微镜检查、真菌培养和分子检测。在一名患者中，尽管印度墨水显微镜检查结果为阴性且未记录淋巴细胞增多，培养仍确认了隐球菌。抗真菌治疗包括脂质体两性霉素B和氟康唑方案，治疗选择受限于药物可用性和器官功能障碍。三例患者最终死亡。

items.title: Planning the Surgical Correction of Age-Related Changes in the Chin Region and Neck Based on Digital and Radiological Imaging Methods: A Literature Review
items.abstract: Age-related changes to the chin region and neck are among the most common reasons for consulting a plastic surgeon, and the outcome of rejuvenation surgery largely depends on the accuracy of preoperative planning. Digital imaging methods allow for an objective assessment of individual anatomical features, personalization of the surgical strategy, and improved predictability of the result. In this narrative review, based on a structured, PRISMA-informed search (PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, and eLibrary; 65 publications included), we systematize contemporary digital and radiological imaging methods for the chin region and neck—two-dimensional photography, three-dimensional photogrammetry, computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging, cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), CAD/CAM technologies, virtual and mixed reality, and artificial intelligence tools—and assess their diagnostic value for planning rejuvenation surgery. Available preliminary, predominantly single-centre evidence suggests that CBCT performed in the upright patient position may be the most informative modality for this task: by capturing bony landmarks together with the position and outer contours of the relevant soft-tissue structures under gravitational load, it supports an objective assessment of the contribution of individual structures to age-related deformities and well-founded, individualized surgical planning. Its intrinsic soft-tissue contrast resolution is nevertheless limited compared with MRI. The integration of digital and radiological imaging methods is a vital part of modern planning of aesthetic surgery for the chin region and neck.
items.authors: Anastasiya S. Borisenko, Valentin I. Sharobaro, Alexey E. Avdeev, Sergey Y. Golovanov, Nigora S. Burkhonova

items.title: Soil Microbiome Signatures Associated with Epidemiological Heterogeneity Across Natural Plague Foci in Inner Mongolia, China
items.abstract: Plague persistence relies on complex host–vector–environment interactions, yet the ecological contribution of soil microbiomes to natural foci remains poorly understood. We performed shotgun metagenomic sequencing of 143 soil samples across four distinct plague foci in Inner Mongolia, China, to characterize microbiome features associated with contrasting epidemiological states. Taxonomic, functional, and network analyses showed that the three active plague foci exhibited lower microbial diversity, simplified co-occurrence networks, and enrichment of specific taxa, particularly Streptomyces. Conversely, the quiescent Marmota sibirica focus harbored a more complex and interconnected microbial network with greater richness and exclusive detection of Yersinia bacteriophages, showing significant concordance with bacterial community structure. These patterns indicate distinct microbiome configurations associated with specific host and geographic settings, highlighting the need to disentangle host- and site-specific effects from broader epidemiological status. Compared with surface and deep soil, burrow-associated soil exhibited greater microbial differentiation and higher richness of bacteriophages, antimicrobial resistance genes, and virulence-associated genes, suggesting its potential as a sensitive environmental matrix for ecological monitoring. Overall, our findings identify distinct soil microbiome signatures—specifically taxonomic shifts, altered network complexity, exclusive Yersinia phage detection, and functional gene enrichment—associated with epidemiological heterogeneity across natural plague foci, providing a baseline for understanding ecological variation among endemic habitats.
items.authors: Yulong Wang, Jianyun Li, Xudong Yang, Fang Liu, Guangqian Pei, Mengnan Cui

items.title: A First-Principles Study on the Adsorption and Desorption of Nitrogen on UN and U(N,C) Surfaces
items.abstract: This work employs first-principles calculations to investigate the adsorption of nitrogen atoms and nitrogen molecules on the uranium mononitride (UN) surface and the desorption behavior of nitrogen atoms, and to construct a surface nitrogen vacancy stability boundary diagram. The UN(001) surface is identified as the thermodynamically most stable low-index surface. Nitrogen atoms preferentially adsorb at hollow sites, while the most stable N2 adsorption configuration has one N atom at a hollow site and the other bonded to a neighboring U atom. Thermodynamic analysis shows that under high temperature and low nitrogen partial pressure, nitrogen atoms tend to desorb from the UN surface. The effect of carbon doping on the stability of the UN surface was further investigated. For the configurations considered, as the carbon content increases, the desorption energy of N atoms generally increases, and the surface nitrogen vacancy stability region on UN(001) is significantly enlarged, thereby effectively suppressing the desorption of N atoms.
items.authors: Panpan Duan, Wanying Li, Xiuli Han, Xiaoqiang Pan, Jing Zhang, Yonghong Lu

items.title: Regulation of Sugar Content and Glass Transition in Jujube Slices via CP-Assisted Pulsed Vacuum Drying: Effects on Physicochemical Properties and Blood Glucose Regulation
items.abstract: Although red dates (Ziziphus jujuba Mill.) are rich in nutrients and have both edible and medicinal properties, during the drying process, due to their high sugar content, they often result in a lower glass transition temperature (Tg), enhanced hygroscopicity, surface agglomeration, and a decline in storage quality, severely limiting the shelf stability of the products and the improvement of the processing quality. Cold plasma (CP) can form cavities through surface etching, promoting water migration, thereby increasing the drying rate and diffusion coefficient. Vacuum pulsation drying (PVD) has a higher drying rate, stronger mass transfer ability, and better quality retention effect compared to ordinary drying methods. Based on these characteristics, we believe that CP and PVD have a synergistic enhancing effect in the drying of date slices. Therefore, in this study, CK-PVD (without plasma pre-treatment, direct vacuum pulsation drying) was used as the control group, and CP-PVD (after plasma pre-treatment, vacuum pulsation drying), A1, A2, and A3 (after plasma treatment, soaking in different concentrations of ethanol and then vacuum pulsation drying) were used as experimental groups to study the effects of CP pre-treatment combined with ethanol extraction on the sugar composition, glass transition temperature (Tg), physical stability, and reduce blood sugar activity of dried date slices. The results showed that CP pre-treatment significantly improved the material transfer efficiency (confirmed by the increases in the areas of T22 and T23 peaks). Compared with the control group, the low-sugar group (A2) exhibited reduced total sugar content, the gel point increased to 35.6 °C, and the microscopic structure changed from regular and smooth to dense and irregular, thereby significantly enhancing the water retention stability. To further evaluate the biological activity of low-sugar red date tablets, an in vivo hypoglycemic experiment was conducted using the zebrafish model. And the zebrafish experiment further confirmed that 0.05 mg/mL of low-sugar date slices could reduce blood sugar by 11.66%, showing lower blood sugar activity. The optimized low-sugar processing conditions (70% ethanol, 50 °C, solid–liquid ratio 1:15, 2.5 h) provided scientific basis and technical support for the development of dry date products with excellent physical stability and health benefits and offered valuable references for the high-value-added processing and functional utilization of high-sugar fruit resources.
items.authors: Mingqiang Xu, Feifan Tian, Wurile Bai, Anan Zhang, Shuangyu Cao, Yan Ma

items.title: Establishment of an Efficient Softwood Cutting Propagation System for Prunus salicina Lindl. via Plant Growth Regulators and Agronomic Regulation
items.abstract: Plum is an economically important stone fruit crop worldwide, but its industrial production is limited by low propagation efficiency and disadvantages associated with conventional grafting. This study established a softwood cutting system for three elite Nai plum cultivars (‘Shibanwannai’, ‘Huangguanli’, and ‘Zaofurong’). Gradient concentrations of two plant growth regulators (PGRs), NAA and ABT, were tested in combination with integrated agronomic practices, including girdling pretreatment, a tested growing substrate formulation, and staged moisture management. The results showed that 100 mg·L−1 NAA and 150 mg·L−1 ABT yielded relatively high seedling survival rates (78% to 85%) and promoted the formation of well-developed mixed adventitious root systems. Distinct cultivar-specific differences in sensitivity to PGRs were detected among the three cultivars. This softwood cutting protocol shortens the nursery cycle to 3–4 months, compared with 18–24 months required by traditional grafting. The established high-efficiency cutting method supports standardized nursery production and may facilitate the sustainable development of the Nai plum industry.
items.authors: Honghong Deng, Yuanyuan Wang, Shishi Luo, Tingting Xie, Aoqi Xue, Feihong Chang

items.title: Effects of Mepiquat Chloride Application Timing and Concentration on Soybean Plant Architecture and Stem Mechanical Properties
items.abstract: Soybean plant architecture and stem mechanical properties are important determinants of lodging-resistance potential. To clarify the regulatory effects of mepiquat chloride (MC) applied at different growth stages and concentrations on soybean stem traits, two cultivars, Heinong 44 (HN44) and Heinong 65 (HN65), were used. Water-sprayed plants served as the control (MCK), and MC was applied foliarly at 50, 100, 200, or 400 mg/L at the V3 and R1 stages. Plant height, stem diameter, stem mechanical traits, and cell-wall components were measured. The effects of MC were strongly dependent on application timing, concentration, and cultivar. Following V3 application, 400 mg/L MC reduced the plant height of HN44 by 21.85% at R1; 200 mg/L MC increased basal stem diameter by 15.01% at R3 and fifth-internode diameter by 17.94% at R4. In HN65, 400 mg/L MC increased bending deflection by 27.01% at R1, whereas 100 mg/L MC increased cellulose content by 36.50%. In HN44, 100 mg/L MC increased lignin content by 77.39% at R2. Following R1 application, 400 mg/L MC increased bending deflection of HN44 by 29.40% at R2; 50 mg/L MC increased basal stem diameter by 20.85% at R6; and 400 mg/L MC increased stem breaking force by 36.23% at R4. In HN65, 200 mg/L MC increased hemicellulose content by 42.62% at R6. Correlation analysis showed a significant positive correlation between hemicellulose and lignin after both V3 and R1 applications, while some cell wall components were negatively correlated with stem bending deflection or breaking force. Overall, MC applied at different growth stages and concentrations regulated soybean plant architecture, stem mechanical properties, and cell wall composition; however, no single concentration was optimal across all cultivars and traits. V3 application produced a more pronounced early effect on plant architecture.
items.authors: Jiaqi Li, Zhipeng Qu, Xiaomei Li, Shenghan Du, Yuchen Zhou, Boyang Li

items.title: Experimental Study on Tensile-Shear Fracture Behavior of Sandstone Under Vertically Non-Uniform Loading
items.abstract: Based on the mechanical characteristics of hard rock strata subjected to vertically non-uniform loading conditions in mountainous regions, gullies, and similar areas, this study investigates the fracture and failure patterns of hard rock strata under such conditions. A stepped rubber cushion loading method was employed to continuously apply distributed loads across the entire upper surface of the sandstone plates. Experiments were conducted to examine the fracture failure behavior of the sandstone plates under central vertically non-uniform loading with lateral clamping constraints. The displacement, stress, strain, and electromagnetic radiation characteristics of the sandstone plates were analyzed. The research results indicate the following: (1) The stepped rubber cushion loading method successfully achieves vertically non-uniform loading on the sandstone specimens. The vertical displacement of the sandstone plates increases with the number of stepped cushion layers. The average stress proportions in the thin, medium, and thick regions are 5.0%, 61.5%, and 100%, respectively. (2) Under vertically non-uniform loading, the fracture process of hard rock strata undergoes three stages: tensile failure, shear fissure development, and shear dislocation. During the tensile failure stage, a brief, stable-hinged micro-structure exists within the rock block. The entire process dynamically alternates between structural failure and the formation of temporary stable structures, accompanied by repeated fluctuations in stress states between decrease and recovery. Upon entering the shear fissure development stage, the frequency of stress fluctuations decreases, indicating a trend towards concentrated failure and instability. In the shear dislocation stage, shear fissures connect, resulting in the maximum stress drop throughout the entire failure process. (3) Under vertically non-uniform loading, tensile-shear fracture of hard rock strata occurs on the side experiencing greater vertical load. Correspondingly, in on-site engineering conditions within mountainous terrains, areas with increased vertical stress may be more prone to roof tensile-shear fracturing, thereby inducing mining tremors. These results may provide preliminary guidance for controlling rock bursts and mining tremors in mines in mountainous and gully areas, although further validation is required.
items.authors: Decheng Ge, Tongbin Zhao, Weitao Li, Xiufeng Zhang, Quande Wei

items.title: Contrasting Effects of Chitosan Molecular Modifications on the Properties of Fish Gelatin Hydrogels
items.abstract: The limited water solubility of chitosan, which necessitates acidic conditions for its dissolution, restricts its application in food and pharmaceutical systems. To overcome this limitation, we chemically modified a chitosan molecule by introducing hydrophilic groups and compared three chitosan forms—unmodified chitosan, its quaternary ammonium derivative, and a graft copolymer with poly-N-vinylpyrrolidone, with respect to their effect on the structural and mechanical properties of fish gelatin hydrogels. An experimental study combining NMR relaxometry and water self-diffusion measurements, scanning electron microscopy, and rheology revealed a distinct supramolecular architecture of gelatin–chitosan hydrogel network for different chitosan modifications. The NMR data gave information on the molecular mobility of water as a marker of hydrogel structure to elucidate molecular basis for the observed rheological properties. Unmodified chitosan maximally reinforces gelatin network and enhances its thermorheological stability. Chitosan grafting with poly-N-vinylpyrrolidone produces a fine-pored xerogel structure with higher thermorheological stability, possibly through a non-cooperative reinforcement mechanism. The quaternary ammonium derivative results in a heterogeneous xerogel morphology with weak mechanical strength and low gel–sol transition temperature. These findings establish the structure–property correlation, demonstrating that chitosan modification governs the molecular network architecture and macroscopic performance of gelatin-based hydrogels, providing molecular-level insights into the behavior of fish gelatin–chitosan systems.
items.authors: Alena A. Nikiforova, Vladislav Abramov, Polina V. Skvortsova, Aydar A. Akhmadiyarov, Ilnaz T. Rakipov, Andrey V. Sorokin

items.title: Antimicrobial Use in European Aquaculture and the Aquatic Environment: From Regulatory Transformation to Sustainable Disease Management
items.abstract: European aquaculture is increasingly shaped by regulatory efforts to reduce unnecessary antimicrobial use and limit antimicrobial resistance risks across the human–animal–environment interface. These efforts are necessary, especially where antimicrobials are used routinely or as a substitute for husbandry or a remedy for biosecurity failures. However, stewardship in aquaculture cannot be reduced to legal restriction or lower antimicrobial input alone. Fish diseases occur in heterogeneous systems, including recirculating systems, flow-through farms, ponds, hatcheries and marine cages, with different patterns of pathogen entry, treatment delivery and environmental exposure. This review examines antimicrobial use in European aquaculture through the conditions required to make reduction clinically and environmentally workable. Its central argument is that regulatory transformation depends on implementation capacity. Aquatic veterinarians are expected to justify and reduce antimicrobial use while responding to bacterial disease events that may progress rapidly, affect populations and threaten welfare. This decision space becomes difficult where diagnostic access, authorised medicinal products, vaccines, records, surveillance systems or aquatic veterinary expertise are limited. Prevention, biosecurity, diagnostics and surveillance are discussed as decision-enabling infrastructure rather than generic sustainability measures. They reduce preventable disease pressure, help distinguish bacterial from non-bacterial morbidity, support justified treatment and provide feedback on health and environmental outcomes. The aquatic environment is treated not only as a recipient of residues, resistant bacteria and resistance genes but also as a source of risk, exposure and governance information. Responsible antimicrobial reduction is, therefore, not simple minimisation. Sustainable disease management depends on connecting regulatory ambition with veterinary decision-making, therapeutic feasibility, diagnostic support and environmental feedback.
items.authors: Konrad Wojnarowski, Dongqing Zhao, Paulina Cholewinska, Kangwei Hou, Hanna Moniuszko
items.title_zh: 欧洲水产养殖中的抗微生物药物使用与环境管理
items.summary_zh: 欧洲水产养殖正受到减少不必要的抗微生物药物使用和限制抗微生物抗药性风险的监管努力的影响。这些努力在抗微生物药物被常规使用或作为养殖替代品时尤为重要。然而，水产养殖的管理不能仅依赖法律限制或降低抗微生物药物的使用。鱼类疾病发生在异质系统中，包括循环水系统、流通养殖场、池塘、孵化场和海洋网箱，病原体的进入、治疗方式和环境暴露模式各不相同。本文审视了欧洲水产养殖中的抗微生物药物使用，探讨了实现减少使用的临床和环境条件。核心论点是监管转型依赖于实施能力。水生兽医需在应对快速进展的细菌疾病事件时，合理化并减少抗微生物药物的使用。诊断、授权药品、疫苗、记录、监测系统或水生兽医专业知识的缺乏使得这一决策空间变得困难。预防、生物安全、诊断和监测被讨论为支持决策的基础设施。

items.title: Statistical Dynamics and Conditional Lorentzian Reduction in an SL(6,C)-Motivated Cosmological Framework
items.abstract: We study the interfaces required to connect an SL(6,C)-motivated statistical geometry to a four- dimensional Lorentzian effective theory. A neutral six-dimensional metric admits three orthogonal four-plus-two inertia allocations without establishing three dynamical spacetime phases, and the pos- itive covariance compression does not select Lorentzian signature. A separate positive-fiber branch permits conditional Lorentzian reduction and a finite internal-mode cutoff. We construct a nonstation- ary reflecting diffusion benchmark whose cell occupations are actual probability integrals and whose derivatives equal boundary fluxes. For a three-well potential, we construct the normalized station- ary Gibbs density and bound a concrete resistance integral. Finite stochastic propagation yields an accumulated occupation-error bound, while finite cumulative activity leaves a quantified memory of the initial state. An explicit finite cohomology quotient carries a positive descended pairing. Within the supplied Lorentzian action, conservation, mediator bounds, charged equilibria, and tensor-source constraints retain their stated domains. A finite covariance construction controls quadratic response errors. These results strengthen individual interfaces but establish no shared cosmological solution, quantum state space, or observational prediction. A complete emergence claim still requires con- trolled metastable projection, calibrated time, dynamical reduction, coupled stress evolution, and source matching.
items.authors: Xu Hui

items.title: span data-teams="true" Protein Directional Vector and Atom Distribution Along Coordinate Axes as Quantitative Attributes in Protein Structure Modelling
items.abstract: Protein structure modelling has traditionally revolved around 3D visualisation of the atom position of all the atoms in the protein. In this work, an attempt was made to introduce more quantitative metrics to describe the 3D structure of protein and enzyme. First, protein directional vector is introduced to identify the net vector or direction of the enzyme. Specifically, all the individual vector of all the atoms in the protein are summed up into a net protein directional vector of the enzyme. In tests with four metabolic enzymes of central carbon metabolism in different microbial species, there appears to be a qualitative correlate between the 3D structure and the direction of the protein directional vector. Next, atom distribution along coordinate axes histogram plot was also introduced in this work to identify clusters of atoms along a coordinate axis. Specifically, clusters of atoms at a particular position along the coordinate axis may mean a catalytic centre, and depending on the shape of the bell-shaped peak, it could be a “shaved” catalytic centre, or relics of an ancient catalytic centre where evolutionary forces removed a large part of the catalytic domain and left behind a protein “tail”. On these postulations, evidence of such bell-shaped peak signifying a catalytic centre, as well as a half bell shaped peak reminiscent of an ancient catalytic centre with part of the catalytic domain removed or “shaved off” by evolutionary forces could be identified in hexokinase, and glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase from different microbial species. Overall, the two proposed protein structural attributes do quantify some measure of a protein structure such as its net direction (i.e., from protein directional vector), as well as its atom distribution cluster along specific coordinate axes (i.e., from atom distribution along coordinate axes), which could help visualise, using bell-shaped peak and its variants, the shape and structure of both present-day and ancient catalytic centre of an enzyme. Future work may want to explore if these two quantitative structural attributes could be applied to other classes of enzymes and structural proteins.
items.authors: Wenfa Ng
items.title_zh: 蛋白质方向向量与原子分布在结构建模中的定量属性
items.summary_zh: 蛋白质结构建模传统上侧重于蛋白质中所有原子的三维位置可视化。本研究尝试引入更多定量指标来描述蛋白质和酶的三维结构。首先，引入蛋白质方向向量以识别酶的净向量或方向。具体而言，将蛋白质中所有原子的个体向量相加，得到酶的净蛋白质方向向量。在对不同微生物物种的四种中心碳代谢酶进行测试时，发现三维结构与蛋白质方向向量的方向之间存在定性相关性。接着，本文还引入了沿坐标轴的原子分布直方图，以识别沿坐标轴的原子簇。特定位置的原子簇可能表示催化中心，且根据钟形峰的形状，可能是“修整过”的催化中心，或是古老催化中心的遗迹。

items.title: Second Fractional Order Differential Constitutive Relations for Viscoelastic Materials of the Fractional Type with Piezoelectric Properties, Representing Rheological Models of Higher Complexity Levels
items.abstract: The author presents newly derived differential constitutive relations (equations) of the second fractional order for complex, higher-level rheological models of fractional-type viscoelastic materials with piezoelectric properties. These newly derived differential equations are of the second fractional order and incorporate Caputo differential operators of the first and second fractional orders. The lecturer outlines an approximate analytical methodology for solving these second-fractional-order differential equations, employing the Laplace transform, expansion into power series with respect to the complex Laplace parameter, and the properties of the convolution of three functions. This methodology yields approximate analytical solutions for the mew derived second-fractional-order differential constitutive equations governing these complex, higher-level rheological materials. These approximate analytical solutions simultaneously serve as integral constitutive relations, establishing the link between normal stresses and axial strains in these complex, higher-level rheological models of fractional-type viscoelastic materials with piezoelectric properties. The theoretical analytical results obtained pertain to complex fractional-type material models, specifically the second-level complexity Letherish-Faraday model for a fractional-type viscoelastic material with piezoelectric properties; The Jeffreys-Faraday model represents a second-level complexity rheological model for a fractional-type viscoelastic material with piezoelectric properties, while the Burgers-Faraday model represents a third-level complexity model of the same type. These three rheological models of higher complexity—in their classical linear forms—are already widely used; the author believes that the newly introduced fractional-type models (named by the author) will also see widespread application, initially in the validation of experimental research and subsequently in practical use. The lecturer also believes that these results open up new challenges regarding the development of software for calculating inverse Laplace transforms of complex Laplace-transformed expressions, thereby expanding the scope of artificial intelligence in areas where it is currently underdeveloped and limited.
items.authors: Katica R. (Stevanović) Hedrih
