items.title: YOLO11n-Cucumber: An Efficient Model for Detecting Visual Indicators Associated with Selected Phenological Stages in Greenhouse-Grown Cucumber
items.abstract: Automated detection of visual indicator targets associated with selected phenological stages can support image-based monitoring of greenhouse cucumber. However, female flowers and young fruits are often small, partially occluded, and visually similar to adjacent developmental indicators, which complicates their detection in greenhouse scenes. In this study, YOLO11n-Cucumber was developed from YOLO11n for detecting seedling plants, female flowers, young fruits, and marketable fruits. The model incorporates an MDGC-GhostNetV3 backbone for feature extraction, a C2PSA-SCSA module for feature enhancement, and an MSF-CIoU loss for bounding-box regression. Experiments were conducted on a greenhouse cucumber dataset constructed in this study, comprising 3,849 images and 8,791 annotated instances. On the internal test set, YOLO11n-Cucumber achieved a precision of 86.4%, a recall of 84.2%, an mAP@0.5 of 86.8%, and an mAP@0.5:0.95 of 61.2%. Compared with YOLO11n, mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 increased by 2.3 and 4.1 percentage points, respectively, while floating-point operations (FLOPs) decreased from 6.4 G to 5.0 G. This reduction in FLOPs was accompanied by increases in the parameter count, from 2.6 M to 3.2 M, and in model size, from 5.6 MB to 6.8 MB. These results indicate that YOLO11n-Cucumber provides an improved accuracy–FLOPs trade-off under the greenhouse image-acquisition conditions of this study. Its generalizability across cultivars, greenhouse types, devices, and environmental conditions requires further evaluation.
items.authors: Yujing Kang, Xiaoyue Hu, Ke Zhu, Pingzeng Liu, Yan Zhang, Qun Yu

items.title: When Transfer Breaks Fairness: A Group-Conditional Perspective on Fair and Robust Adaptation of Large Language Models
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) reach users only after a chain of transfer steps: full or parameter-efficient fine-tuning, preference alignment, prompting, and changes to the decoding procedure. Each step alters the model, the distribution it faces, or both. Yet fairness and robustness are usually assessed once, on a single fixed test set. This paper presents a unified group-conditional framework to analyze how transfer affects the fairness and robustness of LLMs, and how existing methods try to preserve these properties. To characterize these trade-offs, we introduce a analytical framework that views fair and robust transfer as constrained distributionally robust optimization. We view fair and robust transfer as constrained distributionally robust optimization whose feasible set is determined by the transfer interface, and we split any change in a fairness gap into an update term, caused by changing the model, and shift term, caused by changing the data. Building on existing fairness-transfer bounds, we record two elementary consequences that the LLM literature has not made explicit: the group-conditional bound on the shift term is tight, and when only one group shifts, the marginal shift equals exactly a \( \pi_{\min} \) fraction of the fairness-relevant shift, where \( \pi_{\min} \) is that group's proportion. We use these observations to classify mitigation methods by interface and by the term they target, to offer a reading under which conflicting findings on low-rank adaptation are compatible, and to derive reporting recommendations. We close with open problems, including per-group certificates, fairness of approximate decoding, and cumulative drift under continual transfer.
items.authors: Shudong Sun

items.title: Linking Temperature to Microstates: New Thermodynamic Results for Inert and Non-Inert Gases
items.abstract: Here, we have shown that the temperature \((T)\) of an inert gas is proportional to \(w^{\frac{k_B}{nC_p}}\), where \(w\) is the number of microstates, \(n\) is the number of moles and \(C_p\) is the molar heat capacity at constant pressure and \(k_B\) is the Boltzmann constant. The above relationship has been found to be valid using experimental data in a wide range of temperature, e.g., \([298\,\mathrm{K}\text{--}6{,}000\,\mathrm{K}]\) for all the inert gases and we have documented their respective proportionality constants. On the other hand, for the non-inert gases, we have shown that the number of microstates is proportional to \[ T^{nA/k_B} \times e^{\frac{nBT}{1000k_B} + \frac{nCT^2}{2\times 1000^2\times k_B} + \frac{nDT^3}{3\times 1000^3\times k_B} - \frac{nE\times 1000^2}{T^2\times k_B}}, \] where \(A, B, C, D, E\) are coefficients of the Shomate equation for molar heat capacity at constant pressure. For three non-inert gases, namely, Hydrogen, Nitrogen and Oxygen, here we have estimated the values of the respective proportionality constants as well.
items.authors: Ahmed Mehedi Nizam

items.title: From Site-Level Detections to Monthly and Annual National Totals: Multiyear VIIRS Nightfire Estimates of Global Gas Flaring
items.abstract: This study advances global gas-flaring monitoring from a sequence of annual inventories to a monthly, source-resolved, multi-satellite record of upstream gas flaring from March 2012 through December 2025, using VIIRS Nightfire observations from SNPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21. The analysis integrates a persistent multiyear flare catalog, a calibration derived from controlled flare tests relating radiant heat to gas flow rate, and an aggregation framework that separates clear non-detections from cloud-affected, sunlit, or otherwise invalid observations. The framework yields consistent monthly and annual estimates from individual flare sites to country and global scales. Global upstream flaring reached 164.5 BCM in 2025, the third consecutive annual increase, and was highly concentrated: 4.3% of active sites accounted for 80% of the global volume. Summed monthly estimates are internally consistent with direct annual estimates (median ratio 98.1%) while revealing seasonal patterns and short-term changes hidden in annual inventories. Global estimates from the three VIIRS instruments agree within 1–4%, and comparisons with regulatory records for Texas (Permian and Eagle Ford) and New Mexico, regions with reliable reporting but atypically small and intermittent flares, show strong temporal agreement (monthly r = 0.85–0.91) and recovery of 69–96% of reported volumes. Comparisons with legacy estimates further show that differences among flaring products reflect combined changes in source coverage, calibration, satellite sampling, and aggregation rather than a uniform rescaling of annual totals. Cloud-covered overpasses must be excluded rather than counted as non-detections, which would lower global volumes by 27–30%, and the catalog must be refreshed every 6–12 months to remain representative.
items.authors: Mikhail Zhizhin, Tilottama Ghosh, Gregory Gleason, Christopher D. Elvidge, Morgan Bazilian

items.title: Anthropocene Mississippi Delta Sediment Budget Documenting Sedimentary Processes and Human Impacts
items.abstract: We present the first integrated regional subaqueous Mississippi River sediment budget to better understand how declines in sediment load from the Mississippi River over the 20th and 21st centuries contributed to the development and retrogradation of the submarine Mississippi River Delta Front (MRDF). This retrogradation can be partly attributed to downslope mass transport, which may move sediment more rapidly than replenishment from proximal fluvial sources. 210Pb/137Cs geochronology from 67 sediment cores was utilized to calculate apparent sediment mass accumulation rates (MAR) during the 20th and early 21st centuries. 210Pb and 137Cs regional maps documenting MARs from 1953 to 2025 were created to document sediment accumulation across the MRDF, which identified up to 73.8 Mt/y. A regional mass-accumulation budget for the subaqueous delta of this river-dominated system, when compared to mean 1939–2010 sediment discharge rates, indicates an approximate time-averaged retention of 25% of fluvial sediment discharge from major historical outlets on the MRDF. Furthermore, patterns of accumulation record the effects of major anthropogenic reductions in fluvial sediment load, as well as the complex interactions between oceanic and gravity-driven processes.
items.authors: Nathan Figueredo, Samuel J. Bentley, Giancarlo Portocarrero, Faith Walton, Jeffrey Duxbury, Emily Wei

items.title: Effect of Fatty Acid Saturation and Side-Chain Length on the Thermal Behavior and Morphology of Plant Oil-Based Acrylic Polymers
items.abstract: In this work, saturated plant oil-based acrylic monomers (POBMs) derived from coconut oil (CCM), babassu oil (BBM), and fully hydrogenated soybean oil (HG SBM) were investigated as building blocks for semicrystalline biobased polymers. The effects of fatty acid saturation and side chain length on free radical polymerization, copolymerization, and polymer morphology were evaluated. Increasing fatty acid saturation suppressed allylic chain transfer reactions, resulting in lower chain transfer constants and higher polymer molecular weights than those of POBMs with higher degrees of unsaturation. Copolymerization of CCM with styrene yielded reactivity ratios of rCCM = 0.44 and rSt = 0.96 and Alfrey–Price parameters of Q = 0.49 and e = 0.03, demonstrating favorable reactivity of saturated POBMs toward conventional vinyl comonomers in chain copolymerization. Thermal and structural analyses revealed a pronounced dependence of polymer morphology on fatty acid side chain structure. Polymers containing predominantly C12 side chains exhibited limited molecular ordering, whereas highly saturated C16–C18 side chains produced pronounced melting transitions and substantially increased crystallinity. Specifically, semicrystalline morphologies were observed in HG SBM-based (co)polymers with degrees of unsaturation of approximately 4 mol% or lower. Poly(HG SBM) exhibited an enthalpy of fusion of 78 J g−1 and degree of crystallinity of 37%, compared with 67 J g−1 and 26%, respectively, for poly(HG SBM-co-BBM). These findings establish fatty acid saturation and side chain length as complementary molecular design parameters for controlling side chain packing, and morphology in POBM-based polymers. The ability to generate semicrystalline materials from plant oil-derived acrylic monomers provides a strategy for extending the POBM platform toward fully biobased thermoplastic materials.
items.authors: Mariia Usiichuk, Bohdan Domnich, Yuliia Romaniuk, Vasylyna Kirianchuk, Andriy Voronov
items.title_zh: 植物油基丙烯聚合物的脂肪酸饱和度与侧链长度对热行为的影响
items.summary_zh: 本研究探讨了源自椰子油、巴巴苏油和完全氢化大豆油的饱和植物油基丙烯单体（POBMs）作为半结晶生物基聚合物的构建块。评估了脂肪酸饱和度和侧链长度对自由基聚合、共聚合及聚合物形态的影响。结果表明，增加脂肪酸饱和度抑制了烯丙基链转移反应，导致链转移常数降低，聚合物分子量高于不饱和度较高的POBMs。椰子油与苯乙烯的共聚合反应显示反应比为rCCM = 0.44和rSt = 0.96，Alfrey–Price参数为Q = 0.49和e = 0.03，表明饱和POBMs对传统乙烯共聚单体具有良好的反应性。热分析和结构分析显示聚合物形态显著依赖于脂肪酸侧链结构。主要含C12侧链的聚合物表现出有限的分子有序性，而高度饱和的C16–C18侧链则产生明显的熔融转变并显著提高结晶度。具体而言，在不饱和度约为4 mol%或更低的HG SBM基（共）聚合物中观察到了半结晶形态。

items.title: A Nonlinear Model of Complementary Regulatory Dynamics (CRD): Implications for Systems Biology and Dynamical Systems Medicine
items.abstract: Complementary Regulatory Dynamics (CRD) is a proposed integrative theory for understanding Complex Adaptive Systems (CAS). This paper develops a minimal, nonlinear Activator-Regulator (A-R) model that is extensible and falsifiable for studying CRD in CAS. Within defined boundaries and relative to a specified outcome, the functional Activator role promotes and amplifies, whereas the functional Regulator role constrains, inhibits, or restores. The model formally interprets five CRD principles: functional complementarity, mutual regulation, dynamic balance, transformation, and multiscale recurrence. It may support representations of resilience, regulatory failure, compensatory recruitment, regime shifts, and multiscale connections in CAS. Potential biological applications include gene regulation, cell-cycle progression, protein homeostasis, immune activation and resolution, neural activities, and glucose-insulin and host-microbiome homeostasis. The preliminary mathematical model may shift the focus from static biomarker measurements to patient-specific dynamical biopatterns. It can help classify disease trajectories and guide the timing and sequence of interventions. These applications may help integrate and enrich mechanistic systems biology, network medicine, quantitative systems pharmacology, causal inference, and clinical testing. Validated implementations could support analysis of dynamical biotargets, estimation of regulatory reserve, prediction of recovery or transition risks, and hypothesis formulation. CRD may help make personalized therapy and dynamical systems medicine more achievable.
items.authors: Qing Yan

items.title: Decommissioning Enterprise Software: AI Agents and the Collapse of the Replication Moat
items.abstract: I have spent the last six years building software for a living. For most of that time, one rule held: if a company bought a big piece of business software, it was stuck with it, because rebuilding that software would cost far more than just paying for it year after year. This paper is about why that rule is breaking. With an AI coding assistant that costs a few hundred dollars a month, tools that can take apart almost any program, and open models you can run on your own hardware, a single developer can now rebuild the part of a product that a business actually uses, in weeks instead of years. I walk through three real cases from October 2026, the plain economics behind them, what the law does and does not protect, why hiding how your systems work no longer keeps them safe, and who ends up controlling these tools. I am not saying software has lost its value. I am saying the industry can no longer charge people for how hard it is to leave, and the change is going to be messy.
items.authors: Elliot Saha

items.title: Powering Up for a Greener Future: Employee Empowerment and Green Product Innovation in China’s Manufacturing Industry
items.abstract: Growing environmental pressures have increased the need for the manufacturing industry to develop greener products. Employee empowerment is closely associated with green product innovation (GPI). Higher levels of employee empowerment are typically accompanied by greater employee autonomy, which may provide more favorable conditions for GPI. However, existing research offers limited insight into how empowerment specifically influences GPI during the R D process. To address this gap, this study draws on social exchange and social learning theories to explore the impact of GPI from the perspective of employee empowerment. Moreover, by positioning knowledge sharing (KS) as a mediator and green transformational leadership (GTFL) as a moderator, this study aims to explain the internal mechanisms and boundary conditions. We conducted a questionnaire survey of 199 employees in the R D departments of Chinese manufacturing firms and used hierarchical regression to analyse the data. The findings show a positive relationship between employee empowerment and GPI, with KS playing a mediating role. We also find that GTFL strengthens the effect of KS on GPI. This study contributes to the existing knowledge by offering new insights into the association between employee empowerment and GPI. For R D department heads in manufacturing companies, this study provides valuable recommendations for green product development by highlighting the importance of employee empowerment and GTFL.
items.authors: Yue Yu, Rui Shen, Chong Xin, Jiaxuan Wang

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Economic Growth in Jordan: A Mixed-Methods Study of Commercial Banking Applications as a Mediating Channel
items.abstract: We ask what artificial intelligence (AI) is actually doing to macroeconomic growth in the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, and by what route. Three channels are considered: efficiency gains, wider financial inclusion, and lower transaction costs. The paper also treats the “Commercial Banking Applications” platform, hereafter CBAs, as a mediating channel, based on the argument that innovation only reaches the real economy when some concrete piece of infrastructure carries it there. The design is mixed and descriptive–analytical. On the quantitative side, a questionnaire was administered to 403 respondents drawn from employees and experts across Jordan’s banking and financial environment. On the qualitative side, we conducted semi-structured interviews with a purposive sample of 12 experts and senior officials. Among these, the Central Bank, the Securities Commission, and the Association of Banks were represented, along with founders of financial technology start-ups. Structural and path relationships were estimated in AMOS, supported by multiple regression. AI has a statistically significant positive effect on growth overall. The total effect is 0.829 at a significance level of 0.000, and the model accounts for 65.9% of the variance in economic growth. CBAs carry a substantial share of that. Its indirect effect is 0.341, or 34.1%, delivered mainly by cutting the time and effort a transaction takes and by holding together an otherwise fragmented set of financial connections, with liquidity rising as a result. The main recommendation of this article follows from this: invest in comprehensive financial connectivity. Financial connectivity and integration proved to be the factor most closely linked with growth, which makes it necessary to invest in the development of flexible technological channels for the growth of digital systems and to ensure the technical simplicity of interactions between Commercial Banking Applications, start-ups, and government agencies.
items.authors: Salah Turki Alrawashdeh, Mohammad Yousef Abu Safia, Anas Ahmed Yaseen

items.title: First-Trimester Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone Levels and Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: A Retrospective Cohort Study
items.abstract: Background: The clinical relevance of a mildly elevated first-trimester thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) concentration is uncertain, recent meta-analyses disagree, and few studies have directly contrasted a TSH of 2.5–4.0 mIU/L with a TSH above 4.0 mIU/L. Methods: In this single-centre retrospective cohort study, 218 singleton pregnancies with a first-trimester TSH ≥ 2.5 and ≤10.0 mIU/L and a concurrent free thyroxine (fT4) measurement were classified as high-normal TSH (2.5–4.0 mIU/L; n = 168) or elevated TSH ( 4.0–10.0 mIU/L; n = 50; subclinical hypothyroidism in 47 and biochemically overt hypothyroidism in 3). The primary outcome was gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM); secondary outcomes were a composite obstetric complication, individual obstetric and neonatal outcomes, and first- and second-trimester screening markers. Two logistic regression models adjusted for maternal age were fitted; because levothyroxine was started after the index TSH measurement, it was treated as a potential intermediate and examined only in post hoc sensitivity analyses. Results: GDM occurred in 7/50 (14.0%) women with TSH 4.0 mIU/L versus 6/168 (3.6%) with TSH 2.5–4.0 mIU/L (Fisher’s exact test, p = 0.013; unadjusted odds ratio (OR) 4.40, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.40–13.76; risk difference 10.4 percentage points, 95% CI 0.4–20.4). After adjustment for maternal age, TSH 4.0 mIU/L remained associated with GDM (adjusted OR 5.24, 95% CI 1.60–17.16; p = 0.006), an estimate based on only 13 events; additional adjustment for levothyroxine use gave a similar estimate (adjusted OR 4.51, 95% CI 1.33–15.22). The composite obstetric complication did not differ (32.0% vs. 20.2%; χ2(1) = 3.02, p = 0.082; adjusted OR 1.95, 95% CI 0.96–3.98), nor did individual obstetric outcomes, neonatal outcomes or screening markers. Conclusions: First-trimester TSH 4.0 mIU/L was associated with a higher frequency of GDM. Given the few events, the wide confidence interval, unmeasured body-mass index and thyroid-peroxidase-antibody status and the absence of a TSH 2.5 mIU/L comparison group, the finding is hypothesis-generating and does not establish 4.0 mIU/L as a clinically discriminatory threshold.
items.authors: Büşra Şahin, Tansu Bahar Gürbüz, Fazilet Tatar, Rümeysa Uzun, Melike Özyurt Topuzoğlu, Ramazan Erda Pay

items.title: Aspergillus, Aspergillosis, Antifungal Resistance and Dispersal
items.abstract: Aspergillus species may be found in soil, decaying matter, and on or within plants. Some species are pathogens of humans, other animals, or plants, or cause food spoilage. Invasive aspergillosis affects three million people, mostly immunocompromised individuals, and mortality is around 50% where treatment is provided and almost 100% without treatment. Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis affects five million people, particularly asthmatics and cystic fibrosis patients. Resistance to azole antifungals is rising, possibly because of agricultural use of azoles. This review discusses Aspergillus species, aspergillosis, and Aspergillus plant infections; immune reactions and how Aspergilli counteract immune responses; risk factors and virulence factors, including the rise of antifungal resistance and the spread of resistant strains from the environment to humans. This review also discusses the dispersal of Aspergillus spores and mycelial fragments (propagules) and suggests prospects for future work, including the effects of climate change, possible research directions, and methods of detection and treatment.
items.authors: Derek Wilkinson

items.title: Physiotherapy Interventions for Migraine: A Systematic Review of Clinical Trials
items.abstract: Background: Migraine is one of the leading causes of disability worldwide and significantly reduces quality of life. Standard pharmacological treatment is often associated with adverse effects and does not always provide satisfactory long-term outcomes. Consequently, increasing attention has been directed toward non-pharmacological interventions such as physiotherapy. The aim of this systematic review was to evaluate the effectiveness of physiotherapy used as a standalone or complementary treatment for migraine. Methods: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published between 2015 and 2025 was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Electronic databases (PubMed, Cochrane Library, Scopus and PEDro) were searched using predefined search strategies. Studies involving adults diagnosed with migraine who received physiotherapy interventions (e.g., manual therapy, exercise therapy) were included. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Methodological quality of included studies was assessed using the PEDro scale. Results: Thirteen clinical trials (including 12 RCTs) involving 1021 participants were included. The most frequently investigated interventions were manual therapy and exercise therapy. Improvements in at least one primary clinical outcome (migraine frequency, pain intensity, or disability scores such as MIDAS or HIT-6) were observed in 8 out of 13 studies. A reduction in migraine frequency was reported in 4 studies. However, results were inconsistent across trials, and several studies found no statistically significant differences between the intervention and control groups. Conclusions: Physiotherapy may represent a beneficial complementary approach in migraine management, particularly for improving pain intensity and disability outcomes. However, the available evidence is limited by significant heterogeneity in intervention protocols, outcome measures, and follow-up duration, as well as the lack of quantitative synthesis. Further high-quality randomized trials with standardized methodology and longer follow-up periods are required to strengthen the evidence base.
items.authors: Helena Małgorzata Strachanowska, Martyna Anna Kaczmarska, Marlena Robakowska, Michał Brancewicz
items.title_zh: 偏头痛的物理治疗干预：临床试验系统评价
items.summary_zh: 背景：偏头痛是全球主要的残疾原因之一，显著降低生活质量。标准药物治疗常伴随不良反应，且长期效果不理想，因此越来越多关注非药物干预，如物理治疗。本系统评价旨在评估物理治疗作为单独或辅助治疗偏头痛的有效性。方法：根据PRISMA 2020指南，对2015至2025年间发表的随机对照试验（RCT）进行系统评价。通过预定义的检索策略在电子数据库（PubMed、Cochrane Library、Scopus和PEDro）中搜索相关文献。纳入接受物理治疗干预（如手法治疗、运动治疗）的偏头痛成人患者的研究。两名评审员独立筛选记录并提取数据，使用PEDro量表评估纳入研究的方法学质量。结果：纳入13项临床试验（包括12项RCT），共1021名参与者。最常研究的干预为手法治疗和运动治疗。在至少一个主要临床结果（偏头痛频率、疼痛强度或残疾评分如MIDAS或HIT-6）上均有改善。

items.title: Adsorption–Desorption Behavior of the Antibiotic Ofloxacin in Calcium-Rich Sediments at Riverbank Sewage Discharge Outlets: Implications for Sustainable Water Quality Management in an Arid Inland River Basin
items.abstract: Fluoroquinolone antibiotics are widely detected emerging pollutants, yet their interfacial behavior in the alkaline, calcium-rich sediments of arid inland river basins remains poorly quantified, which limits regional risk assessment. This study selected riverbank calcareous sediments from the Ili River and ofloxacin (OFL), a representative fluoroquinolone, and used batch adsorption–desorption experiments to quantify the retention of OFL and the regulatory roles of pH and coexisting cations. Adsorption was biphasic, with a fast stage ( 1 min) followed by slow equilibration, and equilibrium was approached within 8 h. When the pseudo-first-order (PFO), pseudo-second-order (PSO), and Elovich models were all fitted by nonlinear least squares on the original q-t scale, the Elovich model gave the best description at both 1 and 10 mg L−1 (R2 = 0.829 and 0.589, lowest AIC), whereas PFO and PSO performed poorly over the full time range (R2 = 0.20–0.53). Boyd analysis indicates that particle diffusion dominates for the two XFD datasets, whereas a significant positive intercept in a second sediment series shows that film diffusion also contributes. Desorption kinetics were also best described by the Elovich model (R2 = 0.929). Isotherm analysis with 4–11 data points per temperature (rather than the three points used previously) showed that the Langmuir and Freundlich models fit the data comparably, so the results do not justify discriminating between monolayer and multilayer uptake (difference in AIC ≤ 1 at 15 and 35 °C, and 6.5 in favor of Langmuir at 25 °C); the corresponding Dubinin–Radushkevich mean free energy of 0.08–0.25 kJ mol−1 indicates physisorption-dominated uptake. Thermodynamic parameters calculated from the 15/25/35 °C series by the van’t Hoff relation gave Delta-G = −20 kJ mol−1 (spontaneous), Delta-H = −14.5 ± 13.2 kJ mol−1, and Delta-S = 20.5 ± 44.3 J mol−1 K−1, i.e., a weakly exothermic, entropy-assisted process whose enthalpy term is not statistically significant; the 5/15/25 °C series was non-monotonic and is therefore not used to derive the enthalpy. Desorption exceeded adsorption (maximum desorbed/adsorbed ratio 106–136%) and the Freundlich-based hysteresis index rose from −0.09 at 5 °C to 0.37 at 25 °C, so part of the sorbed OFL is retained against desorption. Coexisting cations inhibited OFL adsorption through competition for surface sites, following the order Mg2+ Ca2+ Na+ at matched molarity (0.01 mol L−1), and the inhibition intensified with increasing cation concentration. Because Na+ was applied at the same molarity as Mg2+ as an ionic-strength control while Ca2+ was also applied at a higher concentration, the ranking reflects specific competition by the divalent cations combined with a weaker double-layer (ionic-strength) effect for the monovalent ion. Acidic pH enhanced adsorption and alkaline pH suppressed it, consistent with the change in OFL speciation from cationic through zwitterionic to anionic. This work quantifies the adsorption–desorption behavior of OFL on arid-region calcareous sediments and provides parameter values with uncertainty estimates that support risk assessment and pollution control in the Ili River Basin. From a sustainability perspective, the work converts these site-specific measurements into transferable, uncertainty-bounded parameters (Langmuir and Freundlich capacities, the linear partition coefficient Kd and the hysteresis index) for a sediment type that is widespread in arid inland river basins. It therefore supplies directly usable input for the definition and quantification of water-quality sustainability indicators, the monitoring of the sediment buffering function over time, and the setting of discharge-outlet effluent limits and the seasonal screening of secondary-pollution risk during the warm, low-flow irrigation period, thereby connecting a mechanistic sorption study to the wider objective of sustaining safe water use in a water-scarce region.
items.authors: Xiao Wang, Rensheng Lv, Tianwei Qi, Xiaolan Ma, Pengguo Liu, Bingjie Wang

items.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Multi-Location ABL Wind Profiling with Minimal Instrumentation
items.abstract: The vertical wind profile within the Atmospheric Boundary Layer (ABL) is a critical variable for a wide range of applications, including wind energy, air traffic and Unmanned Aerial System (UAS) management, pollutant dispersion, and urban air mobility. However, its accurate characterization typically requires expensive vertical-profiling LiDAR instruments, which limits the number of locations that can be simultaneously monitored. Building upon previous work in which machine-learning algorithms were trained on LiDAR data from the University of León (Spain) to reconstruct full ABL wind profiles from a single near-surface measurement, this study replaces the traditional data-driven neural network approach with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), embedding a physical constraint directly into the loss function as evaluated by automatic differentiation, and tests two such constraints under architectural control: the Ekman boundary-layer momentum balance, closed with a Monin–Obukhov eddy viscosity, and a shear-constrained formulation based on a power-law profile with an inferred exponent. With dense supervision at the target heights, neither constraint improves on an architecture-matched network without a physical term (RMSE 1.35–1.36 m/s, direction MAE 20.1–20.4∘ across all three, Kruskal–Wallis p=0.0125). In a vertical-extrapolation protocol, training with gates up to 111 m, selecting models by their skill at 140 m, and testing blind on 170–300 m, the Ekman constraint shows no detectable advantage over its own architectural control. In contrast, the shear-constrained model does, reaching 1.80±0.01 m/s speed RMSE and 27.0∘±0.3∘ direction MAE against 2.66±0.10 m/s and 34.2∘±1.8∘ for the Ekman-constrained arm and 2.61±0.12 m/s and 33.9∘±2.0∘ for the physics-free arm, which are statistically indistinguishable from one another; the shear-constrained gain is confirmed against its own architectural control (2.64±0.08 m/s, 33.0∘±1.8∘, matching the physics-free arm), ruling out the additional output as the explanation, and converts an erratic extrapolator into a stable one. The results are consistent with the benefit of embedding physics into the loss being therefore specific to the extrapolation regime and to the formulation tested, not a generic property of physics-informed learning. These findings are based on data from a single suburban site, and multi-site validation remains necessary before they can be generalized. By eliminating the need for continuous LiDAR operation after the training phase, the proposed methodology aims to enable cost-effective monitoring of multiple locations with a single instrument.
items.authors: Rubén Echeverría, Luis Santamaría, Fernando Parra, Adrián Delgado, Adrián García-Gutiérrez

items.title: Developing a Conceptual Framework: Integrating Tumour, Macroenvironment and Resource (TMR) as a Composite Determinant of Ovarian Cancer Outcome in Diverse Resource Settings
items.abstract: Background: Ovarian cancer (OC) poses an escalating global health burden, with marked disparities in incidence, mortality, and survivorship. Social, psychological, and structural determinants, including deprivation, stigma, and access to specialist care, may influence outcomes but are not well-represented in existing models of cancer care. We introduce the Tumour, Macroenvironment and Resource (TMR) framework, a novel conceptual model exploring interactions among tumour biology, social determinants, and healthcare resources in OC survivorship and care. Methods: Framework development occurred in three phases. First, a narrative review identified factors influencing OC outcomes across tumour, macroenvironmental, and healthcare resource domains. Second, multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) was used to structure these factors within a preliminary framework and assign indicative domain weightings. Third, two cross-sectional expert opinion surveys were conducted to refine and validate the concept of the framework. The final model was then evaluated in a retrospective pilot cohort to assess the feasibility of collecting predefined TMR variables from routinely available clinical data. Results: The review identified limited evidence addressing broader determinants of health beyond biological prognostic factors. Available studies suggested interactions between tumour characteristics, social determinants, and healthcare infrastructure that may influence outcomes. A preliminary model allocated 50% weighting to tumour factors and 50% to combined macroenvironmental and healthcare resource factors. Expert surveys (n = 20 and n = 44) achieved consensus and informed development of the final TMR framework. Application to a UK pilot cohort of patients with OC (n = 42) demonstrated the feasibility of collecting variables across all TMR domains and identified multiple adverse factors across tumour, macroenvironmental, and resource domains. Conclusions: The TMR framework provides an integrative, hypothesis-generating model for exploring disparities in OC survivorship and care. Further retrospective and prospective validation are required before clinical or prognostic applications can be considered.
items.authors: Asima Mukhopadhyay, Adam Ruddock, Mohamed Elsebaei, Ally Memon, Daity Bhattacharjee,
items.title_zh: 构建肿瘤、宏观环境与资源综合框架以影响卵巢癌结果
items.summary_zh: 背景：卵巢癌（OC）在全球健康中造成日益严重的负担，且在发病率、死亡率和生存率上存在显著差异。社会、心理和结构性因素，如贫困、污名和专业护理的可及性，可能影响结果，但在现有癌症护理模型中表现不足。我们提出了肿瘤、宏观环境与资源（TMR）框架，这是一个新颖的概念模型，探讨肿瘤生物学、社会决定因素和医疗资源在OC生存和护理中的相互作用。方法：框架开发分为三个阶段。首先，通过叙述性综述识别影响OC结果的因素。其次，采用多标准决策分析（MCDA）将这些因素结构化并分配初步权重。最后，通过两项横断面专家意见调查来完善和验证框架概念。结果显示，现有研究对超出生物预后因素的健康决定因素证据有限。

items.title: Stock Exchange Trading Optimization Algorithm Improved Based on Information Technology Investment Analysis for Numerical Optimization and Practical Problems
items.abstract: Stock Exchange Trading Optimization (SETO) is a population-based metaheuristic with a compact market-inspired search framework, but its performance may be limited by uneven random initialization, coarse Relative Strength Index-based search-state identification, and excessive concentration of trading resources. To address these limitations, this study proposes an improved SETO, termed ISETO, by reformulating concepts from information technology investment analysis into population-search mechanisms. First, an IT investment portfolio screening initialization strategy jointly considers solution quality and spatial diversity to improve initial population coverage. Second, a discounted-return and downside-risk dual-state search strategy evaluates the magnitude, temporal relevance, and risk of historical improvements to adaptively coordinate exploration and exploitation. Third, an entropy-regularized real-option capital reallocation strategy redistributes search resources according to solution quality, capital efficiency, technical debt, and population diversity, while reinvesting abandoned candidates into underexplored regions to mitigate stagnation. The dominant computational complexity remains approximately O(TmaxND). ISETO is evaluated on 22 benchmark functions from the IEEE CEC2020 and CEC2022 suites under 10- and 20-dimensional settings and compared with nine representative metaheuristic algorithms. Under the conventional iteration-based setting, ISETO achieves the best or tied-best mean results on all CEC2020 functions at both dimensions, all 12 CEC2022 functions at 10 dimensions, and 11 of the 12 CEC2022 functions at 20 dimensions. Additional experiments under an identical objective-function evaluation budget confirm that these advantages are not simply caused by additional function evaluations. Holm-adjusted statistical tests and Cliff’s delta effect sizes further support the significance and practical magnitude of the observed improvements. Ablation experiments verify that all three proposed mechanisms contribute positively, while parameter sensitivity and population-diversity analyses demonstrate that ISETO is relatively robust to parameter variation and better able to preserve exploration capability during evolution. The additional mechanisms introduce only a moderate runtime overhead relative to the original SETO. ISETO is further applied to a three-dimensional robotic-arm path-planning problem. Over 30 independent runs, it obtains a best objective value of 290.69 and a mean value of 291.91. Its best result is 5.56% lower than the best competing result, while its mean result improves upon the original SETO by approximately 6.02%. These results demonstrate that ISETO provides improved convergence accuracy, robustness, and search diversity while retaining competitive computational efficiency, and has promising potential for constrained engineering optimization.
items.authors: Jinze Li, Chengpeng Li

items.title: Advances on Anti-Cancer Combination Therapies Targeting DNA Repair Pathway, Epigenetics, Microbiomes and the Immune System
items.abstract: Modern pipelines integrating multi-omics data, chemical libraries, structural biology information and artificial intelligence are currently accelerating drug discovery and precision medicine. Aligned with these advances, the multi-omics profiling technologies enable the identification of unique genetic and epigenetic signatures for stratification of patients based on cancer specific target and vulnerability. Targeted therapies to specific receptor or enzyme mutated or overexpressed often fail because cancer cells can adapt quickly. Tumor cells overgrow driven by new gene mutation and parallel crosstalk of signaling pathways. Patients with cancer and the hereditary syndrome targets such as BRCA1/2, and emerging targets such as ATR, CHK1, WEE1, and POLθ, are hypersensitive to ionizing radiation and PARP inhibitors. Combining synthetic lethality inhibitors, chemotherapy and immunotherapy effectively kill cancer cells by breaking multiple survival signaling pathways. Antibodies to immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting molecules like PD-1, PD-L1, and CTLA-4 can improve survival of patients, though predictive immunotype remains challenging. Emerging pharmacological approaches combining either epigenetic modifiers, oncomicrobiotics or engineered bacteria sequentially convert tumors into a highly antigenic, T cell-inflamed, and checkpoint-responsive tumor, providing a mechanistically grounded framework for next-generation precision immunotherapy. However, large human clinical trials remain necessary to standardize protocols, biomarkers and long-term efficacy. Cancer vaccines have evolved through rational engineering synthetic mRNA encoding tumor-specific antigens or tumor-associated antigens. This will enable the next generation of truly therapeutic and preventive vaccines for many cancers. This review provides a timely synthesis of the basic mechanisms for rational multidrug treatments for cancers.
items.authors: José E. Belizário
items.title_zh: 针对DNA修复通路的抗癌组合疗法进展
items.summary_zh: 现代药物发现与精准医学的进展依赖于多组学数据、化学库、结构生物学信息和人工智能的整合。多组学分析技术能够识别独特的遗传和表观遗传特征，从而根据癌症特异性靶点和脆弱性对患者进行分层。针对特定受体或酶的靶向治疗常因癌细胞快速适应而失败。肿瘤细胞因新基因突变及信号通路的交叉作用而过度生长。BRCA1/2等遗传综合征靶点及ATR、CHK1、WEE1和POLθ等新靶点的癌症患者对电离辐射和PARP抑制剂高度敏感。结合合成致死抑制剂、化疗和免疫疗法可有效破坏多条生存信号通路以杀死癌细胞。针对PD-1、PD-L1和CTLA-4等分子的免疫检查点抑制剂抗体可改善患者生存，尽管预测免疫类型仍具挑战性。新兴药理学方法结合表观遗传修饰剂、肿瘤微生物或工程细菌，逐步将肿瘤转化为高度抗原性、T细胞炎症和检查点反应的肿瘤。

items.title: Fire Detection Algorithm for Complex Warehouse Scenarios Based on YOLOv11n
items.abstract: Fire detection in warehouse scenarios is challenged by complex background interference, weak features of small flame targets, and indistinct flame textures, which can reduce detection performance and constrain model deployment. To address these issues, we propose FC-YOLO (Fire Complexity-YOLO), a lightweight fire detection algorithm based on YOLOv11n. A dynamic upsampling module (DySample) is introduced into the neck network to adaptively adjust feature sampling locations and reduce information loss. An adaptive downsampling module (ADown) is employed in the backbone and neck networks to reduce computational complexity while enabling efficient multi-scale feature extraction. A residual multi-scale attention module (IEMA) is constructed in the neck network to enhance feature representation and focus on critical regions. Finally, an additional small-object detection layer (P2) is introduced to improve small-flame detection. On a self-built flame dataset, FC-YOLO achieves 91.8% precision, 84.7% recall, 90.1% mAP@0.5, and 50.0% mAP@0.5:0.95 with 2.2M parameters. Compared with YOLOv11n, these metrics improve by 1.8%, 4.6%, 2.4%, and 3.7%, respectively, while parameters decrease by 14%. These results demonstrate that FC-YOLO improves detection performance and robustness in complex fire scenarios while maintaining a lightweight architecture, indicating strong potential for deployment on edge devices.
items.authors: Liwei Guan, Bicai Li, Junjie Lu, Yunping Wu, Wenzao Shi, Zhigao Huang

items.title: Immunosenescence in Aging and Cancer: Molecular Mechanisms, Tumor Microenvironment Remodeling, and Therapeutic Implications
items.abstract: Immunosenescence is the decline in immune function with age, which influences cancer progression and treatment outcomes. This process arises from multiple, interconnected molecular and cellular alterations. Among these, mitochondrial dysfunction in aged immune cells may contribute to impaired immune function through altered metabolism, redox imbalance, and inflammatory signaling. This review discusses mitochondrial alterations alongside other age-related mechanisms that shape immune cell function and may promote cancer development. We examine how DNA damage, telomere shortening, epigenetic changes, altered proteostasis, and mitochondrial dysfunction contribute to immune aging and potentially compromise antitumor immunity. The aged tumor microenvironment is characterized by increased immunosuppressive cell populations, persistent inflammatory signaling, and metabolic alterations that can influence tumor development and therapeutic responses. We also examine how aging affects response to current cancer immunotherapies. While some treatments show comparable efficacy in older and younger patients, others may be less effective in the context of age-related immune dysfunction. Older patients may also experience distinct toxicity profiles that require careful clinical management. Understanding how mitochondrial alterations interact with other mechanisms of aging to shape immunosenescence may help identify therapeutic strategies for cancer in older adults. Future approaches may combine interventions targeting mitochondrial fitness, chronic inflammation, and cellular senescence. However, clinical studies specifically designed to include older populations are needed to establish the relevance of these mechanisms in cancer and to guide age-specific therapeutic strategies.
items.authors: Yusra Zarlashat, Syed Salman Shah, Seerat-Uz-Zahra, Rosa Di Lorenzo, Anna Picca
items.title_zh: 衰老与癌症中的免疫衰老：分子机制与治疗启示
items.summary_zh: 免疫衰老是指随着年龄增长免疫功能的下降，这一过程影响癌症进展和治疗结果。免疫衰老源于多种相互关联的分子和细胞变化，其中老化免疫细胞的线粒体功能障碍可能通过代谢改变、氧化还原失衡和炎症信号传导导致免疫功能受损。本文讨论了线粒体变化及其他与年龄相关的机制如何影响免疫细胞功能并可能促进癌症发展。我们分析了DNA损伤、端粒缩短、表观遗传变化、蛋白质稳态改变和线粒体功能障碍如何导致免疫衰老，并可能削弱抗肿瘤免疫。老年肿瘤微环境特征为免疫抑制细胞群体增加、持续的炎症信号和代谢改变，这些因素会影响肿瘤发展和治疗反应。此外，我们探讨了衰老如何影响对当前癌症免疫疗法的反应。部分治疗在老年患者和年轻患者中显示出相似的疗效，但在与年龄相关的免疫功能障碍背景下，其他治疗可能效果较差。老年患者还可能经历不同的毒性反应，需要仔细的临床管理。

items.title: Development of the MWU-Based Combined Standard Time Model for Work-Procedure Reconstruction and Man-Hour Estimation in Shipbuilding Outfitting Work
items.abstract: A Standard Time Unit (STU), defined as standard work time per unit workload, supports production planning and man-hour estimation in shipbuilding. This study developed a Combined Standard Time Model (CSTM) that reconstructs outfitting work standards by recombining reusable work actions. Process analysis structured outfitting work into five Basic Standard Units (BSUs), 16 Minimum Work Units (MWUs), and 54 Factors (six quantity-type and 48 condition-type). The same fixed-order MWU candidate set was applied to all ten evaluated materials, while material-specific procedures were represented through MWU selection and Factor settings. Base MWU time units and Factor values were derived from existing STU records supplemented by expert judgment. The absolute percentage errors for the ten materials ranged from 0.178% to 2.514%, and all were below 3%, with a mean of 1.281% and a standard deviation of 0.839%. The paired t-test yielded t = 1.617 (p = 0.140), the Pearson correlation was r = 0.999, and Bland–Altman analysis showed a mean difference of 0.305 min with estimated 95% limits of agreement from −0.863 to 1.473 min. Applied without re-adjustment to 13 further materials not used in parameter setting, the model gave a mean absolute percentage error of 3.387% against the existing unit-rate values. Thus, the CSTM maintained numerical consistency with the existing STUs while enabling a standardized labor-time framework and component-level traceability across the evaluated materials. Because model parameterization and evaluation used the same STU records, the results demonstrate internal reconstruction rather than independent predictive superiority; validation against measured work times remains necessary.
items.authors: Won Park, Se-Yun Hwang, Jae-chul Lee, Seunghoon Oh, Ye-Na Lee, Soonsup Lee
items.category_raw: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering

items.title: Sustainable Remediation of Acidic and Metalliferous Mine Drainage Using an Adsorption-Constructed Wetland System: A Hybrid and Clean Approach
items.abstract: The efficacy of an engineered treatment wetland system was explored for the treatment of real acid mine drainage. Precisely, the treatment chain was a hybrid approach made up of two distinct stages comprising neutralization with magnesite (stage 1) and phytoremediation using a hydroponic floating wetland planted with Vetiver grass (stage 2). Both stages were operated in step-wise connection at the same flow rate of 1.6 L/d and with a hydraulic retention time of 40 days. Leachates were collected daily at the outlet of each wetland and the concentrations of inorganic pollutants were quantified. The findings revealed that pH increased from 2.8 to 8.4, demonstrating a significant attenuation of inorganic pollutants in the following order: Cu, Ni and Zn (100% each) Fe (99.9%) Al (99.7%) Mn (96.41%) SO42− (77.62%) and a moderate reduction in electrical conductivity (80.7%). Explicitly, a significant quantity of inorganic pollutants was attenuated in stage 1, while stage 2 further purified and polished the water to the desired standard. This, therefore, denotes the effective combination and complementary performance of the hybrid approach.
items.authors: Beauclair Nguegang, Abayneh Ataro Ambushe

items.title: Geopolitical Risk in the Financial Sector: A Systematic Bibliometric Review
items.abstract: Geopolitical risk (GPR) is increasingly recognized as a central concern for financial stability, yet its transmission to the financial sector remains relatively underexplored. To address this gap, a Bibliometric–Systematic Literature Review combining PRISMA-guided screening with bibliometric performance analysis and science mapping (Bibliometrix 5.4.0, VOSviewer 1.6.21) was carried out. A total of 604 journal articles were retrieved from Scopus on the broader GPR and finance literature, including a subsample of 78 documents addressing banking (67), insurance (10), and both sectors jointly (1). Results of the analysis show that scientific production accelerates sharply from 2018, with growth in the banking- and insurance-focused subsample outpacing growth in the field overall. Our co-citation analysis of cited references and authors finds that the field’s intellectual core is organized around Caldara and Iacoviello’s foundational GPR index, alongside clusters extending towards commodity and energy market applications and spillover-index methodology, with four distinct author-centered citation clusters identified; the co-authorship analysis further identified China as the dominant contributor to international research collaboration. Our analysis adds to the growing body of bibliometric reviews on GPR to provide a structured research agenda for future investigations, particularly regarding the still-limited evidence on insurance relative to banking.
items.authors: Elisabetta D’Apolito, Grazia Onorato, Maddalena Salerno

items.title: Geomaterials and GPR Characterisation of the Castellina Fortress (Norcia, Umbria, Italy): Construction and Reconstruction from the 1500s to the Present
items.abstract: An integrated petrographic–geophysical workflow is applied to the Castellina Fortress (16th century AD) to investigate: the masonry texture, construction techniques and lithological provenance. The field activities focused on several architectural structures of the Castellina, including the main façade that was embedded inside the fortress out of a previous building, named Podestà Palace (13th century AD). The petrographic analyses document the use of lithoid limestones from the Maiolica, Scaglia Bianca and Scaglia Rossa Formations (Umbria–Marche Stratigraphic Succession) in the Podestà Palace, while limestone breccias can be mainly found in the cloister columns. The Ground-Penetrating Radar (GPR) data, supported by advanced numerical modelling, show a heterogeneous internal texture in the Castellina Fortress related to the use of both lithoid materials and earthquake-derived debris for the columns. The provenance analysis points out that the limestones were quarried from Monte di Colle, Monte Belvedere and Monte Poggio Vallaccone (southeast of Norcia), whereas the breccias largely derived from debris cones composed of breccia, gravel, and conglomerate deposits that still crop out today in the mountainous area surrounding the plains of Norcia and Santa Scolastica. This study demonstrates the potential of combining two different geoscience disciplines to reconstruct material supply zones and building characteristics in the field of cultural heritage.
items.authors: Giorgio Alaia, Angela Bertinelli, Angela Baldanza, Regina Lupi, Luca Pasqualone, Maurizio Ercoli

items.title: Fourier-Based Characterization of Reflective Surface Topography Using a Heterodyne Optical Profilometer
items.abstract: Optical profilometry based on heterodyne interferometry was used to characterize the lateral surface topography of reflective surfaces with microstructures. A 633 nm laser beam is split into an unshifted object beam and a reference beam that is frequency-shifted by 80 MHz using a traveling-wave acousto-optic modulator. The object beam is focused onto the sample through a 100× microscope objective, recombined with the reference beam, and detected using a photodetector with a bandwidth of 150 MHz. At each scan position, a Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP) acquires the beat signal, and Fourier analysis isolates the heterodyne component. Electrical tests verified the recovery of a prescribed low-amplitude modulation, whereas translation of a plane mirror through focus identified a monotonic region for displacement-sensitive operation. Reflective silicon microstructures and a nominal 300 lines mm−1 grating were examined. The reconstructed maps reproduced the principal lateral features observed by scanning electron microscopy (SEM). For the grating-period comparison, the SEM-derived mean was 3.545 μm, whereas the heterodyne reconstruction yielded a representative period of approximately 3.50 μm, corresponding to an absolute difference of approximately 0.045 μm (1.3%). The present experiments establish Fourier-domain signal recovery and lateral morphological characterization. Because a traceable axial calibration and an uncertainty budget were not available, the reconstructed vertical coordinate remains qualitative, and the results do not yet establish quantitative surface-roughness parameters.
items.authors: Anuar B. Beltrán-González, Geminiano Martínez-Ponce, Guillermo García-Torales, Azael Mora-Núñez

items.title: Electrocrystallization in Rechargeable Batteries: A Review
items.abstract: This work systematically explores the core foundational mechanisms and kinetics of the metal electrocrystallization processes at the anodes of the most studied rechargeable batteries relying on electrodeposition. The analysis requires a consideration of the theoretical principles of electrochemical phase formation, including thermodynamic and kinetic models, with a strong focus on the underlying mechanisms of nucleation and growth. The review provides a comprehensive comparison of alkali and multivalent metals, highlighting their distinct electrocrystallization behaviors in the context of metal anode batteries. Specific focus is placed on metal electrodeposition on foreign substrates, which is relevant to anode-free rechargeable batteries. In these systems, precise control of nucleation and growth is essential, as homogeneous surface morphology is important for avoiding localized crystal growth and the formation of hazardous dendrites that can cause short-circuiting. Special attention is paid to the critical analysis of electrochemical crystal growth with an emphasis on the conditions and mechanisms of developing dendritic and uniform surface morphologies. The aspects of multiple nucleation in the studied systems are discussed. This work will assist electrochemists, material scientists and development engineers to identify optimal operating parameters and conditions for designing batteries based on electroplating. The interrelation between nucleation and growth and battery performance is demonstrated by representative examples.
items.authors: Svetlozar Ivanov, Mario Kurniawan

items.title: Cultural Differences and Quality Trust in Sustainable Cross-Border Closed-Loop Photovoltaic Supply Chain Network Design
items.abstract: Green manufacturing of photovoltaic (PV) modules and the rapid evolution of cross-border production models have given rise to prominent environmental issues and severe cultural differences. Therefore, incorporating sustainability and cultural differences into supply chain network design is particularly necessary. First, this study considers the carbon tax price, the consumer quality trust index (QTI) for recycled and remanufactured products, and the cultural differences faced by cross-border manufacturers. A mixed-integer programming model is constructed for the optimal design of a cross-border PV module supply chain network, incorporating three objectives: economic cost, environmental, and social benefit. The model aims to minimize economic cost and carbon emissions while maximizing social benefit. Second, a triangular fuzzy function is introduced to handle uncertain parameters in the model, and a non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm is used to solve the model and obtain the optimal solution. Finally, a sensitivity analysis of the carbon tax price and cultural differences is conducted, and the effects of different QTI levels on the supply chain network are discussed. The results indicate that these factors have a significant impact on the designed sustainable supply chain network. This study contributes to the sustainable development of cross-border manufacturing enterprises and enhances their ability to cope with cultural differences. It provides effective support for governments in formulating sustainable development policies, for manufacturers in determining procurement ratios, and for supply chain entities in addressing cultural differences.
items.authors: Chengcheng Li, Yuxiang Xia

items.title: Digital Transformation, Carbon Disclosure, and Green Innovation in Energy Transition: Firm-Level Evidence from China’s Energy Sector
items.abstract: China’s dual-carbon goals have made understanding how digital transformation shapes corporate carbon performance a policy priority, and the rapid expansion of firm-reported emissions disclosure since 2020 now makes such inquiry feasible at scale. Drawing on CSMAR financial data and CNRDS digital-transformation keyword frequencies for 914 A-share energy firms over 2020–2025, we combine panel fixed-effects models, a placebo-validated triple-difference design, disclosure-choice models with a Heckman selection correction, and event studies of two policy milestones. We find that digital transformation robustly stimulates green-patent applications and significantly raises the likelihood of carbon disclosure in the cross section, identifying green-patenting and disclosure as the two margins on which digitalization is already measurable. The direct association with disclosed carbon intensity remains statistically insignificant in the selection-corrected model and on the directly disclosed subsample, indicating that emission reductions are not yet measurable at the firm level. A sharp but short-lived emission-reduction pulse among digitalized high-carbon firms in 2021 is consistent with but does not confirm a Porter-type mechanism. Investors nonetheless priced transition-regulatory exposure: ETS-covered firms earned significantly negative abnormal returns around both policy milestones. Thus, digitalization in China’s energy sector is already visible in what firms invent and disclose, with measurable emission and valuation effects likely to follow as disclosure mandates and carbon pricing mature.
items.authors: Anbao Tang, Zirui Wang

items.title: Governing Human Trafficking Across Borders: Layered Coordination and Functional but Fragile Regionalism in Central America’s Northern Triangle
items.abstract: Human trafficking is a cross-border governance challenge in which criminal justice, migration management, victim protection, and regional cooperation intersect. This article examines how formal anti-trafficking commitments are translated into operational coordination in Guatemala, El Salvador, and Honduras. Using a document-led comparative qualitative design, the study analyses 75 coded official and regional records, supplemented by three key-informant interviews and freedom-of-information evidence. The findings identify a layered architecture combining trinational agreements, regional platforms, bilateral channels, and domestic institutions. These arrangements support recurring coordination, shared standards, referral and repatriation routines, capacity building, and information-governance initiatives, but their durability and system-level traceability vary across countries. The article introduces functional but fragile regionalism as a conceptual contribution to explain how institutional density can sustain anti-trafficking cooperation without producing uniform consolidation. The comparison shows that the critical variation lies not in whether formal mechanisms exist, but in how deeply coordination is embedded in national mandates, personnel, resources, administrative routines, and information systems. The findings contribute to debates on human trafficking, transnational organized-crime governance, and cross-border institutional cooperation.
items.authors: Yasmín Stefani Franco Bermúdez, Carlos Alberto Echeverría Echeverría Mayorga

items.title: Positive Solutions of a Fractional BVP and the Reach of the Omitted Ray Fixed Point Theorem
items.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem D0+αu+f(t,u)=0 on (0,1), u(0)=0, D0+α−1u(1)=∫01udA, where 1 α≤2 and the measure dA may change sign. For a measure made of two point masses of opposite sign, we show that the function KA(s)=∫01G(τ,s)dA(τ), through which dA enters the Green function, is nonnegative exactly when the positive weight is at least θ* times the size of the negative one, where θ* is given in closed form. Together with a simple condition Δ 0, this makes the Green function nonnegative. The threshold θ* decreases in α and tends to infinity as α→1+. For α 2 the Green function has no uniform Harnack estimate, so we work in a cone weighted by Ψ(t)=∫01G(t,s)ds, where Schauder’s theorem gives a positive solution with explicit bounds whenever f lies between two positive constants. For the omitted ray fixed point theorem of Avery, Henderson and Liu, we describe exactly when its key inequality holds for the two-point functional used here, and we show that the hypotheses under which we can verify it already imply the classical inward condition. Examples with α=3/2 and α=1.08 illustrate the results.
items.authors: Mahammad Khuddush, Saleh S. Almuthaybiri

items.title: Pharmaceutical Residues in Human Urine from Patients Under Antiretroviral Regimens and Self-Reported Healthy Individuals Before and After Three Months’ Storage: Implication for Agricultural Reuse in Pretoria, South Africa
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pharmaceutical residues in human urine have raised serious concerns about the safe reuse of urine in agriculture. The current study investigates and compares the concentrations of pharmaceuticals in urine samples collected from male patients undergoing active antiretroviral regimens and self-reported “healthy individuals” at a government hospital in Pretoria, South Africa, and determines how the residues changed during three months of ambient storage, which is the usual recommendation before use in agriculture. Methods: The urine samples were collected in a plastic bottle to prevent fecal contamination, and 15 targeted compounds were analyzed using solid-phase extraction and liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry. The linearity ranged from 0.9910 to 0.9999, 75.5% to 99.1% for recovery, and intra-day and inter-day precision were below 6%. The urine from each group was collected into one pooled sample and then analyzed both pre- and post-storage. Results: Thirteen pharmaceuticals were detected in urine from patients on regular medication before storage; in “healthy individuals”, detections rose from eight to twelve after storage. Concentrations in the composite samples after storage were higher for some of the compounds but lower for others, including caffeine, nevirapine, prednisolone and 17α-ethinylestradiol. Metformin was highest overall at 1186.25 µg/L and remained at 806.68 µg/L after storage. The highest concentration for all the pharmaceuticals was reported for metformin, with a value of 1186.25 µg/L, occurring in the group of patients on a regular regimen. There could be a possibility that the rise can be attributed to the hydrolysis of conjugated metabolites during storage; however, no analysis of conjugates was carried out. Conclusions: This study shows the need for appropriate treatment of human urine prior to its reuse as fertilizer and echoes the importance of further research into human exposure pathways and effective pharmaceutical removal strategies.
items.authors: Mugivhisa Liziwe Lizbelt, Baloyi Khanyi Faith, Oluwaseun Mary Oladeji, Olatunde Stephen Olatunji, Joshua Oluwole Olowoyo

items.title: Flocculent Ti3AlC2-Based Two-Dimensional Material Flexible Microneedle Patch for Screening Alzheimer’s Disease Animal Biomarkers and In Situ Revealing Spatial Aggregation of Arachidonic Acid
items.abstract: Efficient diagnosis and pathological elucidation of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) are constrained by the lack of technologies for in situ capture of metabolites in living brain tissues. Metabolic disorders in the parietal lobe highly correlate with AD progression, yet existing methods cannot achieve in situ capture and spatial analysis. A petal-like flocculent Ti3AlC2-based flexible microneedle patch was developed for in situ extraction and mass spectrometry of parietal metabolites in AD rabbits. Sodium hydroxide etching and cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) self-assembly constructed a flocculent micro-/nanostructure, enhancing enrichment ~4-fold (2.5-fold after etching + 1.6-fold after CTAB). The stretchable substrate enables conformal attachment to the curved parietal lobe. Application to the exposed cortex demonstrates mechanical flexibility, linear glucose response (R2 = 0.9958) and resistance to salt/protein interference. Serum profiling of 15 AD patients and 15 controls with OPLS-DA shows clear discrimination (top-5 markers combined area under the curve (AUC) = 0.84). Spatial analysis reveals arachidonic acid’s unique pattern of centralized aggregation with peripheral gradient diffusion. This novel in situ device enables brain metabolite detection and reveals abnormal arachidonic acid aggregation, providing evidence for lipid-pathway AD interventions.
items.authors: Siyuan Chen, Bixiang Li, Tangjing Zhao, Qin Huang, Chengyu Li, Yilamujiang Ainiwan

items.title: Systematic Screening of Reference Genes for qPCR in Procambarus clarkii: RPL13a Shows Stable Expression Under Non-Ionic Ammonia Stress and Multiple Experimental Conditions
items.abstract: Real-time quantitative PCR (qPCR) is a key technique for elucidating the mechanisms underlying environmental stress responses in aquatic animals, and its accuracy relies heavily on stable reference genes for data normalization. In this study, histopathological examination revealed alterations in the gill, hepatopancreas, and muscle tissues of Procambarus clarkii following NH3 stress. Based on transcriptomic screening and reference genes reported in the literature, 13 candidate reference genes were selected. Their expression levels in 8 different tissues before and after NH3 stress were detected using qPCR, and their stability was systematically evaluated using multiple algorithms, including geNorm, NormFinder, BestKeeper, Delta CT and RefFinder. The results identified 60S ribosomal protein L13a (RPL13a), ribosomal protein S18 (RPS18) and eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4A (EIF4A) as the three most stable candidates under NH3 stress, whereas the traditionally used reference genes beta-actin (β-actin) and glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) showed relatively low stability under these conditions. geNorm pairwise variation analysis indicated that the inclusion of a third reference gene could further improve normalization. Validation using four NH3-responsive genes showed that (RPL13a + RPS18) and (RPL13a + RPS18 + EIF4A) yielded similar log2 fold-change estimates, supporting their use as normalization options under the tested conditions. It is worth noting that RPL13a remains highly stable across four conditions: different embryonic developmental stages, different ovarian developmental stages, tissues from both males and females, and following infection with white spot syndrome virus (WSSV). These findings contribute to the selecting and validating reference genes for qPCR analyses in Procambarus clarkii under the specific experimental conditions evaluated in this study.
items.authors: Xiudan Yuan, Xing Tian, Yuanyuan Liu, Zhigang He, Jinlong Li, Yunpeng Fan

items.title: Hydration-Controlled Charge Transport in Polymer Networks and Hydrogels
items.abstract: Water in soft electrochemical materials is far more than a passive solvent—it directly governs ionic transport, dielectric response, and structural stability. Unlocking the full potential of hydrogel electrolytes requires mastering the delicate interplay between polymer networks, confined water dynamics, and mobile ions. Classical models like Maxwell–Garnett fall short in capturing these complex interfaces; percolation-based frameworks like General Effective Medium (GEM) theory can describe transport transitions, though their parameters remain system-dependent. This review bridges molecular-level hydration phenomena, including non-freezing bound water, organohydrogel hybridization, and thermoresponsive phase behavior, with macroscopic performance metrics across bioelectronics, energy storage, and electronic skin. By integrating percolation physics, molecular design, and quantitative cross-system comparisons across material systems, we provide a roadmap to engineer resilient, high-performance soft electroactive architectures for next-generation technologies.
items.authors: Karina Mihilewicz, Katarzyna Bialik-Wąs, Konstantinos N. Raftopoulos

items.title: The Platelet–Adipose Tissue Axis in Metabolic Disease: From Platelet Reprogramming to Tissue Remodeling
items.abstract: Obesity-induced adipose tissue remodeling results from the interplay of metabolic stress, chronic inflammation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and vascular dysfunction. Beyond their established role in thrombosis, platelets have emerged as immunometabolic effectors at the interface between vascular and metabolic responses. This review examines mechanistic, translational, and clinical evidence supporting a platelet–adipose tissue axis and its relevance to obesity-associated cardiometabolic disease. In obesity and related metabolic disorders, platelets display a hyperreactive phenotype characterized by alterations in glycolysis, mitochondrial function, oxidative stress, and secretory activity, together with changes in extracellular vesicle biogenesis and cargo. Through direct cellular interactions and soluble or vesicle-mediated signaling, platelets may influence leukocyte recruitment, macrophage phenotype, fibroblast activation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and endothelial or adipocyte metabolic pathways relevant to adipose tissue dysfunction. However, the extent of direct platelet-dependent effects within adipose tissue is poorly known. We propose that these mechanisms may participate in a feed-forward thromboinflammatory circuit in which metabolic stress promotes platelet reprogramming, while platelet-derived signals may in turn amplify endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, fibrosis, and impaired adipose tissue plasticity. Although direct causal evidence in humans remains limited, current data support a biologically coherent framework in which platelets may act as amplifiers of adipose tissue dysfunction rather than established primary drivers. Overall, this platelet–adipose tissue axis may provide a framework for investigating novel molecular pathways relevant to cardiometabolic risk stratification and therapeutic strategies.
items.authors: Rosa Simone, Cosimo Damiano Perrone, Valentina Lemmo, Chiara Lonobile, Silvia Stella Barbieri

items.title: Effects of Irrigation Regimes on Crop Growth and Yield of Chile Peppers Under Sprinkler Irrigation in the Semiarid Climate
items.abstract: Irrigation management is essential for successfully cultivating Chile peppers (Capsicum spp.), as it influences plant yield, fruit quality, and susceptibility to soil-borne diseases. This study investigates the effects of various sprinkler irrigation regimes on different Chile pepper varieties to optimize water use efficiency and enhance overall production. The varieties included in the study are ‘TAM Mild Jalapeno’, ‘Anaheim’, ‘Sandia’, ‘NM#6’, ‘California Wonder’, and ‘Red Knight’. Field experiments were conducted at the Agricultural Science Center in Farmington during the 2024 and 2025 growing seasons. A split-plot design with three replicates was employed to assess the effects of varying irrigation levels (100%, 80%, and 60% ET), which corresponded to 0%, 20%, and 40% water savings, respectively. Each plot comprised three rows of 10 plants, with 0.762 m between rows and 0.305 m between plants. In both 2024 and 2025, the amounts of applied irrigation and total water supplied varied across the irrigation treatments, with greater depths under the 100% ET regime and progressively lower amounts at 80% ET and 60% ET. Irrigation Water Use Efficiency (IWUE) values varied from 4.06 kg m−3 in ‘NM#6’ to 9.57 kg m−3 in ‘TAM Mild Jalapeno’ in 2024. In 2025, IWUE values ranged from 4.62 kg m−3 in ‘California Wonder’ to 8.76 kg m−3 in ‘TAM Mild Jalapeno’. On average, ‘TAM Mild Jalapeno’ consistently had the highest IWUE across both years, while ‘NM#6’ had the lowest. Evapotranspiration Water Use Efficiency (ETWUE) values ranged from 5.41 kg m−3 in ‘NM#6’ to 12.13 kg m−3 in ‘TAM Mild Jalapeno’ in 2024. In 2025, ETWUE values ranged from 6.99 kg m−3 in ‘California Wonder’ to 12.82 kg m−3 in ‘TAM Mild Jalapeno’. On average, ‘TAM Mild Jalapeno’ consistently had the highest ETWUE across both years, while ‘NM#6’ had the lowest. Results indicated that both ‘TAM Mild Jalapeno’ and ‘California Wonder’ achieved the highest marketable yields in 2024, while ‘TAM Mild Jalapeno’ and ‘Red Knight’ had the greatest marketable yields in 2025. Moderate deficit irrigation (20% water savings) maintained or improved marketable yield and water use efficiency. In contrast, a 40% water savings strategy led to significant reductions in both yield and plant growth. ‘TAM Mild Jalapeno’ exhibited the greatest adaptability to water-limited conditions, consistently achieving the highest irrigation and evapotranspiration water use efficiency. Conversely, ‘California Wonder’ was more sensitive to severe water deficits.
items.authors: Yusuf O. Anifowoshe, Dennis Lozada, Soumaila Sanogo, Koffi Djaman

items.title: Toward a National Tuberculosis Lateral-Flow Urine Lipoarabinomannan (LF-LAM) External Quality Assessment Program in Thailand: Feasibility Demonstration Through Panel Development, Validation, and Proficiency Testing, March 2025–April 2026
items.abstract: Background: The World Health Organization and the Thailand National HIV Treatment Guidelines recommend the use of lateral flow urine lipoarabinomannan (LF-LAM) testing for tuberculosis (TB) detection in people living with HIV (PLHIV) with advanced HIV disease who have signs and symptoms of TB or are seriously ill. As Thailand decentralizes LF-LAM testing, a robust quality assurance system is needed to maintain diagnostic accuracy across healthcare levels. Methods: We developed, validated, and rolled out Thailand’s first national external quality assessment (EQA) and internal quality control (IQC) framework for urinary TB LF-LAM testing. Pre-characterized urine panels were distributed to 20 provinces spanning 12 health regions nationwide across four cycles from 2025 to 2026. Longitudinal monitoring of reporting compliance, pass rates, and failure modes was performed across 30 participating sites in 2025 and 64 and 42 sites in 2026 Rounds 1 and 2, respectively. Results: IQC coverage increased from 7 to 68 facilities by the final cycle in January 2026, with satisfaction rates of 85.7–100%. EQA pass rates showed a stepwise improvement: 83.3% in Round 1/2025, 93.1% in Round 2/2025 and 97.5% and 98.4% in the 2026 rounds (p 0.05). Initial failures were primarily due to false-positive interpretation of Grade 1 bands and deviation in the reading window. Targeted retraining and standardized reference match-cards reduced user-dependent false-positive results to 0% in the final cycle. Conclusions: A centralized national quality assurance framework may be an effective mechanism for standardizing the reliability and interpretation of point-of-care LF-LAM testing across decentralized healthcare systems. This approach strengthens diagnostic capacity at peripheral facilities and supports the safe expansion of TB services for PLHIV.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Decision Support Systems: Contributions, Emerging Patterns, and Future Directions
