items.title: Narrating the Self After Communism: Memory and Identity in Contemporary Romanian Fiction
items.abstract: The present study seeks to provide a coherent and critically valid perspective on contemporary Romanian prose, which, through its thematic focus—namely the exploration of human destinies drawn into the maelstrom of history—as well as its meaningful narrative structures, guides the reader toward multiple interpretations. Contemporary Romanian writing repeatedly returns to the individual and collective consequences of the communist experience, yet the narrative relationship with this past differs according to the writers’ temporal and experiential position towards it. In numerous Romanian post-revolutionary texts, we can discern an art of reminiscence that could be described as a mimesis of remembrance, in which memory, retrospection, and introspection become narrative means of negotiating the relationship between personal experience and historical memory. Through a comparative reading of texts belonging to different generations and genres, the study examines two interconnected modes of narrating the communist past.In the works of Dan Lungu, Lavinia Braniște, and Alina Nelega, the communist past is approached retrospectively, through narratives that recover and reconstruct its social realities, mentalities, and individual consequences from a post-totalitarian perspective. By contrast, in the works of exiled writers such as Norman Manea, Virgil Tănase, Dumitru Țepeneag, and Matei Călinescu, the relationship with the communist past is grounded more directly in lived experience, autobiographical memory, exile, and the attempt to reclaim or reconfigure personal identity. By bringing these two modes of writing the past into dialogue, the study argues that contemporary Romanian prose moves between the recoveryand narrative reconfigurationof lived memory and the retrospective reconstruction of a past that must increasingly be accessed through testimony, research, mediated images, and retrospective interpretation.
items.authors: Iuliana Petronela Barna

items.title: Groundwater Recovery and Land Deformation in the Beijing Plain: A Review
items.abstract: Groundwater recovery can reduce land subsidence without immediately reversing aquifer-system compaction. This review synthesizes 101 original studies of the Beijing Plain to examine deformation during groundwater depletion and subsequent recovery. The evidence includes interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR), leveling, groundwater records, borehole deformation measurements and laboratory experiments. Historical surveys and satellite observations document expanding subsidence centers followed by widespread deceleration and localized rebound. Groundwater pressure changes are the principal regional forcing. Sedimentary architecture, hydraulic connectivity and loading history govern the magnitude and timing of deformation. Delayed pressure equilibration and time-dependent strain can sustain compaction after aquifer heads rise, while irreversible strain limits recovery of lost elevation. Surface uplift can therefore coexist with compaction at depth and does not establish restoration of aquifer-system storage capacity. Observational coverage remains uneven: 75 studies use InSAR, whereas 17 report borehole deformation measurements. Paired pressure and interval-deformation measurements are needed to identify the sources of continuing compaction. Differential ground movement remains relevant to infrastructure assessment even where regional subsidence slows.
items.authors: Zeping Wang, Honglei Yang, Pan Wang, Jiawang Wang, Tiantian Wang

items.title: Identification of Quasi-Solid Bound Water in High-Liquid-Limit Soils Based on Water Density Evolution
items.abstract: High-liquid-limit soils may exhibit relatively low compressibility despite their high water contents and void ratios, suggesting that conventional descriptors alone may not fully capture the effects of soil–water interactions on their engineering behavior. This study proposes the concept of quasi-solid bound water (QSBW) and develops a density-evolution-based method to identify it. Seven soils with different liquid limits were investigated using helium pycnometry, one-dimensional consolidation tests, falling-head permeability tests, and bound-water characterization by NMR, thermogravimetric analysis, and the volumetric flask method. Water with a density exceeding that of free water (0.997 g/cm3) was operationally identified as QSBW and treated as an equivalent solid to define an effective void ratio. The measured QSBW contents ranged from 12.1% to 28.1% by dry soil mass, with an average density of approximately 1.25 g/cm3. At the same conventional void ratio, soils exhibited substantially different compressibility and hydraulic conductivity, which generally decreased with increasing QSBW content. When compared at the same effective void ratio, their consolidation curves and hydraulic conductivities showed marked convergence. The novelty lies in linking water density evolution with an effective-void-ratio framework for interpreting the compression and seepage behavior of high-liquid-limit soils.
items.authors: Xiwang Wang, Yupeng Xiao, Lu Li, Rui Zhang, Zhengnan Liu

items.title: FedCuraLM: Reliability-Calibrated and Resource-Aware Label Auditing with Small Language Models for Non-IID Federated AIoT
items.abstract: Federated Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) activity-recognition systems learn from decentralized wearable and smart-home records with potentially incorrect labels, non-IID client distributions, and unequal edge-device resources.Our objective is to improve downstream learning from these labels while limiting harmful corrections and respecting auditing, review, and communication budgets.FedCuraLM addresses this objective by converting sensor records into deterministic Semantic Evidence Cards, obtaining candidate-constrained small language model (SLM) assessments, and calibrating and combining them with task-model, prototype, and temporal evidence. Conflict-aware decisions retain observed labels, apply provisional soft corrections, request trusted review, or quarantine uncertain samples without overwriting annotations. Review-grounded reliability and communication-budgeted multi-prototype exchange support collaboration, while resource-aware scheduling assigns feasible SLM tiers across heterogeneous devices. Extensive evaluation on WISDM-W, WISDM-P, and CASAS using controlled symmetric, semantic-asymmetric, instance-dependent, and temporal-boundary corruption under varying client heterogeneity reveals that FedCuraLM significantly improves downstream performance over recent baselines and improves lower-tail client outcomes, audit precision, selective-correction safety, calibration, and communication efficiency. Edge-device measurements characterize latency, memory, and energy trade-offs. The findings position federated label curation as a semantic, statistical, communication, and systems problem.
items.authors: Md Tahmid Rashid, Md Saikat Ahmed, Nafiz Imtiaz

items.title: Smart Identification Method for B-Axis and Tool-Nose Center Misalignment in Ultra-Precision Lathe Using Servo-Based Contact Detection
items.abstract: In recent years, B-axis rotary motion has often been utilized in ultra-precision turning operations, where it is essential to align the tool-nose center precisely with the center of the B-axis rotation and compensate for the residual misalignment that usually remains. Conventionally, this alignment relies on time-consuming, low-accuracy manual operations, resulting in the need for compensation machining after measurement and a reduction in both machining accuracy and overall efficiency. To overcome this issue, this study proposes a smart B-axis and tool-nose center misalignment identification method using servo-based tool–workpiece contact detection. In this paper, the thrust command signal of the Z-axis linear servo motor is used as the servo signal. By using this method, an external-sensorless, automatic, and high-precision alignment is expected to be realized. This paper presents the concept of the developed B-axis and tool-nose center misalignment identification method, and experiments are conducted to evaluate its effectiveness. The results show that the tool–workpiece contact position is identified with a repeatability of about 0.05 µm, and that the B-axis and tool-nose center misalignment identified by the proposed method is reduced from 6.2 µm to 0.34 µm by a single compensation.
items.authors: Ryota Taniguchi, Kyungki Lee, Seiichi Uto, Takehiro Hayasaka, Yuta Iwasaki, Ryosuke Imura
items.category_raw: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing

items.title: Factors Associated with Medical and Health Talent Agglomeration at the City Level in China: Economic, Social, and Ecological Perspectives
items.abstract: Background: Medical and health talent (MHT) is a core strategic resource for safeguarding public health. Understanding the factors associated with MHT agglomeration is essential for improving healthcare workforce planning and optimizing the allocation of health resources. Methods: Using panel data from 285 prefecture-level cities in China spanning 2004–2019, this study extended the previously established multidimensional framework for analyzing MHT agglomeration encompassing density, scale, intensity, and equilibrium to a longitudinal urban setting. Spatial autocorrelation analysis and a two-way fixed effects panel model were used to examine economic, social, and ecological factors associated with MHT agglomeration. Robustness tests, endogeneity checks, and heterogeneity analysis were also conducted. Results: The spatial autocorrelation analysis reveals that the spatial distribution of MHT exhibits a generally random and dispersed pattern. Urban hospital beds per 1000 population maintained a significant positive association across all model specifications, representing the most robust factor associated with talent agglomeration. Sci-tech expenditure exhibited nonlinear association, while ecological factors displayed pronounced dimensional heterogeneity and regional differentiation. Conclusions: MHT agglomeration is associated with factors across multiple dimensions, with hospital bed capacity showing a particularly consistent association.
items.authors: Lei Zhang, Lingmin Shao, Cheng Hu, Dayong Zhang

items.title: What Epidemiological Studies Tell Us About Depression Among Black Populations?
items.abstract: Depression among Black patients is shaped by the interaction of clinical symptoms, cultural meanings, social conditions, and experiences of care. This narrative review examines evidence among African American and other Black populations, including Black–White comparisons and within-Black differences, on symptom presentation, measurement, persistence, disability, comorbidity, and social and cultural correlates, across the United States and selected Canadian, European, and African settings. Targeted searches identified population surveys, clinical studies, psychometric investigations, qualitative research, intervention trials, and relevant reviews. James S. Jackson's research agenda provides a starting point: understanding comparatively favorable findings in the context of historical and continuing adversity. Several United States surveys report lower lifetime prevalence of interview-defined major depression among Black than White adults, while symptom scales often indicate greater depressive burden among Black adults. This Black–White mental health paradox varies by outcome and population; some studies identify greater persistence and disability among Black adults with depression. Studies of hope, positive affect, coping resources, and physical health suggest that the correlates of depression may also differ across groups, although no single mechanism explains the pattern. Evidence on distinctive symptom presentation is mixed. Some studies identify Black–White differences or within-Black variation in bodily symptoms, self-criticism, or interpersonal experiences, whereas others find substantial similarity after accounting for severity and social or medical conditions. Psychiatric and physical comorbidity among Black adults with depression varies across samples, including in comparisons with White adults. Associations of depressive symptoms or MDD with smoking, disease self-management, self-rated health, inflammation, and mortality differ across studies and populations; colorism, trauma, sexuality, gender, and migration further identify within-Black heterogeneity. The review examines associations of discrimination, financial strain, employment conditions, family relationships, and gendered expectations with depressive symptoms, MDD, and treatment use among Black populations. Studies of Black populations also examine political representation and insurance expansion in relation to self-reported mental health, and loneliness, personality, and distinct church-based relationships in relation to depressive symptoms or MDD. Social support, religious involvement, mastery, and socioeconomic resources are associated with depressive symptoms or MDD in several studies, with variation across measures, social positions, and national settings. Studies also identify disparities in medication initiation and selection, communication, continuity, and care quality; stigma, discrimination in care, and medical debt are relevant to treatment access and experience. Cultural assessment and accessible, sustained depression care may improve recognition and engagement. Future research should distinguish symptom burden from diagnosed disorder, assess longitudinal course directly, and avoid treating Black identity as a single cultural or biological category.
items.authors: Shervin Assari
items.title_zh: 黑人群体抑郁症的流行病学研究概述
items.summary_zh: 黑人患者的抑郁症受临床症状、文化意义、社会条件和护理经历的交互影响。本文综述了非裔美国人及其他黑人群体的相关证据，包括黑人与白人之间的比较及黑人内部差异，涉及症状表现、测量、持续性、残疾、共病及社会文化相关因素，研究范围涵盖美国及部分加拿大、欧洲和非洲地区。通过针对性检索，识别了人口调查、临床研究、心理测量研究、定性研究、干预试验及相关综述。一些美国调查显示，黑人成年人自我报告的重度抑郁症终生患病率低于白人，但症状量表常指示黑人成年人抑郁负担更重。这种黑人与白人心理健康悖论因结果和人群而异，部分研究发现黑人成年人抑郁症的持续性和残疾程度更高。希望、积极情感、应对资源和身体健康的研究表明，抑郁症的相关因素在不同群体间可能存在差异。

items.title: Best Administrative/IT Practices When Rolling Out Custom Agents
items.abstract: Educational institutions recognizing the widespread value of artificial intelligence agents may desire to adopt the emerging technologies within their own organizations. However, the deployment of custom agents involves risks for the institutions in the form of prompt injection attacks, hallucinations, embarrassing responses, data leaks, RAG poisoning, and more. Accountability structures, proper identity and access management, and legal compliance standards (FERPA, AI Disclosure Laws, and ADA accessibility) must be maintained on an administrative level to ensure the institution can safely and efficiently deploy agentic technology. When it comes to the initial deployment of the agent, technical teams should implement guardrails, RAG databases, and rate limiting to protect against many of the associated agentic-specific risks, excluding traditional software risks. Finally, subject matter experts can review existing metrics and agent traces to adjust RAG database documents, token limits, tools, and more to ensure optimal agentic output.
items.authors: Anurag Mathews, Coco Shen, Edward Zeng, Asad Malik

items.title: MiND: Minimal Deterministic Middleware for Auditable Large Language Model Interactions
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded in research software, yet many integrations preserve only the visible prompt and answer while losing structured evidence about configuration, provider metadata, timing, failures, and the exact request procedure. MiND is an open-source, provider-neutral middleware that places a small audit boundary between an application and an LLM. For each attempted interaction it normalizes the input, constructs an explicit request, invokes a provider adapter, normalizes the result, and stores a versioned Cycle Artifact containing the observable execution context. The same core is available through a Python API, command-line interface, local HTTP API, and a self-contained Windows interface. MiND is deliberately non-agentic: it does not infer human intention, expose hidden model reasoning, or claim deterministic repetition of stochastic model output. Its purpose is narrower—to make the surrounding execution procedure inspectable and reusable.
items.authors: Edervaldo José de Souza Melo

items.title: The Local Path to Preserving 30% of the Land by 2030: The Case of Vermont
items.abstract: Ten US states and dozens of countries have adopted a goal to preserve 30 percent of their land and water resources by 2030. The US 30 × 30 effort seeks to protect wildlife habitats, provide recreation opportunities, mitigate climate change, and avoid the fragmentation of natural areas and working farms and forestlands. Yet, very little research exists on the practice of how to achieve 30x30. In 2023, the State of Vermont passed legislation setting 30x30 and 50x50 as goals. Because Vermont is heavily forested, the preservation of forestland is key to reaching its goals. Fragmentation and parcelization of forests both degrade the forest ecology and reduce the attractiveness for preservation. Land preservation and retention decisions about private property occur locally, but no studies have yet examined the locally available land use tools that influence achieving the 30% goal. This study fills that gap by analyzing the interaction among land preservation, local zoning, state sponsored pref-erential property taxation, and land parcelization activity in 13 forested Vermont towns. Findings show considerable benefit from preferential property taxation, limited benefit from natural resource zoning, and a wide variation in the amount of land preserved. We also found little change in the number of large parcels pre- and post-COVID but some continued land fragmentation among smaller parcels. Sustained funding for land preservation together with the management of forests will be essential steps toward effective preservation in any forested region over the long run.
items.authors: Thomas L. Daniels, Amy Lynch

items.title: Single Species and Variable Environments but Different Fish? A Case Study of the Gray Rockfish em Sebastes glaucus /em (Sebastidae, Scorpaeniformes) in the Northern Sea of Okhotsk
items.abstract: The speciﬁc habitat conditions in different parts of the species’ range may give rise to intraspeciﬁc polymorphism at various levels (morphological, biological, genetic, etc.), but this phenomenon has not been sufficiently studied. The results of research of the morphological, biological, genetic, karyological, and parasitological characteristics of the gray rockﬁsh Sebastes glaucus (Sebastidae, Scorpaeniformes) in two water bodies differing in habitat conditions are presented, i.e. a desalinated lagoon and adjacent sea areas off the Zavyalov Island (the northern Sea of Okhotsk). It was found that individuals in both water bodies differ signiﬁcantly in terms of some morphological characters (the number of the lateral line pores and the total number of vertebrae), size (the ﬁsh in the lagoon has smaller length and body weight), maximum age and growth rates (individuals in the sea reach a greater age and grow faster), chromosome morphology and the number of chromosome arms, and the degree of infection with metacercariae of trematodes (100% in the lagoon and their complete absence in the sea). Furthermore, samples from the lagoon and the sea are reliably differentiated from each other based on genetic analysis using mtDNA markers. The identiﬁed differences may be due to a combination of factors, including both abiotic (lower temperature and salinity in the lagoon and its isolation from the sea) and biotic (limited forage resources and high parasite load in the isolated lagoon) factors.
items.authors: Olga A. Radchenko, Mikhail V. Nazarkin, Irina N. Moreva, Alexander V. Shestakov, Vitaly V. Pospekhov, Anna V. Petrovskaya

items.title: Conjunctive Windows and Fast Recovery in Venus Flytrap Trap Closure
items.abstract: Venus flytrap (Dionaea muscipula) trap closure is a discrete, energetically costly commitment that requires two action potentials (APs) within a memory window. A threshold-product model, R = Φ·(A·D·C) ≥ θ, was previously applied to this system (Rahman, 2026a) and then frozen with parameters in an unpublished pre-registration, including a slow inactivation gate (recovery constant τ_φ0 = 8 s) that vetoes a second AP arriving within 4.6 s of the first. Here the frozen model is tested against trial-level data from Burri et al. (2020) and against values reported in more than a dozen further studies. In the raw voltage traces of closing events, the two APs were separated by 0.98 s (single slow deflection) and approximately 0.75–1.1 s (double deflection), and both traps closed. This bounds τ_φ0 at 1.7 s or less and falsifies the frozen veto boundary. In 31 matched fail/succeed pairs of single deflections, the AP threshold in angular-displacement × angular-velocity space was a bounded window: a model with a velocity window ranked 29 of 31 pairs correctly under leave-one-out, against 22 for a power-law product and 9 for an additive rule. All six traps that failed at fast velocity (1.4–6.5 rad/s) fired when velocity was halved at equal or larger displacement, which no rule monotone in both factors permits. Across studies, the calcium memory constant converged (30–40 s), while reported two-touch windows ranged from 16 to 50 s. Digitized temperature data (Molis et al., 2006) fit a single calcium memory with τ = 32 s at 20 °C and Q10 = 1.64, and show that the memory is partly local to the touched hair. Counts of stimuli to closure at intervals up to 20 min (Brown, 1916) require a second, slow component with a time constant of hours. A revised model, frozen before independent calcium-imaging data (Suda et al., 2020) were examined, predicted a two-stimulus closure window of 13.5 s; the measured 50% closure duration was 30.9 s (95% CI 21.4–45.4 s), which locates the failure in a closure threshold imported from another preparation. Two independent trigger-hair transcriptomes over-express CYP710A1, which converts sitosterol to stigmasterol, so any sterol-dependent gate is more likely in the sensor than across the trap. Because stigmasterol also activates the H⁺-ATPase, such a gate would act on drive as well as on Φ. A flat-lobed mutant (DYSCALCULIA) shows that a deficit in A can be offset by more APs, but it cannot separate a product from a sum. The data support conjunctive gating with vetoes at both edges of the stimulus window and a fast baseline recovery gate. The multiplicative A·D·C product and a sterol-dependent Φ remain untested; six experiments are specified with kill conditions and sample sizes, including a factorial with independent measurement of drive and sterol analysis of the trigger hair.
items.authors: Tahir Rahman

items.title: Treatment Outcomes of Short Versus Standard Regimens in Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis: A Retrospective Cohort Study
items.abstract: Background: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) remains a major public health challenge in resource-constrained settings. This study compared treatment outcomes between shorter and longer/conventional MDR-TB regimens in the rural Eastern Cape, South Africa. Methods: This retrospective cohort study analyzed records of 233 patients treated for MDR-TB between January 2020 and December 2024 in O.R. Tambo District Municipality. Treatment success was defined as cure or treatment completion. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the association between regimen and treatment success, adjusting for age, sex, HIV status, and previous TB treatment. Results: The mean age was 37.9 ± 14.1 years, and 60.1% were male. Most patients received a shorter regimen (89.7%), while 10.3% received a longer/conventional regimen. Overall, 45.1% were cured and 21.0% completed treatment, yielding a 66.1% treatment success rate. Treatment success was higher with shorter than longer/conventional regimens (69.4% vs. 37.5%; p = 0.003). In multivariable analysis (n = 224), the longer/conventional regimen was associated with lower odds of treatment success (aOR 0.26, 95% CI 0.10–0.66; p = 0.005). Increasing age was also associated with lower odds of success (aOR 0.96 per year, 95% CI 0.94–0.98; p lt; 0.001). Adverse-event data were substantially incomplete. Conclusions: Shorter regimens were associated with higher treatment success; however, non-randomized treatment allocation, regimen-group imbalance, residual confounding, and incomplete routine data preclude causal interpretation. Prospective studies and strengthened clinical data systems are needed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of regimens in rural settings.
items.authors: Luvo Ntombana, Lindiwe Modest Faye, Ntandazo Dlatu, Mojisola Clara Hosu
items.title_zh: 短程与标准方案在多药耐药结核病治疗中的效果比较
items.summary_zh: 背景：多药耐药结核病（MDR-TB）在资源有限的地区仍然是重大公共卫生挑战。本研究比较了南非东开普省农村地区短程与长程MDR-TB治疗方案的效果。方法：本回顾性队列研究分析了2020年1月至2024年12月期间在O.R.坦博区治疗的233名MDR-TB患者的记录。治疗成功定义为治愈或完成治疗。多变量逻辑回归评估了方案与治疗成功之间的关联，调整了年龄、性别、HIV状态和既往结核治疗。结果：平均年龄为37.9 ± 14.1岁，男性占60.1%。大多数患者接受了短程方案（89.7%），而10.3%接受了长程方案。总体治愈率为45.1%，完成治疗率为21.0%，治疗成功率为66.1%。短程方案的治疗成功率高于长程方案（69.4% vs. 37.5%；p = 0.003）。在多变量分析中，长程方案与较低的治疗成功几率相关（aOR 0.26, 95% CI 0.10–0.66；p = 0.005）。年龄增加也与成功几率降低相关（aOR 0.96每年，95% CI 0.94–0.98；p < 0.001）。不良事件数据严重不完整。结论：短程方案与更高的治疗成功率相关。

items.title: Evaluation of Short- and Long-Term Outcomes of Patients with Carotid Artery Stenting: 16-Year Experience at a Single Center
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Carotid artery stenting (CAS) is a preventive treatment for symptomatic moderate-to-severe and asymptomatic severe carotid stenosis. This study evaluated short- and long-term complications and outcomes of CAS. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 584 patients who underwent CAS at our Neurology Clinic between January 2004 and December 2020. Results: Of 584 patients, 271 (46.6%) were symptomatic and 311 (53.4%) asymptomatic. At 30 days, myocardial infarction (MI) occurred in 2.2%, major stroke in 2.4%, major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) in 4.1%, and vascular death in 1.4%. Mean Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) was higher in patients with 30-day MACCE (p=0.014) and vascular death (p=0.003). Atrial fibrillation (AF) independently predicted 30-day MACCE (OR 3.57, 95% CI 1.17-10.89) and vascular death (OR 10.17, 95% CI 2.18-47.42); CCI independently predicted MACCE at 5 and 10 years. Diabetes mellitus (69.7%) was not independently associated with MACCE, restenosis, or mortality after adjusting for CCI. Smoking, rather than sex, independently predicted 5-year restenosis (OR 4.61, 95% CI 1.80-11.79); the higher crude restenosis rate in men appears attributable to smoking prevalence. Actuarial analysis showed 10-year overall survival of 81.0%, MACCE-free survival of 75.3%, and restenosis-free survival of 73.4%. Conclusions: CAS is generally safe, but close follow-up is necessary to monitor complications, and careful preoperative risk assessment is essential. CCI and AF status should be considered alongside stroke history, carotid anatomy, and smoking status for perioperative risk assessment.
items.authors: Tuğba Erdoğan, Bijen Nazlıel, Hale Zeynep Batur Çağlayan, Taylan Altıparmak, Ahmet Baran Önal, Mehmet Koray Akkan

items.title: Stress Distribution in Short Zirconia and Titanium Dental Implants: A Finite Element Study
items.abstract: Treatment with short implants is considered as predictable as conventional implants. Objective: This in silico experimental study aimed to determine the stress distribution in short zirconia dental implants using finite element analysis (FEA). Methods: Thirty-six implant-crown designs were modeled in ANSYS 2019 R2. Loading conditions included an oblique force of 150 N (30°, ISO 14801:2016), vertical forces of 300 N and 400 N, and a 32 Ncm screw tightening torque across Type I and Type III bone models using three implant diameters (4.1, 4.8, and 5.0 mm). Results: Under both oblique and vertical loads, zirconia generated lower bone deformation but higher overall stress concentrations than titanium. When stratified by bone density, zirconia concentrated higher peri-implant stress in low-density (Type III) bone. Discussion: In both loading scenarios, a progressive increase in implant diameter successfully and proportionally mitigated stress concentrations, which aligns with established biomechanical literature on titanium systems while matching findings from recent comparative studies showing elevated stress levels in zirconia structures. Conclusion: Stress concentrations are higher in zirconia than titanium, particularly in low-density bone; however, this biomechanical limitation can be effectively compensated for by increasing the implant diameter.
items.authors: Catherine Tamayo, Carlos Cutuli, Eduardo Cepeda

items.title: Transfer Optimization in Professional Football: A Total Cost of Ownership Decision Framework Adapted from Industrial Procurement
items.abstract: Despite record revenues across European professional football, many clubs consistently report negative annual results. Player transfers represent the single largest controllable cost driver, yet investment decisions are rarely evaluated through a rigorous economic lens: the headline transfer fee dominates deliberation while salary obligations, injury exposure, and player-attributable revenue contributions receive little systematic attention. This paper proposes a holistic investment decision framework for professional football by adapting the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) concept from industrial procurement. The framework treats players as capital assets and integrates further financially relevant dimensions into a net economic metric assessed over the contract period and discounted to present value. We illustrate the framework using the 2025 transfer of Florian Wirtz from Bayer Leverkusen to Liverpool FC (initial fee approximately EUR 118 million, £100 million), which also draws on age-based market value forecasting and probabilistic injury risk assessment among its inputs. The analysis highlights economic dimensions beyond market-price-based evaluation. By applying the framework, total costs in the base case are approximately 1.6 times the headline fee in present-value terms, and the illustrative scenario range spans approximately EUR 80 million. Statistical and machine learning market value models can inform specific framework inputs rather than functioning as alternative valuation approaches. The approach is designed as a decision-support tool especially for the interface between sporting directors and CFOs, enabling transfer candidates to be evaluated on a comparable economic basis.
items.authors: Jörg H. Grimm, Jörn Justiz, Nicola Rüegg

items.title: Autologous Platelet-Rich Plasma for Endometrial and Ovarian Dysfunction: Mechanistic Insights and Clinical Outcomes
items.abstract: Although assisted reproductive technology (ART) has been widely applied worldwide, thin endometrium (TE), diminished ovarian reserve (DOR), and other conditions remain the core bottlenecks of refractory infertility, and existing therapies fail to effectively preserve tissue and prevent functional damage. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP), as an autologous regenerative agent, has demonstrated promising application potential in reproductive medicine due to its multi-targeted regulatory capacity. Therefore, this review is intended as a narrative overview that aims to systematically elucidate the possible mechanisms by which PRP improves the endometrial microenvironment and ovarian function, integrate the latest clinical evidence to evaluate its therapeutic efficacy, analyze translational challenges such as the lack of standardization, and provide an evidence-based basis for its standardized clinical application.
items.authors: Xiaofang Qin, Ting Yang, Lu Bai, Yuanyuan Xin, Xiaohui Liu, Haofei Shen

items.title: The Clinical Spectrum and Significance of ABCC8 Gene Variants in the Diagnosis of Monogenic Diabetes
items.abstract: Background: ABCC8 gene variants have been linked to a range of conditions that affect insulin secretion, such as congenital hyperinsulinism, neonatal diabetes and maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY). This study aimed to characterise ABCC8 variants and to assess their relationship with clinical phenotypes and family segregation. Methods: Between 2017 and May 2026, tNGS (targeted next-generation sequencing) analysis was performed on the DNA of 1202 patients who were referred for suspected monogenic diabetes. The exons and flanking intronic regions of the ABCC8 gene were assessed for single nucleotide variants (SNVs) and small insertions and deletions (indels). Rare variants were prioritised based on population frequency, in silico predictions and clinical classification. Selected variants were confirmed, and segregation analysis was performed using Sanger sequencing. Results: We identified five patients carrying pathogenic or likely pathogenic ABCC8 variants. A frameshift ABCC8 variant had not been previously reported. All patients had diabetes, with some also presenting with a history of hypoglycaemia. Family studies also revealed intra-familial variability and enabled the identification of previously unrecognized affected relatives. Conclusions: Our findings support the broad clinical spectrum associated with ABCC8 variants and highlight the importance of family segregation analysis. Comprehensive molecular and clinical evaluation may improve the detection of patients with ABCC8-related diabetes and distinguish this condition from other forms of monogenic diabetes.
items.authors: Natalia Kapelan, Piotr Tust, Sebastian Skoczylas, Tomasz Płoszaj, Karolina Gadzalska, Monika Gorządek
items.title_zh: ABCC8基因变异在单基因糖尿病诊断中的临床意义
items.summary_zh: 背景：ABCC8基因变异与胰岛素分泌相关的多种疾病有关，如先天性高胰岛素血症、新生儿糖尿病和青少年发病糖尿病（MODY）。本研究旨在表征ABCC8变异，并评估其与临床表型及家族分离的关系。方法：2017年至2026年5月，对1202名疑似单基因糖尿病患者的DNA进行tNGS（靶向下一代测序）分析，评估ABCC8基因的外显子及其邻近内含子区域的单核苷酸变异（SNVs）和小插入缺失（indels）。根据种群频率、计算预测和临床分类优先考虑稀有变异。选定变异后，通过Sanger测序进行确认和分离分析。结果：我们发现五名患者携带致病或可能致病的ABCC8变异，其中一个框移变异为首次报道。所有患者均有糖尿病，部分患者有低血糖病史。家族研究显示家族内变异性，并识别出先前未被认知的受影响亲属。结论：我们的研究结果支持ABCC8变异相关的广泛临床谱系，并强调家族分离的重要性。

items.title: Cognitive and Physical Functioning in Young Adults with Stroke: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study of Anxiety, Depression, and Stress
items.abstract: Background: Stroke in young adults is an increasingly important public health concern because of its long-term impact on cognitive functioning, psychological well-being, and social participation. Understanding the interplay between cognitive impairment, psychological distress, and stroke severity is essential for optimizing post-stroke management. Objective: To compare cognitive function and symptoms of depression, anxiety, and stress between young adults with stroke and healthy controls and to investigate the associations of these outcomes with sociodemographic and disease-related characteristics. Methods: This cross-sectional case–control study was conducted at a university hospital in Türkiye between January and December 2025. A total of 160 participants, including 80 patients aged 18– 65 years with a clinical diagnosis of stroke and 80 healthy controls, were enrolled. Cognitive function was evaluated using the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), neurological severity using the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), functional disability using the Modified Rankin Scale (mRS), and psychological symptoms using the Depression Anxiety Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21). Group differences were examined using multivariate general linear models, and Pearson correlation analyses were performed to evaluate associations between disease-specific characteristics and psychological and cognitive outcomes. Results: Across the study groups, the control group exhibited significantly higher levels of depression, anxiety, and stress than the stroke group. These between-group differences remained significant after adjustment for age, whereas the age-adjusted between-group difference in MMSE scores was not statistically significant. Age was not significantly associated with depression, anxiety, or stress scores but was significantly associated with MMSE performance. After adjustment for study group and age, the examined sociodemographic characteristics—gender, education level, employment status, income level, marital status, alcohol use, and smoking—showed no statistically significant main effects on depression, anxiety, stress, or MMSE scores. Although employment status showed a trend toward an association with anxiety, this finding did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.053). Higher NIHSS and mRS scores were significantly associated with higher depression, anxiety, and stress scores and lower MMSE scores (all p 0.001). Conclusions: Psychological distress and cognitive performance demonstrated distinct patterns of association in young adults following stroke. Neurological severity and functional disability were consistently associated with both psychological distress and cognitive performance. After adjustment for study group and age, the examined sociodemographic characteristics showed no statistically significant main effects on depression, anxiety, stress, or MMSE scores. In contrast, age was significantly associated with MMSE performance but not with depression, anxiety, or stress. The unexpectedly higher levels of depression, anxiety, and stress observed among controls persisted after adjustment for age and warrant further investigation, particularly in relation to potential contextual, psychosocial, and recruitment-related factors. These findings highlight the importance of considering psychological, cognitive, neurological, and functional measures together when assessing young adults with stroke.
items.authors: Dilek Baykal, Ozge Fircasiguzel, Demet Aygun

items.title: Restrained Expansion and End-Zone Stress Compensation in a Pretensioned Precast Concrete Pavement Slab: Full-Scale Strain Monitoring and Mechanical Assessment
items.abstract: Pretensioned precast pavement slabs exhibit reduced compressive stress near their free ends owing to the finite transfer length of prestressing strands. This study investigated an 800 mm self-stressing concrete end segment using five mixtures containing 0%, 6%, 10%, 12%, and 18% expansive agent and a 3700 mm × 975 mm × 240 mm instrumented slab monitored during strand release and for 180 days thereafter. The E10 and E12 restrained specimens developed calculated self-stresses of 1.36 and 1.53 MPa, respectively, whereas the E18 specimen exhibited a visible longitudinal crack. At 28 days, the expansive mixtures attained compressive and flexural strengths of at least 59.2 and 7.7 MPa, respectively. In the slab, strand-induced compression was approximately 0.50 MPa at 125 mm from the end and 1.25 MPa in the interior, indicating a local deficit of 0.75 MPa. The mean end-segment strain 24 h before release was 221.23 με, corresponding to 1.86 MPa of calculated restraint stress. Total compression at 125 mm reached 2.24 MPa immediately after release and was estimated at 1.58 MPa on day 140 before thermal correction. A full-length compatibility model estimated the end-plate device contribution at 0.12 MPa after release and 0.07 MPa on day 140. The monitored release response indicates that restrained expansion restored compression in the slab end relative to the interior reference.

items.title: Breaking the Graphite Trilemma: An Isotropic Core–Shell Anode for High-Energy and Fast-Charging Li-Ion Batteries
items.abstract: High-energy-density Li-ion batteries demand highly graphitized graphite anodes, yet elevated graphitization inevitably amplifies structural anisotropy, obstructing Li+ intercalation and compromising rate capability. To resolve this trilemma, we establish a precursor–structure–performance framework for pitch-based artificial graphites, revealing that this performance trade-off is governed by impurity content, ordered domains, and micropores: low-impurity precursors facilitate crystallite growth along the c-axis to realize high graphitization; ordered domains promote in-plane crystallite growth; and intrinsic micropores restrain excessive in-plane crystallite enlargement, lowering the orientation index and maintaining structural isotropy. Purified coal-based needle coke emerges as the optimal matrix, featuring a high graphitization degree of 94.89% alongside a moderate orientation index of 10.25. A resin-derived hard-carbon coating, with markedly higher disorder than its pitch-derived counterpart, is applied to construct an isotropic core–shell architecture (AG-R). The disordered surface layer acts as a Li+ transfer station, preserving low-rate capacity while boosting the Li+ diffusion coefficient by ~2.2-fold. In 2.5 Ah 18,650 full cells, AG-R achieves an energy density exceeding 430 Wh kg−1 (based on the total active material mass), retains 92.3% capacity at 10 C discharge and 81.6% at 3 C charge, and sustains over 80% capacity retention after 4600 cycles at 1 C. This work validates that precursor-directed bulk isotropy regulation, coupled with surface disordering engineering, offers a viable pathway toward fast-charging, high-energy graphite anodes.
items.authors: Bing Kang, Siqi Liu, Liekai Liu, Wenliang Hu, Keju Ding, Yongcheng Zou

items.title: Offline-Certified Robust Block Backstepping for Perturbed Underactuated Mechanical Systems
items.abstract: This paper develops certifiable enhancements to a block-backstepping controller for n-DOF underactuated mechanical systems in the Spong normal form. Two offline-computable tests, each reducible to a finite algebraic computation over a prescribed compact domain, are established: a minimum singular-value margin certifying uniform invertibility of the decoupling matrix, and a Jacobian Hurwitz condition certifying local exponential stability of the zero dynamics—the latter derived via an implicit zero-manifold parametrisation. Robustness overlays are introduced, comprising a bi-power term on the velocity-error channel and a matched-disturbance observer. Together, they supply an explicit observer transient budget and a practical entrance bound to(ε)+Tent for ∥z˙1∥2. No finite-time convergence of the complete closed-loop state is claimed. The resulting workflow permits offline tuning and verification prior to deployment. A simulation on a high-fidelity cart–pendulum model is consistent with those bounds; it is not a substitute for the offline certificates.
items.authors: Shubhobrata Rudra, Mahmut Reyhanoglu

items.title: Algorithmic Gestation: Inference, Stages and Prescription in the Organisation of Biographical Time
items.abstract: Algorithmic personalisation holds a central place in platform studies, where it has been described as the outcome of classification, profiling and adaptation to inferred preference. That vocabulary proves insufficient once what the system attributes is no longer a stable property of the subject but a condition with a beginning, an internal articulation into stages and an end, since the platform must then hold a model of how the attribution will change and distribute content in accordance with it. My focus falls on this form of temporal organisation, and I develop the concept of algorithmic gestation through five jointly necessary features: inference of an emerging biographical state, stage-sensitive temporal sequencing, progressive stabilisation of an algorithmic identity, anticipatory presentation of practices and needs, and normative prescription indexed to the projected trajectory. The argument rests on a nine-month digital autoethnography carried out during my own pregnancy, in which I documented the reconfiguration of an Instagram feed, and it sits within a feminist STS genealogy that treats obstetric visualisation, prenatal diagnosis, self-tracking and intensive mothering as layers which accumulate rather than succeed one another. The material proves consistent with four of the five features and required revision of the fifth, since stabilisation of identity appears to operate as subordination of earlier configurations rather than as their replacement. I argue that algorithmic inference constitutes the most recent layer of reproductive governance, set apart by the absence of a threshold, by the absence of disclosure and by its address to a subject identified in advance of any account she gives of herself, and that platform power extends beyond the management of visibility to the organisation of biographical time.
items.authors: Suania Acampa

items.title: National-Scale Climatological Assessment of Ground Snow Loads in Kazakhstan: Eurocode-Based Zoning from Five Decades of Observations
items.abstract: Spatially differentiated snow-load assessment is essential for updating building provisions in Kazakhstan, where climatic contrasts and complex terrain produce substantial regional variations in snow accumulation. This study develops a national-scale methodology for ground snow load zoning consistent with the characteristic-value approach of Eurocode 1 (EN 1991-1-3:2003). The assessment uses observations from 210 Kazhydromet meteorological stations for 1971–2020 and snow survey data from 17 mountain river basins. Cluster analysis, minimum spanning tree regionalization, Gumbel extreme-value estimation, regional elevation-dependent regression relationships, and GIS mapping were combined to estimate characteristic ground snow loads with an annual exceedance probability of 0.02, corresponding to a 50-year mean return period. The resulting national map delineates nine snow-load zones, with assigned values of 0.8, 1.2, 1.5, 1.8, 2.4, 3.2, 4.0, 4.8 kPa and an open-ended highest class exceeding 5.6 kPa. Regional regression equations quantify elevation-related variations in snow loads within the investigated mountain and upland areas, complementing the geographical differentiation represented by the map. The results provide an observational and statistical basis for updating national snow-load provisions and selecting regionally appropriate ground snow loads for structural design. The underlying snow water equivalent data also support subsequent hydrological assessments of snow storage.
items.authors: Aliya Nurbatsina, Aisulu Tursunova, Temirbek Choduraev, Zhanat Salavatova

items.title: Method for Automatic Detection of the Technical State of Insulated Coolboxes in the Cold Chain Based on IoT Sensor Data
items.abstract: Maintaining temperature stability within the cold chain is critical to preventing food spoilage and financial loss. Insulated containers (coolboxes) using eutectic plates are widely employed to maintain passive cooling during transport. However, mechanical wear, seal damage, or improper latching can lead to microclimatic fluctuations inside the container, compromising product safety. This paper presents a non-invasive method for the automatic detection and classification of the technical state of coolboxes (fully functional, conditionally functional, and faulty) based on internal temperature and humidity measurements collected via wireless IoT sensors. Experimental trials conducted in a controlled climatic chamber simulating real-world operations demonstrate that micro-temperature gradients and heating rates allow for the early detection of seal degradation and incomplete door closures before critical thermal thresholds are violated. Specifically, the results confirm that uncompressed or damaged seals accelerate internal heating rates by up to 60%, and the diagnostic algorithm successfully classifies technical states with high sensitivity based on a degradation index threshold (∆Q ≤ 10% for fully functional, 10% ∆Q ≤ 30% for conditionally functional, and ∆Q 30% for faulty units). The proposed diagnostic framework supports predictive maintenance and improves overall cold-chain traceability.
items.authors: Augustyn Lorenc, Małgorzata Kuźnar, Janusz Pobędza, Artur Gawlik, Artur Guzowski

items.title: Migration-Driven Phylogeographic Homogeneity in the Red Macroalga Halymenia durvillei (Halymeniales, Rhodophyta) Along the Andaman Coast of Thailand
items.abstract: The Thai-Malay Peninsula is an important marine biodiversity hotspot at the boundary between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Yet, phylogeographic understanding of macroalgae along the Andaman Sea coast of Thailand remains limited relative to other benthic species. Here, by sequencing mitochondrial cox1 and chloroplast rbcL sequences from 333 specimens of the red seaweed Halymenia durvillei across 20 sites, we found low genetic diversity (11 and 4 haplotypes, respectively) and a lack of pronounced population structure. A single dominant haplotype per marker was restricted to Phuket Island and Phang Nga. Analysis of variance (AMOVA) revealed no significant genetic differentiation between the Myanmar Shelf and the Malacca Strait Shelf, with most of the variation (90.28–98.63%) partitioned within populations. Gene-flow estimates revealed significantly asymmetric migration among populations, with most sites (i.e., Ranong, Phangnga, and Phuket) functioning as both sources and sinks of migrants, broadly consistent with the dispersal mediated by ocean currents during the northeast monsoon season. Bayesian Skyline Plot analysis revealed a sharp demographic contraction during the early middle Miocene, followed by a progressive expansion since the early Pleistocene. The presence of endemic haplotypes in the northern Malacca Strait suggests this area likely served as a marine refugium during glacial maximal low stands. In brief, phylogeographic homogeneity of H. durvillei along the Andaman Sea reflects the combined effects of glacial bottlenecks during glacial sea-level fluctuations and postglacial recolonization driven by ocean circulations. These results highlight populations with unique genetic diversity (e.g., Tankhen Bay, Phuket, and Lam Kaen Beach, Phangnga) as candidates for in situ protection and integration into protected area networks under climate warming.
items.authors: Ze-Hui Liu, Xiao-Meng Sun, Xuan Vy Nguyen, Juan Diego Gaitan-Espitia, Stefano G. A. Draisma, Zi-Min Hu

items.title: Perinatal and Early Respiratory Factors Associated with Invasive Mechanical Ventilation in Very Preterm Infants: A Retrospective Cohort Study from Kazakhstan
items.abstract: Background: Evidence on factors associated with the timing of invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) among very preterm infants in Central Asia remains limited. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included infants born at 22–30 weeks gestation in two tertiary perinatal centers in Kazakhstan between 2021 and 2025. Analyses were restricted to 381 infants with complete data. IMV initiated during the first week of life was classified as early IMV, and IMV initiated after the first week as late IMV. Separate multivariable logistic regression models were constructed for any, early, and late IMV. Results: Any IMV was recorded in 191 infants (50.1%), including 132 (34.6%) with early IMV and 59 (15.5%) with late IMV. Early IMV was associated with gestational age ≤ 27 weeks (aOR 3.91, 95% CI 1.66–9.22), absence of spontaneous breathing at birth (aOR 151.93, 95% CI 18.26–1263.88), and initial FiO2 0.30 (aOR 4.39, 95% CI 1.97–9.77). Complete antenatal corticosteroid exposure was inversely associated with early IMV (aOR 0.38, 95% CI 0.20–0.72). Late IMV was associated with birth weight 1000 g (aOR 3.51, 95% CI 1.47–8.35) and initial FiO2 0.30 (aOR 2.12, 95% CI 1.02–4.39). An initial set CPAP ≥ 12 cmH2O was recorded in 71.9% of infants and was associated with any IMV but not with early or late IMV separately. Conclusions: Early and late IMV were associated with different clinical patterns. These observational associations may support risk assessment but do not establish causal effects of respiratory-support practices.
items.authors: Umid Alimukhamedov, Nishankul Bozhbanbayeva, Merih Çetinkaya, Talgat Tolykbayev, Altynay Sadykova, Bekzat Suieubekov

items.title: Predictive Tires for Electric and Autonomous Vehicles: A Comprehensive Review
items.abstract: The role of tires in vehicle dynamics has evolved from passive support elements to active sources of information. This paper provides a comprehensive synthesis of recent advances in wheel–road interaction, structural optimization, and intelligent sensing, toward the emerging concept of the predictive tire. Fundamental phenomena, including slip-induced energy losses, aquaplaning thresholds, and radial stiffness variation, are analyzed for their impact on safety, ride comfort, and energy efficiency. Structural developments, including multi-objective optimizations and advanced composite materials targeting rolling-resistance reduction and NVH (Noise, Vibration, Harshness) improvement, are important for electric-vehicle applications. At the same time, progress is being made in the integration of sensors, such as polyvinylidene fluoride piezoelectric films (PVDF), distributed strain sensors, embedded accelerometers, and hybrid tire pressure monitoring systems (h-TPMSs), along with advanced data-driven methods such as fuzzy logic, hybrid Kalman filters, and Transformer neural networks for estimating friction coefficients and contact forces. The integration of these directions supports the tire’s transition toward a predictive multifunctional platform supplying real-time variables for the anti-lock braking system (ABS), electronic stability control (ESC), torque vectoring, and advanced driver assistance systems (ADASs), reinforcing its role in the safe and intelligent mobility of electric and autonomous vehicles.
items.authors: Constantin-Cosmin Danci, Nicolae Burnete, Adrian Todoruț, Nicolae Cordoș, Irina Duma, István Barabás

items.title: Heme-Binding Groups in Cytochrome P450 Inhibitors: Coordination Mechanisms, Evidence Standards and Implications for CYP19A1 Ligand Design
items.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes are heme-thiolate monooxygenases whose inhibition can result from direct reversible axial ligation of the distal heme iron, perturbation of the axial-water environment, or metabolism-dependent heme interactions. This focused review critically examines the chemical classes used as putative heme-binding groups in small-molecule CYP inhibitors, with emphasis on imidazoles, 1,2,4-triazoles, pyridines, 1,2,3-triazoles, sulfur-containing heterocycles, hydroxamates, nitriles and isonitriles. We discuss the evidential limits of ligand-induced type II spectra, distinguish direct parent–ligand coordination from mechanism-based inactivation, and outline an evidence hierarchy integrating enzymology, UV–Vis spectroscopy, EPR-based methods, structural biology and QM/MM calculations. CYP19A1 is used as a medicinal-chemistry case study illustrating how donor identity, binding geometry, scaffold recognition and selectivity against drug-metabolising and steroidogenic CYP enzymes must be optimized concurrently. We propose practical design and validation principles for the development of selectively heme-directed CYP19A1 inhibitors.
items.authors: Paweł Kozyra, Maciej Masłyk

items.title: Gain-Scheduled Internal Model Control of Full-Bridge CLLC Resonant Converters for Wide-Range CC/CV Regulation: A Simulation-Based Study
items.abstract: This paper proposes a gain-scheduled internal model control (GS-IMC) strategy for wide-range constant-voltage (CV) and constant-current (CC) regulation of a full-bridge CLLC resonant converter. The symmetric CLLC resonant network inherently enables zero-voltage switching (ZVS) of the primary-side switches; the contribution of this work lies in the control-oriented modeling and regulation of the converter under pulse-frequency modulation (PFM). Traditional first-harmonic approximation (FHA) models neglect the dominant pole formed by the output capacitance and load resistance and lose accuracy far from resonance, which limits their usefulness for closed-loop design. To overcome these limitations, the nonlinear voltage-gain and frequency-sensitivity characteristics of the converter are characterized over the full range of switching frequency and load using Piecewise Linear Electrical Circuit Simulation (PLECS). The resulting small-signal sensitivities are stored in two-dimensional (2D) lookup tables, from which the parameters of the internal plant model are scheduled according to the measured operating point, without online parameter estimation. The IMC controller is then derived from the scheduled model, so a single filter time constant sets the closed-loop response at all operating points. Simulation results on a 750-V/11-kW converter show that, for CV regulation from 330 V to 900 V and CC regulation from 5 A to 14 A over a load range of 25–150 Ω, the proposed GS-IMC achieves a settling time of 12 ms, eliminates the tracking plateaus, and reduces the overshoot compared with a fixed-gain IMC.
items.authors: Shyr-Long Jeng, Wei-Hua Chieng

items.title: Target Color Contrast and Eccentricity in Visual Search: Implications for Control Panel Design
items.abstract: Control panel and monitoring interfaces require operators to perform visual search while assessing system status. This study examined how Target Color Contrast and Target Eccentricity, operationalizing specific visual and spatial aspects associated with the Salience and Effort components of the SEEV framework, were related to target acquisition in simulated control panel displays. Thirty-four participants completed a controlled eye-tracking experiment using a fully repeated-measures two-by-two design, and computational image analyses characterized the physical properties of the experimental stimuli. Target Eccentricity yielded the largest omnibus effect on Time to First Fixation (TTFF). Critically, however, the effect of Target Color Contrast depended on target location: the High-Contrast condition was associated with substantially shorter TTFF under High Eccentricity, whereas no reliable contrast difference was observed under Low Eccentricity. This interaction remained significant after excluding 16 observations with TTFF equal to zero milliseconds. The findings provide context-specific evidence that the manipulated visual and spatial factors were jointly, rather than independently, associated with target acquisition. From a design perspective, the results suggest a potential hierarchical approach in which spatial layout is considered first and visual prominence is selectively increased when central placement is impractical. This approach represents a design implication requiring validation in operational environments.
items.authors: Nicolas Lopez, Suat Kasap

items.title: Evaluation of Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) Systems with Polarization Diversity for Railway Infrastructure: Effects of Fiber Type and Installation Conditions on System Performance
items.abstract: Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) systems based on ϕ-OTDR are increasingly used for real-time infrastructure monitoring, but their performance is limited by coherent and polarization fading, which create signal blind spots along the fiber. This study evaluates two coherent-detection DAS architectures—with and without polarization diversity—together with the influence of optical cable type and ground-coupling method, in an operational railway environment. Field experiments were conducted along a 40 km SNCF (Société Nationale des Chemins de fer Français) railway line using train passages as excitation sources, complemented by controlled sledgehammer tap tests on a 500 m calibration platform connecting four fiber configurations (telecom vs. sensing cables, buried vs. duct-installed). Signal amplitude, differential phase, and phase Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) were used to quantify sensing performance. Polarization diversity reduced the fraction of faded signals below −40dB from approximately ≈8.4% to ≈1% of the fiber length and improved the Phase Stability Index (PSI) from ≈6dB to ≈10dB at 20 km, significantly mitigating polarization-induced signal dropouts across the 40 km span. Among the tested cables, the tight-buffered sensing fiber directly buried in the ground consistently provided the strongest and most stable response, while telecom fiber installed in a High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) duct showed the weakest coupling. These results demonstrate that combining polarization-diversity detection with an optimized fiber-cable coupling strategy substantially improves the robustness of DAS for railway infrastructure monitoring.
items.authors: Alex Chedid, Ali Kabalan, José Grand, Tarik Hammi, Gabriel Papaiz Garbini, Ianis Gaudot

items.title: Error Enhancement in Physical Rehabilitation: From Motor Learning Theory to Robotic Neurorehabilitation– A Comprehensive Review
items.abstract: Error enhancement (EE), also referred to as error augmentation (EA), represents a distinctive ap-proach to motor rehabilitation in which errors are not minimized but deliberately magnified in a controlled manner. The underlying premise is derived from contemporary theories of motor learning and sensorimotor adaptation: when the nervous system detects a discrepancy between the intended and actual consequences of a movement, this error provides a powerful teaching signal that can modify subsequent motor commands. Robotic systems make it possible to manipulate this error precisely by applying externally generated forces that deviate the limb from its intended trajectory. This review examines the theoretical basis of error enhancement, its development as a rehabilitation strategy in particular attention is given to studies conducted in healthy individuals and stroke survivors. The available evidence is then considered in relation to sensorimotor inte-gration, virtual reality, constraint-induced movement therapy, and the Bobath concept. Finally, the emergence of the BioXtreme/deXtreme robotic platform is discussed as a translational development that combines robotic force-field manipulation, three-dimensional movement, virtual reality and adaptive error enhancement. Although the evidence remains preliminary and larger controlled trials are required, error enhancement provides a compelling framework for converting movement error from a problem to be suppressed into a signal that can actively drive motor adaptation and rehabilitation.
items.authors: Eli Carmeli

items.title: Dynamics-Aware Gradient Clipping: Separating Feedback from Threshold Scheduling
items.abstract: Adaptive gradient clipping can improve training without establishing that its feedback signals are useful. We examine Dynamics-Aware Gradient Clipping (DAGC), a bounded threshold controller driven by clipping exposure and consecutive-gradient alignment. Its exposure term tightens clipping when clipping is already frequent. We show that an interior target-exposure equilibrium is unstable in a stationary mean-field model, even with exponential smoothing. We then compare the frozen controller with tuned clipping rules, an alignment ablation, and a predetermined threshold schedule on FashionMNIST and CIFAR-10, using validation-only calibration and twelve paired confirmation seeds in each of three conditions.These controls separate threshold scheduling from evidence for an online feedback mechanism; the analysis does not claim convergence of the coupled training dynamics.
items.authors: Yuxin Li, Zisong Yuan

items.title: Device Design Implications on RON×QOSS FOM in p-GaN Power HEMTs: A Simulation Study
items.abstract: In this paper, we analyze by means of numerical simulations the device design implications on the RON×QOSS Figure of Merit (FOM) in p-GaN power HEMTs to be employed in soft-switching converters. During switching, p-GaN power HEMTs experience dynamic RON increase but also dynamic QOSS reduction, effectively establishing a trade-off between the two device parameters. This trade-off stems from the physical mechanism of hole redistribution within the C-doped buffer. Device design choices such as field plate length, channel and buffer thickness as well as C-doping concentration influence both parameters; however, the relative variation of the two parameters is not necessarily symmetric. Simulations are therefore carried out to identify the best device design choices depending on the target trade-off between RON and QOSS.
items.authors: Nicolò Zagni, Giovanni Verzellesi, Alessandro Chini

items.title: Rapidly Reversible Monitored Anesthesia Care with Remimazolam and Flumazenil Reversal for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Randomized Controlled Trial
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Monitored anesthesia care (MAC) is increasingly used for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), where rapid recovery of consciousness may facilitate early postoperative neurological assessment. Remimazolam provides sedation that can be pharmacologically reversed with flumazenil. We compared emergence from sedation between a remimazolam–flumazenil-based MAC strategy and a conventional dexmedetomidine-based strategy in patients undergoing transfemoral TAVR. Methods: In this single-center randomized controlled trial, 84 patients undergoing transfemoral TAVR were randomized 1:1 to remimazolam–remifentanil (R group) or dexmedetomidine–propofol–remifentanil (D group) MAC. Flumazenil was administered at the initiation of the postoperative awakening attempt in the R group. The primary outcome was arousal time, assessed using two prespecified measures: time from discontinuation of all anesthetic infusions to arousal and time from initiation of the postoperative awakening attempt to arousal. Arousal was defined as a Modified Observer’s Assessment of Alertness/Sedation score of 5. Results: Eighty-three patients were included in the analysis (R group, n = 42; D group, n = 41). The time from discontinuation of all anesthetic infusions to arousal was shorter in the R group than in the D group (19.05 [15.77–23.59] vs. 24.09 [19.25–34.78] min; p = 0.0045). The time from initiation of the awakening attempt to arousal was also shorter (0.60 [0.33–1.00] vs. 1.00 [0–4.72] min; p = 0.0117). No patient in the R group required rescue propofol. No significant between-group differences were observed in major procedural or postoperative outcomes. Conclusions: A remimazolam-based MAC strategy with flumazenil reversal provided faster and more reliable emergence from sedation than a conventional dexmedetomidine-based strategy during transfemoral TAVR. These findings suggest that a reversible sedation strategy may facilitate rapid recovery of consciousness when early postoperative assessment is desired, although its impact on neurological or other clinical outcomes remains to be established.
items.authors: Atsuhiro Kitaura, Takashi Mino, Yukari Yoshino, Hiroatsu Sakamoto, Mayuka Matsushima, Yoshinobu Nakayama

items.title: Social Dynamics Are Associated with Plant-Based Dietary Consumption Patterns Among Rural Adults in the U.S.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Social dynamics are known to influence eating behaviors and differ across geographic contexts. Some evidence suggests healthy plant-based diets (PBDs) are associated with reduced risk of chronic diseases, morbidity and mortality, and have lower environmental burdens. This paper examines the role of social influence, expectations, and pressures in consumption of PBDs among rural residents in the United States, with attention to gender differences. Methods: National survey data from rural adults (n = 2210) were analyzed using adjusted logistic regression models including an interaction between social beliefs and gender, and qualitative interviews (n = 55) thematically explored gendered social influences on PBD patterns. Results: Results showed that perceived expectations from important members of the respondents’ social network were positively associated with PBD adherence (p 0.001), without a significant overall interaction with gender (p = 0.163). Perceived social pressure was also associated with PBD adherence overall (p = 0.009), and the association differed by gender (interaction p = 0.001), but did not show a consistent trend across levels of agreement. Qualitative findings suggested that family members influenced the feasibility of PBD, while friends were more commonly described as supportive. Women appeared to face challenges to enacting a PBD when family members (especially male partners) were not supportive. Conclusions: These results suggest social relationships have complex and gendered roles in shaping PBD among rural residents in the United States.
items.authors: Sevda Alvirdizadeh, Saadatu Abdul-Rahaman, Rebecca A. Seguin-Fowler, Emily H. Belarmino

items.title: Regional Perivascular Space Burden in Pediatric Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension: A Case–Control MRI Study
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Altered perivascular fluid dynamics and glymphatic function have been implicated in the pathophysiology of idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH), but data in pediatric patients remain limited. Our aim was to evaluate MRI-visible perivascular space (PVS) burden in pediatric IIH and investigate its relationship with conventional MRI findings, transverse sinus stenosis (TSS), and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) opening pressure. Methods: In this retrospective case–control MRI study, 46 pediatric patients with clinically confirmed IIH and 46 controls frequency-matched by age and sex were included. PVS burden was independently assessed by two pediatric radiologists on axial T2-weighted images using the Potter grading system. Conventional MRI findings associated with IIH and TSS were evaluated. Associations between PVS burden, TSS, and CSF opening pressure were analyzed. Interobserver agreement was assessed using Cohen’s kappa statistics. Results: Basal ganglia PVS scores were significantly higher in pediatric IIH patients than in controls (p = 0.005), while no significant differences were observed in centrum semiovale or brainstem PVS scores. Centrum semiovale PVS scores differed according to TSS status; TSS-negative patients had lower scores than both TSS-positive patients and controls (Holm-adjusted p = 0.007 for both comparisons), whereas TSS-positive patients did not differ significantly from controls. No significant correlation was observed between CSF opening pressure and PVS scores in any evaluated region. Interobserver agreement for PVS grading was good for the centrum semiovale and basal ganglia and moderate for the brainstem. Conclusions: Pediatric IIH was associated with increased basal ganglia PVS burden, suggesting a regionally heterogeneous pattern. Pediatric IIH was associated with increased basal ganglia PVS burden, suggesting a regionally heterogeneous pattern. Centrum semiovale PVS burden differed according to TSS status, with lower scores in TSS-negative patients than in both TSS-positive patients and controls, whereas TSS-positive patients did not differ significantly from controls.
items.authors: Seda Kaynak Sahap, Eda Almus, Ömer Bektaş, Serap Teber, Suat Fitoz

items.title: Trends and Outcomes of COVID-19 Hospitalizations Among Patients with Cirrhosis: Insights from United States National Inpatient Sample, 2020–2022
items.abstract: Background: COVID-19 infection has been a major cause of hospitalization and mortality in the United States. Patients with liver cirrhosis may be especially vulnerable to severe outcomes of COVID-19 infection because of immune dysfunction, systemic inflammation, portal hypertension, and reduced physiological reserve. These factors can increase the risk of severe infection, multiorgan complications, and poor inpatient outcomes. Using the 2020–2022 United States National Inpatient Sample, this study evaluates the effect of cirrhosis among adults hospitalized with COVID-19. Methods: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) database. Adult hospitalizations with COVID-19 from 2020 to 2022 were included and stratified according to the presence or absence of cirrhosis. Using multivariable logistic regression analyses, we evaluated in-hospital mortality as the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included the need for mechanical ventilation, septic shock, ARDS, ECMO utilization, acute kidney injury, renal replacement therapy, length of stay, and hospital charges. Results: A total of 5,934,565 hospitalized COVID-19 patients were included, of which 115,170 had concomitant cirrhosis. COVID-19 patients with cirrhosis had a higher in-hospital mortality than those without cirrhosis (16.8% vs. 11.3%; aOR 1.28; 95% CI 1.22–1.32). Patients with liver cirrhosis were also associated with higher odds of invasive mechanical ventilation, vasopressor use, and septic shock. Conclusions: Cirrhosis was independently associated with increased in-hospital mortality and complications including the need for invasive mechanical ventilation and septic shock in adults hospitalized with COVID-19. Although mortality associated with these patients has declined over time, they represent a high-risk group that requires close monitoring.
items.authors: Antony Arumairaj, Dili Dhanani, Vimala Sravanthi Vajjala, Anuradha Shunmugam Veluswamy, Poojaben Dhorajiya, Radhika Arya
items.title_zh: 肝硬化患者COVID-19住院趋势与结果分析（2020-2022）
items.summary_zh: 背景：COVID-19感染在美国导致了大量住院和死亡，肝硬化患者因免疫功能障碍、系统性炎症、门脉高压及生理储备减少，可能面临更严重的COVID-19后果。本研究利用2020-2022年美国国家住院样本（NIS）评估肝硬化对COVID-19住院成人患者的影响。方法：采用回顾性队列研究，纳入2020至2022年住院COVID-19成人患者，并根据是否伴有肝硬化进行分层。通过多变量逻辑回归分析评估住院死亡率为主要结果，次要结果包括机械通气需求、脓毒性休克、急性呼吸窘迫综合征（ARDS）、体外膜氧合（ECMO）使用、急性肾损伤、肾替代治疗、住院天数及医院费用。结果：共纳入5,934,565名住院COVID-19患者，其中115,170名伴有肝硬化。肝硬化患者的住院死亡率高于非肝硬化患者（16.8% vs. 11.3%；aOR 1.28；95% CI 1.22–1.32）。

items.title: A Reduced Madelung-Type Model for Seismic Activation: Localization Dynamics and Baseline-Aware Validation
items.abstract: We developed a one-dimensional Madelung-type model to test whether seismic activation dynamics improve agreement with future earthquake distributions beyond empirical baselines. The model couples activation density, activation-flow velocity, effective loading, structural heterogeneity, and a curvature-sensitive potential. Synthetic simulations examined localization, while temporally separated United States Geological Survey (USGS) Japan–western Pacific catalog tests compared the model with persistence and historical relative intensity. Principal component analysis (PCA) preprocessing excluded holdout data, and weak-evolution parameters were calibrated independently on 2022 data. On the July–December 2023 complete-catalog holdout, weak evolution underperformed persistence on most metrics, including Pearson correlation (0.4156 versus 0.4837); paired moving-block bootstrap intervals for correlation and cosine differences included zero. In January–June 2023, several continuous metrics improved over persistence, but operating-point results remained mixed. Declustering favored weak evolution over persistence on most metrics, while relative intensity retained higher Pearson and Spearman correlations. Removing the curvature term produced stronger concentration, indicating a regularizing rather than uniquely focusing role. Grid refinement revealed resolution sensitivity in strong evolution. These results support a mechanistic and numerical proof of concept whose empirical performance depends on catalog treatment, forecast window, and metric; they do not establish robust earthquake forecast superiority.
items.authors: Dragos Nica, Călin Gheorghe Buzea, Alina Stefania Dobos, Dragos Ioan Rusu, Adrian Timofte, Diana-Corina Bostan

items.title: Continuous Pathway Reinforced Polyurethane-Based Thermal Interface Materials for High-Power Density Chips
items.abstract: Thermal interface materials (TIMs) are indispensable in electronic thermal management, as they mitigate interfacial thermal resistance and improve heat transport efficiency between adjacent components. A major factor hindering the thermal performance of conventional TIMs is the substantial interfacial thermal resistance arising at the interfaces between non-continuous fillers and the polymer matrix. To overcome this limitation, this study develops a continuously oriented TIM using a monolithic pyrolytic graphite film (PGF) combined with film-coating and hot-pressing processes. A polyurethane layer is coated onto PGF films, which are stacked and hot-pressed into a dense composite block. Sectioning the block perpendicular to the pressing direction yields a PGF/PU TIM. The material delivers a thermal conductivity of 118.5 W/(m·K) and demonstrates superior heat dissipation behavior under practical testing conditions. Through the establishment of continuous heat transfer pathways, this strategy alleviates interfacial resistance at filler–matrix interfaces and provides both theoretical basis and technical routes for high-power-density electronic packaging applications.
items.authors: Houde Wu, Xulei Wu, Yongkuan Zhou, Xiaojing Wang

items.title: Local Induction Melting Combined with Ultrasonic Melt Treatment: A Pilot Study on Porosity, Mechanical Properties, and Energy Efficiency in AlSi12 Castings
items.abstract: Light metal foundries consume large amounts of energy and rely mainly on gas-fired melting, which is inefficient and promotes porosity caused by dissolved hydrogen. This pilot study examines local induction melting combined with ultrasonic melt treatment (UST) as a decentralized and electrified alternative. AlSi12 was cast with varied mold temperature, casting temperature, UST duration and remelted fraction. Porosity was characterized by optical microscopy in 2D and, for a subset of specimens, by X-ray computed tomography in 3D, and the mechanical behavior by tensile testing. An experimentally benchmarked simulation was used to estimate the energy demand for larger batch sizes. Including the energy required for cooling, the measured laboratory efficiency was 7.9% to 14.9%, and the simulation predicts 41.3% for 100 kg, or 48% with a preheated crucible, against 53.1% derived for industrial induction furnaces. Specimens treated with UST showed a lower mean porosity, 0.56% against 2.14% in optical microscopy and 0.153% against 0.367% in computed tomography, where the pore count was 73% lower at almost unchanged pore size. Their mean strain at fracture was 45.5% higher and their mean toughness 53.2% higher, whereas the 4.4% higher mean tensile strength lies within the scatter of the measurements.
items.authors: Serouj Djabraian, Johannes Dettelbacher, Alexander Buchele, Fabian Teichmann, Sebastian Müller

items.title: The Importance of Biomechanically Appropriate Pediatric Footwear in Children
items.abstract: Background: The selection of appropriate footwear during childhood is crucial for healthy foot development, gait acquisition, and long-term musculoskeletal health. Despite the wide variety of children’s footwear available, there is no clear consensus on the optimal characteristics of footwear that supports healthy foot biomechanics during development. Biomechanically appropriate pediatric footwear (PF) is defined as footwear designed to accommodate the child’s foot morphology during growth, allow natural movement, and provide appropriate support and stability without altering physiological gait patterns. Methods: A systematic review was conducted and reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 Statement and registered in PROSPERO (CRD42022337587).
