The search included studies published between 2010 and 2025 in MEDLINE (via PubMed), Scopus, Cochrane Library, and Dialnet, focusing on preschool (2–6 years) and school-age (6–12 years) children. Younger children ( 2 years) and adolescents ( 12 years) were excluded due to gait and footwear data and developmental differences that could confound comparisons. Studies evaluating the effects of footwear on foot health, gait mechanics, balance, and functional outcomes were included. Results: A total of 1276 studies were identified, with 25 meeting the inclusion criteria. Findings indicate that certain footwear characteristics have been associated with foot discomfort, altered gait patterns, and variations in foot posture. While some studies suggest that barefoot walking or minimalist footwear improves postural control and reduces lower-limb impact forces during gait, others report that footwear does not significantly alter gait mechanics in young children. Variability in study designs and methodologies limits the ability to establish definitive recommendations. Conclusions: Although current evidence remains inconclusive due to methodological heterogeneity, variations in study populations, and inconsistent footwear classifications, biomechanically appropriate pediatric footwear and moderately minimalist footwear appear to be associated with more favorable functional outcomes in several studies. Further standardized longitudinal and age-specific studies with clearly defined footwear characteristics are needed to determine the long-term effects of pediatric footwear on foot biomechanics and musculoskeletal development.
items.authors: Inmaculada Requelo-Rodríguez, Ramón Mahillo-Durán, Gabriel Gijon-Nogueron, Álvaro Gómez-Carrión, Gabriel Dominguez-Maldonado, Lucía Roldán-Fernández
items.category_raw: Journal of the American Podiatric Medical Association

items.title: Electrochemical Behavior of Copper in Aqueous Solutions Under Industrial-Frequency Alternating Current Polarization
items.abstract: The electrochemical behavior of copper under industrial-frequency (50 Hz) alternating current polarization was investigated in sulfate- and chloride-containing aqueous solutions using Cu-Cu and Cu-Ti electrode pairs. Copper–copper pairs showed practically no directional electrochemical processes, whereas replacing one electrode with titanium caused copper oxidation owing to a passive TiO2 film that forms on the titanium surface during the anodic half-cycle and acts as a rectifier. By varying the electrolyte composition (H2SO4, Na2SO4, HCl, NaCl), current density (from 2 × 104 to 1.5 × 105 A·m−2) and Cu2+ concentration (5–30 g·L−1), different copper compounds could be synthesized selectively and with high current efficiency: copper(II) oxide (CuO) formed in Na2SO4 (current efficiency up to 89.2%), metallic copper powder formed in H2SO4 containing Cu2+ (up to 75.2%), copper(I) oxide (Cu2O) formed in NaCl (99.1%), and copper(I) chloride (CuCl) formed in HCl with an apparent current efficiency exceeding 100% owing to concurrent processes.
items.authors: Abduali Bayeshov, Azhar Bayeshova, Makpal Turlybekova, Fatima Zhumabay

items.title: Two Seasonal Patterns of the Thermal Effect of Building-Integrated Photovoltaic Curtain Walls in Cold Regions: Shift in the Dominant Driver and Temporal Expression
items.abstract: Existing studies on the thermal effect of building-integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) curtain walls are mostly numerical and mainly use absolute PV temperature; few have compared the relative roles of ambient temperature and solar radiation across seasons, or their temporal expression, in cold regions. This study conducted continuous field measurements on a south-facing ventilated CIGS PV curtain wall of a free-running demonstration building in Jinan, China, over 62 summer and 60 winter days at 10-min intervals. Single and two-factor regressions, standardized coefficients and partial correlations were used to compare the two drivers, including an incidence-angle-corrected radiation input; diurnal profiles, cross-correlation and positive/negative temperature-excess integrals characterized the temporal response and day-night asymmetry. Results show that: (1) the daytime mean PV surface temperature was higher in summer (35.2 vs. 13.8 °C), whereas the daytime temperature rise above ambient (ΔT) was 2.4 times higher in winter (+10.7 vs. +4.5 °C); (2) within the two-factor model, the dominant driver of ΔT shifted from ambient temperature in summer (75.5% relative statistical contribution) to solar radiation in winter (62.4%), a ranking unchanged with the corrected radiation input; (3) in winter, the warming rate was 2.26 times that in summer and the peak occurred 1.3 h earlier, while normalized diurnal profiles were similar in shape; (4) the PV surface was a daily net heat source relative to ambient air, with positive-to-negative integral ratios of 6.16 in summer and 2.48 in winter. Scientifically, the seasonal variation reflects a shift in the relative importance of the two boundary conditions rather than a change in heat-transfer mechanism. Theoretically, absolute temperature and temperature rise should be chosen according to the analysis purpose. In practice, summer operation should limit daytime heat gain, winter operation should limit nocturnal heat loss, and heating-season analyses should allow for the apparent response lag.
items.authors: Yingge Zhang, Tian Mu, Yu Liu

items.title: When Genetics Meets the Mediterranean Diet Across Metabolic Diseases
items.abstract: Metabolic diseases and related cardiometabolic conditions, including type 2 diabetes (T2D), obesity, metabolic syndrome (MetS), and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), arise from complex interactions between genetic predisposition and environmental factors. Among dietary patterns, the Mediterranean diet (MedDiet) has consistently been associated with improved metabolic health and a reduced risk of cardiometabolic diseases. However, substantial interindividual variability in metabolic responses to dietary exposures suggests that genetic susceptibility may contribute to differences in response to the MedDiet. Over the past two decades, nutrigenetic research has investigated whether adherence to the MedDiet can modify the effects of genetic variants associated with metabolic risk. Initial studies focused primarily on candidate genes involved in glucose metabolism, adiposity regulation, circadian rhythms, and hepatic lipid metabolism, including variants in genes such as TCF7L2, FTO, CLOCK, ADIPOQ, and PNPLA3. More recently, research has expanded to genetic risk score and polygenic risk score approaches, providing a broader assessment of inherited susceptibility. This literature review summarizes current evidence on MedDiet–gene interactions in T2D, obesity, MetS, MASLD, and related cardiometabolic traits, highlighting the transition from candidate-gene approaches to aggregate genetic risk models. Overall, the available literature suggests that the beneficial effects of the MedDiet are observed across different levels of genetic susceptibility, whereas evidence supporting clinically relevant gene–diet interactions remains heterogeneous and limited. Further large-scale, multi-ancestry, and well-designed prospective studies are needed before genetically tailored MedDiet recommendations can be routinely implemented in clinical practice.
items.authors: Francesca Gorini, Mariangela Palazzo, Morena Gabriele, Andrea Borghini

items.title: Evaluating the Robustness of Zero-Shot Time Series Models Against Data Degradation in Industrial Sensor Streams
items.abstract: Zero-shot time series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast unseen series without target-specific training, offering a way to significantly reduce the deployment overhead in enterprise pipelines and industrial sensor streams. However, their performance is documented almost exclusively on pristine benchmarks, whereas industrial data streams feature missing values, sensor outages, and amplitude spikes. Whether these models absorb such faults natively, and thus whether costly imputation stages can be removed, remains unquantified. In this study, we evaluate the robustness of three TSFMs from distinct architectural families, Chronos (tokenization), TimesFM (patching), and TiRex (xLSTM), subjecting their context windows to random missing data, contiguous block missingness, and injection of point anomalies at escalating severities and assessing point accuracy (relative RMSE) and 80% interval reliability (PICP) against a clean baseline. The results show that random dropout and transient spikes are natively absorbed by all three models (accuracy loss below 3%), while sustained contiguous outages are the dominant failure mode, with patch-based TimesFM most exposed (up to 59%). TiRex stays well calibrated throughout, while tokenization-based Chronos yields persistently overconfident intervals. These patterns persist and the contiguous outage vulnerability is amplified on data with genuine operational anomalies. For the evaluated models, sensor streams, and tested corruption severities, the results indicate that direct inference remains close to the clean-context baseline under independent random loss and sparse positive spikes, whereas prolonged outages warrant additional missing-data handling.
items.authors: Eleftherios Varverakis, Panagiotis Michael, Demetris Trihinas

items.title: When Anxiety Meets Anxiety: A Dyadic Co-Regulation Model of Teacher-Student Mathematics Anxiety in Special Education
items.abstract: Research on mathematics anxiety (MA) transmission has examined how teacher anxiety shapes student outcomes through instructional behavior. A more complex reality remains unaddressed. Teachers supporting students with mathematics difficulties do so under emotional conditions that may compromise their own regulatory resources, and these conditions may interact with the anxiety they are trying to relieve. The current paper draws on interpersonal complementarity theory, cognitive reappraisal theory, and the Collaborative for Academic, Social, and Emotional Learning (CASEL) framework of social-emotional competencies to propose a closed-loop dyadic co-regulation model of teacher-student MA in elementary special education mathematics instruction. In this model, students’ MA-related, low-agency behavioral cues are proposed to elicit complementary, controlling teacher responses that, in turn, heighten students’ MA. We theorize teacher MA and mathematics teaching anxiety (MTA), treated jointly, as an amplifying moderator of this loop. Special education settings are expected to be particularly susceptible, given their concentrated dyadic format and the fact that many special education teachers lack formal mathematics preparation. Among teachers, MA and MTA tend to co-occur. Teacher cognitive reappraisal, enabled by self-awareness and social awareness, is proposed as the regulatory entry point for interrupting this loop. The model generates testable predictions and argues for incorporating dyadic regulatory awareness into special education teacher preparation.
items.authors: Dana Sury, Oshrat On, Einat Kleider Tesler

items.title: Preliminary Assessments of Phenolic Profiles, Antioxidant Capacities, and Antiviral Activities of Fifteen Rosaceae Species
items.abstract: The increasing prevalence of antiviral drug resistance is limiting the number of available therapies, prompting a need to introduce novel antiviral compounds. Because nature represents a rich reservoir of bioactive molecules, a broad spectrum of research endeavors has been initiated for the exploitation of plant-origin extracts. In this context, the methanolic extracts of the aerial parts of 15 Rosaceae plant species belonging to the Amygdaloideae and Rosoideae subfamilies were investigated with regard to their phenolic content, antioxidant capacity and antiviral properties. Their total phenolic and flavonoid contents were determined, and the presence of individual phenolic compounds was quantified by LC–MS/MS analyses. Additionally, the antioxidant capacities of extracts were evaluated utilizing ABTS and DPPH assays, while antiviral properties were assessed against a broad panel of DNA and RNA viruses. All investigated extracts displayed strong antioxidant potency, as well as substantial variation in their phenolic profiles, with Prunus webbii exhibiting the highest total phenolic content (541.3 mg GAE/g DWE) and Sorbus umbellata exhibiting the highest total flavonoid content (116.1 mg QE/g DWE). With regard to the presence of individual phenolics, chlorogenic acid was the prevailing molecule in Amygdaloideae subfamily plants, with Pyrus spinosa displaying the highest content (35,173.6 mg/100 g DWE), while ellagic acid was the most abundant phenolic in Rosaceae plants, with Potentilla speciosa exhibiting the highest concentration (4127.0 mg/100 g DWE). All extracts exhibited notable antiviral activity against one or more of the tested virus strains. The lowest IC50 values were recorded against the influenza A and B strains, with the Sorbus Umbellata extract displaying an IC50 value of 0.8 μg/mL across all tested influenza strains. The Potentilla recta, Crataegus orientalis and Pyracantha coccinea extracts exhibited specific activity against the influenza A (H3N2) strain, with IC50 values of 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 μg/mL, while Pyracantha coccinea extract was active against the influenza A (H1N1) strain, with an IC50 value of 1.6 μg/mL. These preliminary findings provide initial evidence of antiviral and antioxidant activity of the investigated Rosaceae extracts that warrant further investigation.
items.authors: Serkos A. Haroutounian, Anna Apostolou, Lieve Naesens, Epameinondas Evergetis, Sandra Liekens, Eleni D. Myrtsi

items.title: More Area, Less Coffee Per Hectare? Reconciling Expansion and Productivity in Nepal Coffee Sector, 1994–2025
items.abstract: Nepal’s coffee sector is promoted as a high-value, climate sensitive opportunity for mid-hill smallholders, yet its progress is usually judged by planted area. We harmonise official statistics spanning three decades a national series (1994/95–2013/14), five later national observations (2014/15–2024/25) and district tables for 2013/14 and 2024/25 and triangulate them against FAO yields, trade records and a recent plot level study. Reported plantation area grew from 136 ha to 5,501 ha (10.1% yr⁻¹ after 2013/14), whereas green bean output reached only 642 t; yield on plantation area fell from about 225 kg ha⁻¹ (2013/14) to 117 kg ha⁻¹ (2024/25), 17.5% of Ethiopia’s FAO reported yield. Between 2000/01 and 2013/14, production moved one-for-one with area (elasticity 1.01, R² = 0.94) and yield showed no trend (p = 0.74), a pattern consistent with area-derived production estimates. In 24 matched districts, median yield fell from 238 to 111 kg ha⁻¹ (21 declines; Wilcoxon p lt; 0.001), but the fall was unrelated to expansion speed (Spearman ρ = -0.05) and occurred in all six slowly expanding districts, which weakens an immature plantation explanation. Three districts (Kavre, Nuwakot, Ilam) supply 46% of output, and Koshi Province holds 31.5% of area but 20.0% of output. Meeting claimed demand of 6,000–8,000 t would need 51,000–69,000 ha at today’s reported yield but 12,000–22,000 ha at plot-level yields of 364–486 kg ha⁻¹. Nepal’s coffee constraint is therefore productivity and measurement rather than land. We propose a bearing area census and plot-level monitoring as preconditions for evidence-based coffee policy.
items.authors: Prabin Gauli

items.title: Complementary Therapy Use and Parkinson’s Disease Symptom Severity and Progression: A Prospective Cohort Analysis Across Four Analytic Approaches
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Parkinson’s disease (PD) progression is highly heterogeneous, and prognostic biomarkers guiding personalized management remain elusive. Complementary therapies are widely used by people with PD, their real-world associations with long-term symptom progression remain poorly characterized, and conclusions drawn from observational data depend on the analytic approach used. We examined baseline complementary therapy use in relation to symptom severity and progression using four complementary analytic approaches. Methods: Data came from the Modifiable Variables in Parkinsonism prospective cohort study (2013-present, n=2612 at baseline). Participants reported consistent use of 51 complementary therapies over the prior six months; the outcome was the Patient-Reported Outcomes in PD (PRO-PD) score. Four approaches were applied: (1) separate regression models for each therapy, (2) a multivariate model including the 24 therapies with ≥100 users, (3) unadjusted smoothed trajectories, and (4) linear mixed-effects models with a Time × therapy interaction. Adjusted models accounted for age, gender, income, and years since diagnosis. Results: Vitamin D (61.7%), vitamin B12 (39.7%), and fish oil (38.7%) were most frequently used. After accounting for concurrent use, low-dose lithium, fish oil, and oral glutathione were independently associated with lower baseline symptom severity. Baseline use of oral glutathione, coconut oil, estrogen, homocysteine-lowering B vitamins, multivitamin/mineral supplements, and inhaled marijuana predicted slower progression, whereas N-acetyl cysteine (NAC) and probiotics predicted faster progression. Associations frequently changed across analytic approaches, and several therapies reversed direction between cross-sectional and prognostic analyses. Only oral glutathione was associated with fewer symptoms or slower progression in every analysis. Conclusions: Findings about nutritional and lifestyle exposures depend strongly on the analytic approach, and cross-sectional associations were a poor guide to progression. Oral glutathione showed the most consistent favorable associations and warrants evaluation in interventional trials.
items.authors: Laurie Mischley, Magdelena Murawska
items.title_zh: 补充疗法使用与帕金森病症状严重性及进展的前瞻性分析
items.summary_zh: 背景/目的：帕金森病（PD）的进展高度异质，个性化管理的预后生物标志物尚不明确。补充疗法在PD患者中广泛使用，但其与长期症状进展的真实关联尚未充分表征。我们使用四种分析方法考察了基线补充疗法使用与症状严重性及进展的关系。方法：数据来自可修改变量在帕金森病前瞻性队列研究（2013年至今，基线n=2612）。参与者报告了过去六个月内一致使用的51种补充疗法，结果为帕金森病患者报告结果（PRO-PD）评分。采用四种方法：1）每种疗法的单独回归模型；2）包含≥100名用户的24种疗法的多变量模型；3）未经调整的平滑轨迹；4）带有时间×疗法交互的线性混合效应模型。调整模型考虑了年龄、性别、收入和诊断年限。结果：维生素D（61.7%）、维生素B12（39.7%）和鱼油（38.7%）使用最为频繁。考虑到同时使用后，低剂量锂、鱼油和口服谷胱甘肽与基线症状显著降低独立相关。

items.title: Degradation Regime Discovery for EIS-Based Lithium-Ion Battery SOH Estimation Using Equivalent-Circuit and Vision-Based Features
items.abstract: Accurate State of Health (SOH) estimation is essential for the safe and reliable operation of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), yet most electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS)-based approaches fix a single equivalent circuit model (ECM) topology and measurement state without testing whether that choice is actually the most degradation-sensitive one, and rarely cross-check circuit-based findings against an independent, model-agnostic representation of the same impedance data. This study addresses both gaps through a physics-constrained framework applied to four commercial Li-ion cells cycled to end of life, with EIS spectra acquired at nine states in a cycle. Six ECM topologies (1R to 2RCPEW) were fitted at each state, and Pearson Correlation Coefficient was used to jointly rank topology–state combinations by their sensitivity to capacity fade. The best-ranked ECM parameters were then used as input to a left-to-right Hidden Markov Model (HMM) to segment battery ageing into ordered latent degradation regimes, with results compared against an HMM applied to DINOv2 embeddings of Nyquist and DRT plots. Finally, Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) was used to estimate SOH with and without the HMM-derived regime label as an auxiliary feature. Results show that State V (reached after a post-charge rest) yields the highest degradation sensitivity for most ECMs, with ohmic and charge-transfer resistances as the dominant health factors. Adding the latent regime feature improved SOH prediction for the 1RC and 1RCPE models (MAE reduced by up to 46.5%) but degraded uncertainty calibration for the 2RC model, indicating that the value of latent degradation information depends on how much temporal structure the underlying ECM already captures.
items.authors: Milad Tulabi, Roberto Bubbico

items.title: Aligning Multi-Sensor Images of Different Resolutions for Image Fusion: A Feature-Based and Mutual-Information-Based Registration Pipeline
items.abstract: Image fusion combines images from different sources into a single, more informative image and is used in panorama construction, remote sensing, medical imaging and infrared–visible surveillance, among other fields. The quality of the fused result depends directly on how accurately the input images have been geometrically aligned (registered) beforehand. This paper systematically presents two complementary approaches for aligning two images for fusion: (i) feature-based alignment for images from similar sensors (SIFT/SURF/ORB, ratio test, RANSAC, homography), and (ii) intensity-based alignment using mutual information (MI) for images acquired by different sensors at different resolutions. Preprocessing, transformation model selection, optimization, warping, fusion and post processing are organized into an end-to-end pipeline, and practical guidance is given on handling resolution differences in physical coordinates. The paper also discusses frequent implementation pitfalls in MI-based registration and appropriate evaluation measures. The pipeline is described reproducibly using the open-source OpenCV and SimpleITK libraries.
items.authors: Mustafa Tütüncü

items.title: Calib-Abstain: Uncertainty-Calibrated Self-Checking to Reduce Hallucinations in LLM Reasoning
items.abstract: Hallucinations in large language models (LLMs) remain a critical challenge for deploying these systems in high-stakes domains. We introduce Calib-Abstain, a framework that combines token-level uncertainty estimation with multi-path consistency checking to generate calibrated confidence scores. When confidence falls below a learned threshold, the system triggers tiered mitigation actions: retrieval augmentation, query reformulation, or abstention with explanation. Our approach employs temperature scaling and isotonic regression to minimize Expected Calibration Error (ECE). Experiments on mathematical reasoning (GSM8K, MATH), code generation (HumanEval), and general knowledge tasks (MMLU) demonstrate that Calib-Abstain reduces hallucination rates among answered queries by 24--31% while maintaining 80--88% coverage, with ECE improvements of 0.08--0.12 across datasets.
items.authors: Hejun Huang, Xikai Yang, Yuzhong Mei, Lei Mao, Hengguang Cui, Hongrui Liu

items.title: Virial CMB Thermodynamics
items.abstract: Since its formal discovery in 1965, the cosmic microwave background (CMB) played a cornerstone role in modern astronomy. The study of CMB became the main tool of astronomers in trying to gauge the early universe and to test their inflationary models against the CMB data as its radiation provided evidence of the big bang origin of the universe and studying the CMB anisotropies gave clues about the normal matter evolution and large structure formation in the universe. While applying the virial theorem at different scales, the discussion will show another important aspect of the role CMB radiation in describing the universe and its evolution.
items.authors: Ayman Kassem

items.title: em Alcaligenes faecalis /em A12C Modulates Hepatic and Renal Injury Response Associated with Sepsis: Experimental Study In Vivo
items.abstract: Sepsis is characterized by a dysregulated host response to infection; this can lead to multiorgan dysfunction where liver and kidneys play a key role. This study evaluated whether long-term oral administration of A12C modulates hepatic and renal homeostasis under basal conditions and during polymicrobial sepsis. Forty-five male Sprague–Dawley rats were allocated to healthy control (SAN), healthy A12C-treated (STO), septic control (IC), or septic A12C-treated (IA) groups. A12C was administered in drinking water at 6×108 CFU/mL for 30 days, and sepsis was induced by caecal ligation and puncture (CLP). Gene expression, protein abundance, antioxidant enzyme activities, and histopathological alterations were evaluated in liver and kidney. Under basal conditions, A12C reduced hepatic Tlr4 and Tgfb1 expression and TLR4, ICAM-1, and SOD2 protein abundance, whereas renal Tnf and Icam1 expression and SOD and GRd activities increased. During sepsis, A12C-treated rats showed lower hepatic expression of Tnf, Il6, Ccl2, Icam1, and Nos2, together with increased SOD1 protein abundance. In kidney, A12C reduced Tlr4, Il6 and Icam1 expression and increase CAT, GPx, and GRd activities. Reduced expression of several inflammatory and endothelial mediators was detected in both organs and a marked enhancement of renal antioxidant defences during sepsis. The present results support the potential of A12C to improve the host response to sepsis and limit sepsis-associated organ dysfunction, possibly through a preconditioning-like mechanism.
items.authors: Rafael Alayón-Afonso, Carlos José Martel-Benitez, Gabriel Escarrer-Garau, Ruth Henríquez-Cabrera, Josep Mercader-Barceló, Antonio Espinosa de Los Monteros y Zayas

items.title: CATCH-EVseq, an Ultra-Sensitive Capture Assay to Monitor Human Enterovirus RNA
items.abstract: The detection of low-abundance viral RNA in chronic or persistent infections remains a major challenge in virology, constrained by the sensitivity and specificity of traditional methods. One such infection, chronic enterovirus (EV) infection, has been proposed as a potential underlying factor in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis (ME), although this hypothesis remains debated. Supporting evidence for EVs as a viral trigger includes historical spatiotemporal overlaps between ME outbreaks and poliomyelitis epidemics, frequent reports of “flu-like” illness at disease onset, seasonal outbreaks patterns, and serological findings. To address the problem of EV detection, we developed CATCH-EVseq, an ultra-sensitive platform built on the CATCH framework. By integrating high-throughput sequencing with cDNA capture using 49,847 probes targeting 3410 EV genomes, CATCH-EVseq achieved a detection limit in artificially created samples as low as one copy in a microgram of RNA for two out of three biological replicates. Additionally, spike-in controls allow for rigorous validation of the capture and sequencing throughout the CATCH-EVseq procedure. When applied to a small number of blood samples from both ME patients and healthy controls, CATCH-EVseq detected no EV RNA, either in direct assays or after in vitro viral amplification. While these results do not support the presence of circulating EV RNA in the blood of individuals with ME, they do not rule out persistent infection in other tissues or organs. Critically, CATCH-EVseq establishes a robust, ultra-sensitive framework for future investigations of low-level EV persistence in biopsies, post-mortem tissues, or other clinical contexts where chronic enterovirus infection is suspected.
items.authors: Arnaud Germain, Maureen R. Hanson

items.title: Structural Elucidation and Quantitative Characterization of BDDE-Crosslinked Recombinant Human Type III Collagen by NMR Spectroscopy: Crosslinking Sites, Product Distribution, and Enhanced Properties
items.abstract: Recombinant humanized collagen type III (rhCol III) has attracted growing interest as a biomaterial for tissue engineering, wound healing, and dermal fillers because of its excellent biocompatibility, low immunogenicity, and crucial role in tissue repair and regeneration. However, native rhCol III suffers from poor mechanical stability and rapid enzymatic degradation in vivo. Chemical crosslinking with 1,4-butanediol diglycidyl ether (BDDE) represents a well-established strategy to enhance the structural stability and application performance of collagen-based biomaterials. In this study, we present a comprehensive NMR spectroscopy investigation of BDDE-crosslinked rhCol III, combining one-dimensional (¹H and ¹³C) and two-dimensional (COSY, HSQC and HMBC) NMR experiments to definitively identify crosslinking sites, characterize reaction products, and quantify key crosslinking parameters. Using a recombinant type III collagen of approximately 55 kDa con-taining 18 lysine residues per molecule, we demonstrated that BDDE crosslinks collagen predominantly through covalent modification of the ε-amino groups of lysine residues under alkaline conditions. Quantitative NMR analysis determined key parameters including the degree of modi-fication (MoD), the crosslinker ratio (CrR), and the degree of crosslinking. Physicochemical characterization further showed that BDDE crosslinking markedly enhanced the thermal and mechanical stability of rhCol III, with the denaturation temperature increasing from 55.94 °C to 68.18 °C and the apparent viscosity improving by approximately 100-fold. Importantly, toxicity and safety as-sessment confirmed the biocompatibility of the crosslinked material. Collectively, these results establish a robust NMR-based characterization platform for BDDE-crosslinked collagen and demonstrate that the resulting biomaterial affords enhanced structural stability together with excellent biocompatibility, supporting its potential for tissue engineering and dermal filler applications.
items.authors: Jiahua Cui, Liguo Zhang, Yang Lyu, Zhiwei Luan, Haiyun Peng, Lin Yang

items.title: Thermal Modeling of Submarine High Heat Flow Anomalies on the Southwestern Margin of the South China Sea
items.abstract: The southwestern margin of the South China Sea (SCS) features a well-developed strike-slip fault system. The Zengmu Basin and its adjacent areas, bounded by the Wan’an, Lupar and Tinjar strike-slip faults, exhibit prominent high heat flow anomalies that substantially exceed the regional average geothermal value of the SCS, with a maximum heat flow of 140 mW/m2. Nevertheless, the genetic mechanism governing these extreme geothermal anomalies remains poorly constrained, representing a key scientific issue in regional geothermal research. Based on integrated geological and geophysical datasets, this study conducts numerical thermal modeling to explore the effect of shear frictional heat on regional high heat flow anomalies under variable slip rates and thermophysical conditions. The results show that, under the assumed model conditions, shear frictional heating generates heat flow of 24.5–47.5 mW/m2 and accounts for approximately 22–35% of the total surface heat flow, indicating that it is a significant heat source in this region. The high heat flow anomalies on the southwestern margin of the SCS originate from the superposition of three dominant heat sources: mantle heat input driven by mantle upwelling along deep-seated faults, persistent shear frictional heat generated by continuous strike-slip activity, and crustal radioactive heat production from abundant heat-producing elements. The findings provide a robust theoretical basis for understanding the thermal evolution and maturity assessment of source rocks in sedimentary basins of the SCS.
items.authors: Gui Fang, Hongping Wang, Guozhang Fan, Guoping Zuo, Xuefeng Wang, Zhili Yang
items.category_raw: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering

items.title: Transient Synchronizing Stability Analysis of VSG Considering Voltage/Current Source Mode Switch Induced by Current Saturation Limit
items.abstract: The virtual synchronous generator (VSG) has been proven to be a promising control strategy for grid-forming (GFM) converters, which is applicable to power systems with a high penetration of converter interfaced generation. However, different from real synchronous generators (SGs) consisting of copper–iron, the VSG is essentially a power semiconductor device with poor overcurrent capability. Current saturation limiting is usually employed in the VSG to prevent overcurrent, which may induce transient voltage/current source switching mode (TVCSM) and deteriorate VSG’s transient synchronizing stability. In this paper, the transient stability of the VSG-based GFM converter is focused on with the effect of the TVCSM considered especially. First, concerning the VSG’s virtual rotor motion influenced by the TVCSM, a switching dynamic model is developed to depict the VSG’s synchronizing behavior. It is identified that the TVCSM introduces switching dynamics and reshapes the equivalent P-δ curve of the VSG’s virtual rotor motion. Then, the impact mechanism of the TVCSM on the transient synchronizing stability is clearly revealed based on the acceleration/deceleration area method. Analysis results indicate that the TVCSM increases the acceleration area and decreases the maximum deceleration area, worsening transient stability. To quantitatively assess the impact of the TVCSM on the transient stability further, a novel analysis idea combining the phase portrait method and inverse trajectory method is proposed to accurately estimate the critical clearing angle (CCA) and critical clearing time (CCT). Finally, the influence factors including the power reference, maximum allowable current, grid impedance, damping and grid voltage sag are investigated. MATLAB/Simulink simulations are presented to verify the theoretical analysis.
items.authors: Yongbo Chen, Tingan Wang, Qi Hu

items.title: Sharing, Reconciliation, and the Ethics of the Other: Indigenous Perspectives on Treaty Relationships and the Duty to Consult in Canada
items.abstract: The constitutional duty to consult has become one of the central principles governing Crown–Indigenous relations in Canada. Although constitutional and administrative law scholarship has extensively analyzed the duty’s doctrinal framework, this article asks how Indigenous treaty philosophies can illuminate its jurisprudential purpose as an expression of continuing relationships. This article explores that question by examining how Indigenous relational understandings of treaties illuminate the development of consultation jurisprudence. Through an analysis of the Supreme Court of Canada’s decisions in Haida Nation v. British Columbia (Minister of Forests), 2004, Taku River Tlingit First Nation v. British Columbia (Project Assessment Director), 2004, and Mikisew Cree First Nation v. Canada (Minister of Canadian Heritage), 2005, it argues that, despite arising in markedly different legal contexts, these decisions converge in recognizing that Indigenous relationships with traditional territories persist beyond reserve boundaries and continue to generate reciprocal obligations on the part of the Crown. Read through Indigenous treaty philosophies, consultation emerges as more than a procedural doctrine regulating governmental decision-making. It can also be understood as a contemporary legal expression of the enduring relationships established between Indigenous nations and the Crown. Rather than suggesting that Canadian courts have adopted Indigenous understandings of treaties, the article argues more modestly that Indigenous treaty philosophies reveal an interpretive dimension of consultation jurisprudence that helps illuminate how the duty to consult may be understood more consistently with the constitutional commitment to reconciliation.
items.authors: Frederico Oliveira

items.title: Entanglement Crossovers Under Time-Dependent U(1) Symmetry Breaking in Monitored Quantum Circuits
items.abstract: Conservation laws reshape quantum information dynamics by restricting how scrambling can occur. In monitored circuits, this raises a natural dynamical question: when a symmetry constraint is gradually relaxed, how quickly do the entanglement dynamics forget the symmetric regime? We address this question in one-dimensional monitored random circuits by driving the two-qubit gate ensemble from exact U(1) conservation toward unconstrained Haar dynamics. The response is not instantaneous: the entanglement retains a finite-depth memory of the conserving dynamics and crosses over toward the unconstrained behavior over a rate-dependent time window. Operational 25%, 50%, and 75% crossover times all move to later circuit depths for slower drives. At p=0.4, the same rate ordering is also observed through L=32 in a finite-time matrix-product-state consistency check with a limited trajectory ensemble. By contrast, the weak fixed perturbations studied here, ϵ(t)=ϵ0≤0.1, remain close to the conserving reference over the same finite observation window. Within this finite-time window, the driven crossover is therefore not reproduced merely by waiting under the fixed perturbations tested. Purification dynamics from a maximally mixed state exhibit the same qualitative response. We therefore interpret the results as a finite-time dynamical crossover from symmetry-constrained dynamics toward less constrained scrambling, rather than as evidence for a universal crossover exponent or a microscopic noise law. The study provides a controlled setting for asking how long symmetry-dependent information-processing behavior persists as a conservation law is deliberately weakened.
items.authors: Terrence Lingzhu Zhao, Zhou Shangnan

items.title: Latitudinal and Elevational Shifts in South Korean Plant Occurrence Records: Sensitivity to Sampling Heterogeneity
items.abstract: National occurrence databases combine sources with different objectives and spatiotemporal coverage, complicating the interpretation of changes in recorded locations. We evaluated the sensitivity of species-level shifts in mean recorded latitude and DEM-derived elevation to analytical specifications in an integrated South Korean vascular-plant database of 1,351,189 records, using 1980–2023 records for period-specific analyses. Empirical sensitivity comparisons were combined with controlled simulations of known centroid displacement. The primary analysis retained 1281 species and yielded across-species median shifts of +0.171° latitude and −102.7 m elevation. Aggregate estimates were similar before and after spatial thinning and record-count balancing. Positive latitude medians persisted under most specifications, but not under every spatial-support definition. Elevation estimates were more sensitive to temporal weighting and source composition: annual equal weighting reduced the median shift to −17.1 m, and omitting National Park records reversed its sign. In simulations, subtracting an assemblage-derived footprint markedly reduced recovery of imposed displacement. The empirical analyses characterize directional occurrence-centroid patterns and their sensitivity, rather than establish biological movement. Footprint subtraction cannot be assumed to recover unbiased change, and consistency across specifications does not demonstrate the absence of residual sampling bias.
items.authors: Kyungeun Lee, Seungbum Hong

items.title: Development of a Recommended Voltage Estimation and Control Methodology for Educational Building Power Systems: Integration of Factorial Experimental Design with PLC-Based Real-Time SCADA
items.abstract: The increasing electricity demand of educational buildings requires the development of intelligent approaches to power supply management that improve energy efficiency and ensure the reliable operation of electrical networks. This study aims to develop a mathematical model for determining the recommended voltage level in the power supply system of an educational building and implement it in a PLC-based SCADA control system. A second-order central composite design was applied to investigate the influence of three factors, including total electrical load, building wiring length, and external supply line length, on the recommended voltage level. The regression model was statistically validated using Cochran’s, Student’s, and Fisher’s criteria. The obtained model demonstrated high adequacy for the experimental data (R2 = 0.9934, adjusted R2ad = 0.9884, RMSE = 0.447 kV, and F = 0.175 Fcr = 2.30). The developed algorithm was implemented in the OWEN PLC300 controller using the EnLogic programming environment and integrated with the ENTEK SCADA system for automated voltage calculation and load management according to consumer priority. The proposed methodology can be applied in the design and modernisation of automated power supply systems for educational buildings and provides a practical approach to improving the efficiency of electrical energy distribution.
items.authors: Baglan Bekbauov, Kuttybek Arystanbayev, Elmurod Bozorov, Aizhan Apsemetova

items.title: Patent Foramen Ovale Closure Alleviates Long-Term Drug-Refractory Epilepsy: A Case Report
items.abstract: Background: Drug-refractory epilepsy (DRE) poses a persistent clinical burden, and the identification of reversible extracranial contributing factors represents a promising strategy to improve seizure control. Patent foramen ovale (PFO) with right-to-left shunt (RLS) has been recognized as a potential modifiable driver of epileptic seizures, yet clinical data on patients with extremely long-standing DRE exceeding 40 years remain exceedingly scarce. Methods: We report a 46-year-old female patient with a 44-year history of DRE, who experienced daily secondarily generalized tonic–clonic seizures (GTCSs) despite sequential treatment with six mechanistically distinct antiseizure medications. Systematic workup was performed and the patient underwent percutaneous transcatheter PFO closure, with a follow-up period of 14 months. Results: Systematic workup confirmed severe PFO-related RLS (grade III by contrast transthoracic echocardiography, grade IV by contrast transcranial Doppler), while brain MRI revealed no definite structural epileptogenic lesions other than an old ischemic infarct in the right corona radiata. At the latest follow-up, the patient had achieved complete freedom from GTCS with a markedly reduced antiseizure medication burden, retaining only infrequent mild focal absence-like seizures. Follow-up video electroencephalography unmasked previously occult focal epileptiform discharges in the left temporal region. Conclusions: This case suggests that severe PFO-related RLS may serve as a reversible aggravating factor even in decades-long refractory epilepsy, and provides electroclinical evidence supporting a hypothetical two-hit model of seizure generalization. PFO screening may be considered in selected patients with cryptogenic drug-refractory epilepsy, particularly those with non-lesional MRI, non-localizing EEG, and morning-predominant seizures.
items.authors: Yaning Sun, Xianying Zhao, Xuehua Cui, Xiaolei Song, Zihao Wang, Wenbo Liu
items.title_zh: 卵圆孔未闭封闭缓解长期药物难治性癫痫：病例报告
items.summary_zh: 背景：药物难治性癫痫（DRE）对临床造成持续负担，识别可逆的颅外因素是改善癫痫控制的有效策略。右向左分流的卵圆孔未闭（PFO）被认为是癫痫发作的潜在可调节因素，但关于超过40年DRE患者的临床数据极为稀缺。方法：我们报告了一名46岁女性患者，患有44年DRE，尽管接受了六种不同机制的抗癫痫药物治疗，仍每日发生继发性全身强直-阵挛发作（GTCS）。经过系统评估后，患者接受了经皮导管卵圆孔未闭封闭，随访14个月。结果：系统评估确认严重的PFO相关右向左分流（通过对比超声心动图为III级，通过对比经颅多普勒为IV级），脑MRI未发现明显的癫痫病灶，仅有右侧放射冠的旧缺血性梗死。在最新随访中，患者完全摆脱GTCS，抗癫痫药物负担显著减少，仅保留偶发轻微的局灶性缺失发作。随访视频脑电图揭示了之前隐匿的局灶性癫痫活动。

items.title: Association of Anti-TNF Therapy with Ventricular Repolarization Indices in Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Longitudinal Electrocardiographic Study
items.abstract: Background: Patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) have an increased risk of cardiovascular morbidity that cannot be fully explained by traditional cardiovascular risk factors alone. Chronic systemic inflammation has been implicated in myocardial electrical remodeling, yet the effect of anti-tumor necrosis factor (anti-TNF) therapy on ventricular repolarization remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated longitudinal changes in electrocardiographic markers of ventricular repolarization following anti-TNF therapy in patients with RA. Methods: This retrospective longitudinal study included 115 patients with RA who initiated anti-TNF therapy and had clinical, laboratory, and 12-lead electrocardiographic assessments at baseline and after approximately 24 weeks. Ventricular repolarization was evaluated using QT, corrected QT (QTc), Tpeak–Tend (Tp-e), corrected Tp-e (cTp-e), and Tp-e/QT. Cross-sectional associations between repolarization indices and inflammatory/disease-related variables were assessed at 24 weeks, together with longitudinal correlations between changes in these variables and changes in repolarization indices. Results: The mean age was 54.4 ± 12.2 years, and 81.7% of participants were women. After 24 weeks of treatment, significant reductions were observed in CRP, ESR, DAS28-CRP, and HAQ scores (all p 0.001). The Tp-e interval decreased from 85.1 ± 13.6 to 75.3 ± 13.5 ms, and the Tp-e/QT ratio decreased from 0.20 ± 0.04 to 0.18 ± 0.03 (both p 0.001), with moderate within-subject effect sizes for both changes (Cohen’s dz = 0.46). At 24 weeks, Tp-e and Tp-e/QT were positively correlated with inflammatory markers, disease activity, functional impairment, and disease duration. However, longitudinal change-to-change analyses showed no consistent associations between changes in inflammatory/disease activity measures and changes in repolarization indices, except for a weak correlation between ΔDAS28-CRP and ΔTp-e (r = 0.201, p = 0.031). Despite a significant reduction in mean QTc, the proportion of patients with prolonged QTc remained unchanged (18.3% at both assessments; McNemar p = 1.00). Conclusions: Anti-TNF therapy in patients with RA was associated with significant improvements in several ECG-derived ventricular repolarization indices alongside reductions in inflammatory and disease activity. However, the lack of consistent longitudinal correlations and the unchanged prevalence of prolonged QTc indicate that these findings should be interpreted as treatment-associated changes rather than evidence of a direct electrophysiological or antiarrhythmic effect of TNF inhibition. Prospective controlled studies incorporating clinical cardiovascular outcomes are warranted.
items.authors: Melih Pamukcu, Tugba Izci Duran, Bora Demircelik
items.title_zh: 抗TNF治疗与类风湿关节炎患者心室复极指标的关联研究
items.summary_zh: 背景：类风湿关节炎（RA）患者的心血管疾病风险增加，传统心血管风险因素无法完全解释。慢性系统性炎症与心肌电重塑有关，但抗肿瘤坏死因子（抗-TNF）治疗对心室复极的影响尚不明确。本研究探讨了RA患者接受抗-TNF治疗后心电图心室复极标志物的纵向变化。方法：本回顾性纵向研究纳入115名接受抗-TNF治疗的RA患者，基线及约24周后进行临床、实验室及12导联心电图评估。通过QT、校正QT（QTc）、Tpeak–Tend（Tp-e）、校正Tp-e（cTp-e）及Tp-e/QT评估心室复极。结果：平均年龄为54.4±12.2岁，81.7%为女性。治疗24周后，CRP、ESR、DAS28-CRP及HAQ评分显著降低（均p<0.001）。Tp-e间期从85.1±...

items.title: Interpretable Machine Learning in Food Analysis: Closed-Form Chemometric Calibration of Mid- and Near-Infrared Spectra Using Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks
items.abstract: A Kolmogorov–Arnold network (KAN) learns a univariate function on every edge, so a trained network can be written as a closed-form equation, unlike a multilayer perceptron (MLP). A KAN was compared with five models, with selection nested within each withheld-lot or withheld-season fold, on tahini adulteration by attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infrared (ATR–FTIR) spectroscopy (1554 spectra, released here) and mango dry matter by near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy (across-season test). No accuracy advantage was found: the KAN’s coefficient of determination (R2) was comparable to a parameter-matched MLP’s but never higher on average, and on withheld lots no difference between the leading models was significant. Most of the accuracy lost in converting the network to an equation was due to the conversion procedure; correcting it raised the median external R2 of the tahini equation from 0.952 to 0.988. Repeated conversions of one network gave equations scoring −0.76 to 0.96, whereas an elementary edge basis makes the printed equation identical to the network up to rounding. With every lot serving as the blank, detection limits for samples resembling the calibration population were 8.9–21.6% adulterant, and blends at 4–12% were not quantified. The KAN provides an exact, inspectable screening calibration rather than higher accuracy.
items.authors: Abdulhamid Batayhi, Muhammed Özgölet, Hasan Cankurt, Muhammet Arici

items.title: Design and Testing of an Autonomous Laser Weeding Robot with Cross-Modal Vibration Prediction for Cotton Fields
items.abstract: Laser weeding is a non-chemical, non-contact precision weeding method particularly suited for inter-row operations during the crop seedling stage. However, maintaining precise laser targeting on weed stems during dynamic field operation remains challenging. This task requires close coordination among perception, control, and actuation modules, while vehicle vibration from uneven terrain further degrades strike precision on the move. This paper presents a fully autonomous laser weeding robot for inter-row operation in cotton seedling fields, integrating weeding control, automatic mode switching, and autonomous navigation into a coordinated multi-process architecture. Vibration-induced strike deviation is mitigated by STCF-Net (Spatio-Temporal Cross-modal Fusion Network), a cross-modal prediction framework that fuses forward-looking depth maps with historical IMU signals to forecast vibration severity over a 3 s horizon. The prediction enables the control system to proactively adjust travel speed and weeding mode before encountering rough terrain, balancing precision and efficiency under dynamic field conditions. Field experiments validated weeding performance in static and dynamic scenarios and demonstrated that STCF-Net-guided predictive switching reduced operational time by 11.5% to 13.9% compared with a conservative baseline in two controlled experiments, with only a marginal reduction in weeding precision. This study reports the system-level design of a fully autonomous laser weeding robot and introduces feedforward vibration prediction to the laser weeding domain, providing a practical reference for integrating predictive algorithms into field-deployable weeding systems.
items.authors: Yunqi Bian, Jun An, Yujie Bai, Hao Yang, Wanzhou Ji, Zizhao Wu

items.title: Soil Water Infiltration Under Bare Soil and Maize Straw: A Field Comparison of a Double-Ring Infiltrometer and a Rainfall Simulator
items.abstract: Soil water infiltration (SWI) is central to hydrology and erosion assessment, but the measurement method and surface condition may affect the rates obtained. We compared a double-ring infiltrometer (DRI) with a rainfall simulator (InfiAsper) on a Dystric Acrisol with a sandy clay loam A horizon, under bare tilled soil and under maize straw. InfiAsper applied five rainfall treatments of equal erosivity, combining intensities of 44.6–75.0 mm h−1 with durations of 106–38 min, on four to five plots per treatment and surface. DRI tests were carried out in the same fields (22 under bare soil, 13 under ground cover) and analysed as an independent group. We (i) determined the final infiltration rate (SIR_f), (ii) compared DRI with InfiAsper, and (iii) evaluated the Kostiakov–Lewis, Horton and Philip models. Under bare soil, InfiAsper means ranged from 21.6 to 37.7 mm h−1 and the DRI mean was 86 mm h−1. A planned contrast between DRI and the mean of the five InfiAsper treatments gave a DRI/InfiAsper ratio of 1.80 (95% CI 1.00–3.23; p = 0.049); with the 20 tests of at least 15 readings, it was 2.13 (1.22–3.71). Under ground cover, InfiAsper means ranged from 15.4 to 26.3 mm h−1 and the ratio was 0.65 (0.36–1.18) with all 13 tests and 1.73 (0.93–3.22) with the five tests that ran for at least 75 min. The ratio tended to be larger on bare soil than under ground cover, depending on which ground-cover tests were used. The intensity–duration combination did not significantly affect InfiAsper SIR_f. Horton fitted best for both methods and Philip worst. DRI thus gave roughly twice the final infiltration rate of rainfall simulation on bare soil, whereas no excess was found under ground cover.
items.authors: Wilk Sampaio de Almeida, Luiz Fernando Coutinho de Oliveira, Daniel Fonseca de Carvalho

items.title: Detection and Phylogenetic Characterization of Canine Distemper Virus (Morbillivirus canis) in Wild Foxes and Badgers from Northern Italy in 2021–2026
items.abstract: Canine distemper virus (CDV) is a highly contagious multisystemic pathogen posing severe threats to wild carnivores and domestic animals. To investigate CDV circulation and lineage diversity in Piacenza Province, Northern Italy, wildlife surveillance was conducted under the Regional Wildlife Monitoring Plan between 2021 and June 2026. Forty-three wild carnivores—comprising red foxes (Vulpes vulpes), European badgers (Meles meles), wolves (Canis lupus), stone martens (Martes foina), and one jackal (Canis aureus)—were evaluated by necropsy, histopathology and molecular assays (RT-qPCR/RT-PCR). Overall, 12 animals (27.9%, 95% CI: 15.3–43.7; six foxes and six badgers) were confirmed to be CDV-positive. No positivity was found before 2024. Positive animals displayed characteristic lesions, including hemorrhagic enteritis, pulmonary hepatization, and footpad hyperkeratosis. Sequencing of the hemagglutinin (H) gene of the four complete H genes obtained revealed that they belonged to clade A of the European/South American 1 lineage, showing the highest nucleotide identity with Alpine CDV strains from Switzerland and Northern Italy. These results confirm the recent circulation of CDV amongst foxes and badgers in Piacenza. Continuous molecular monitoring and integrated cross-border surveillance remain essential for the effective management of transmission at the interface between wildlife and domestic animals.
items.authors: Anita Filippi, Stefania Lauzi, Chiara Garbarino, Alessandro Reggiani, Riccardo Rossi, Fabiana Ferrari

items.title: Neurophysiological Characterization of the BigP3BCI Dataset and Preliminary Machine Learning Evaluation for P300-Based Brain–Computer Interfaces
items.abstract: The P300 component is a well-established event-related potential (ERP) widely employed in brain–computer interface (BCI) systems, particularly in visual oddball paradigms such as the P300 speller. In this study, we analyze the large-scale BigP3BCI dataset to characterize the neurophysiological properties of P300 responses and to perform a preliminary evaluation of machine learning-based classification. EEG recordings were segmented into epochs aligned to stimulus onset and averaged separately for Target and non-target conditions to compute ERPs. The analyses revealed differences between Target and non-target responses, with a predominantly centro-parietal distribution broadly consistent with the classical P3b component. Although the grand-average ERP exhibited an earlier positive deflection, additional analyses performed separately across study/paradigm groups demonstrated substantial variability in ERP morphology and peak latency, highlighting the heterogeneous composition of the dataset. A preliminary machine learning analysis was subsequently performed using Logistic Regression and shrinkage Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA). Classification performance improved progressively with epoch averaging, reaching an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of approximately 0.82 after averaging ten epochs. Performance was initially evaluated using five-fold stratified cross-validation at the classification-example level. To assess generalization under stricter leakage-controlled conditions, additional group-disjoint analyses were performed using leave-one-participant-out, leave-one-study-out, and leave-one-paradigm-out validation. In these analyses, train/test groups were defined before epoch averaging, which was performed separately within each partition and restricted to epochs from the same participant, session, and class. Classification performance increased with epoch averaging under both the preliminary example-level and group-disjoint validation schemes. With ten-epoch averaging, mean ROC-AUC reached approximately 0.81 under participant-disjoint validation, 0.78 under study-disjoint validation, and 0.77 under paradigm-disjoint validation. Overall, the study provides a large-scale neurophysiological characterization of BigP3BCI together with interpretable linear-classification baselines and an initial assessment of cross-participant, cross-study, and cross-paradigm generalization.
items.authors: Vera Gramigna, Arrigo Palumbo

items.title: DA-Transformer: Building Damage Assessment Under Complex Changing Conditions Through Multimodal UAV Data
items.abstract: Accurate damage assessment is critical for reconnaissance and rescue missions. Damage assessment based on unmanned aerial vehicle images is a relevant topic. However, sharing pre- and post-damage knowledge is hindered by the lack of same-viewpoint images in damage assessment for building restoration and reconstruction work. We propose a novel method for generating images based on the same view before and after damage occurs. A point cloud registration method based on serialized matching is presented for spatial transformation with complex damage variations, achieving lower errors and reducing training time. Then, the transformed data are utilized to train a pre-damage differentiable rendering model, generating the undamaged images of buildings from post-damage drone views. Therefore, damage assessment using a large language model (LLM) is conducted by comparing pre- and post-damage images and point clouds. We also construct pre- and post-destruction datasets based on videos. Our method overcomes the limitation of obtaining paired image data from the same perspective, improving the efficiency of evaluation and reducing the difficulty and cost of data collection. We validated the effectiveness of the method through scaling experiments and real explosion scenarios.
items.authors: Zhuoyue Yang, Yuxin Xu, Qizhi Xu, Kang Yu, Hao Song

items.title: Adaptive Arc-Voltage Control for Narrow-Gap Pulsed TIG Welding Based on Feedback Reconstruction and Effective-Error Identification
items.abstract: Reliable arc-length regulation is essential in narrow-gap pulsed tungsten inert gas (TIG) welding because restricted groove clearance makes small torch-height errors capable of destabilizing the arc and reducing process repeatability. However, pulse switching, wire–pool interaction, and acquisition noise generate voltage transients that conventional arc-voltage control (AVC) may misinterpret as geometric deviations, whereas strong filtering delays genuine drift correction. This study proposes a reconstruction–decision–adaptation architecture. An experimentally calibrated actuator–arc model supports adaptive Kalman filter (AKF)-based feedback reconstruction; an amplitude–duration–area criterion fixed from open-loop statistics rejects brief disturbances; and only identified effective errors drive online fuzzy-PID gain adaptation. Using fixed decision thresholds, NSGA-II jointly tunes estimator and controller parameters based on voltage RMSE and cumulative actuator travel. Across 20 simulation seeds, the tuned configuration reduced voltage RMSE and ramp-disturbance error by 15.8% and 51.0%, respectively, while travel decreased by 1.9%. Physical welding tests demonstrated improved voltage regulation while maintaining actuator activity: the 13.0 V comparison reduced RMSE by 19.7% and adjustment events by 8.3%, while six additional records at three prescribed voltages showed consistent mean voltage regulation within the tested conditions.
items.authors: Haiping Fan, Lei Guo, Yunda Duan, Weihua Liu, Yuefeng Chen, Minjun Peng

items.title: AI Tutor, Online Course, or Both? A Randomized Experimental Pilot Study for Evaluation Capacity Building
items.abstract: Extension lacks literature comparing standalone generative artificial intelligence (AI) with structured professional development for capacity building. Guided by Social Cognitive Theory and Cognitive Load Theory, this study evaluated the effects of an asynchronous online course and a custom AI tutor on evaluation knowledge and self-efficacy among Cooperative Extension professionals. We conducted a randomized 2 × 2 factorial pilot study crossing access to an evaluation certificate course with access to a custom Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT). Of 144 registrants, 78 provided matched pre- and post-test data, with attrition differing across conditions. Data were analyzed using a three-way mixed factorial ANOVA. Course access and GPT access each increased objective knowledge, with post-test means around 91% across treatment groups. No statistically significant additive effect was detected for knowledge gain. However, given a possible ceiling effect and limited statistical power, this result is inconclusive. Course access and GPT access each increased self-efficacy, but the combined condition produced the smallest self-efficacy gain among treatment groups. Because these estimates are based on participants who completed the study, findings are preliminary. If replicated, results suggest that Extension should combine AI tutors and coursework only when each modality provides known complementary value.
items.authors: Lendel Kade Narine, John M. Diaz

items.title: The Ideology of Mexico’s Catholic Bishops: Topic Modeling, Text Scaling, and Episcopal Networks, 1976–2026
items.abstract: This study examines ideological variation among Mexico’s Catholic bishops using computational analysis of 2330 documents (1976–2026): topic modeling, Wordfish scaling, and consecration network analysis. Topic modeling recovers nine topics organized around a spiritual emphasis pole (homiletics, pastoral life) and a social engagement pole (social pastoral, Chiapas/indigenous rights). Wordfish’s primary dimension contrasts prophetic/individual voice with institutional/consensus. Liberation theology bishops deviate most from the episcopal conference’s administrative register. Network analysis identifies the apostolic nunciature, through which the Holy See shapes episcopal appointments, as the dominant consecration hub. Regional and temporal variation are substantial but partly reflect source composition effects. A multilevel test that merges Protestant/Evangelical population share with bishops’ actual diocesan assignments, accounting for clustering by bishop and by state, finds that greater Protestant presence predicts more doctrinal and less indigenous rights discourse, closer to the supply side reading of religious economy theory than to its mobilization reading. Ideological differentiation within this hierarchical religious institution appears driven by differences in issue emphasis, and in the balance between charismatic and bureaucratic forms of episcopal authority.
items.authors: Alejandro Díaz-Domínguez

items.title: BioReason: Retrieve-Then-Reason MLLMs for Interpretable Fine-Grained Species Classification
items.abstract: Fine-grained species classification involves distinguishing visually similar taxa and remains challenging for general-purpose visual recognition models. We propose BioReason, a retrieve-then-reasonframework that uses BioCLIP candidates to formulate a multiple-choice task for Qwen2.5-VL-7B, followed by two-source supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and group relative policy optimization (GRPO). We clarify that the implemented evaluation retrieves the Top-5 labels from each benchmark-specific class vocabulary, rather than directly from the complete 454K taxonomy. When the ground-truth label is absent, it is inserted into the candidate set; consequently, the reported MLLM accuracy measures conditional candidate reranking and is not an end-to-end open-world zero-shot result. The executed SFT uses 31,023 caption samples and 4929 reasoning samples, while GRPO combines binary format and answer-accuracy rewards. Across nine benchmarks, SFT(A+B) obtains 40.81% macro accuracy and the subsequent GRPO checkpoint obtains 40.33%; GRPO improves the five-subset Camera Trap mean from 46.06% to 46.42% but does not yield a consistent overall gain. Generated responses follow the requested think – answer structure in 99.95% of cases, although this syntactic measure does not establish biological correctness or faithfulness of the explanations.
items.authors: Yicheng Duan, Xingyu Zhu, Yifan Zhang, Ganlin Wang, Kun Cheng

items.title: Triboelectric Nanogenerators for Self-Powered Distributed Urban IoT Sensing Networks: Devices, Applications, and System-Level Perspectives
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructure in smart cities is reshaping urban energy demand. Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs), which harvest ambient mechanical energy from wind, rain, vibrations, and human motion, are being investigated as sources for intermittently powered distributed sensing. This review examines TENG technologies in relation to energy-system planning, demand management, and potential roles in distributed energy markets. We summarize reported device outputs and sensing demonstrations, with an emphasis on hybrid integration with storage, power management, and complementary harvesters. Wearable and edge-based TENG applications are discussed primarily as ways to reduce battery dependence or maintenance frequency under specified excitation and duty-cycle conditions. Digital twins, load forecasting, and demand-management links are treated as potential system-level applications; quantitative city-scale validation remains limited.
items.authors: Junjie Tang, Manyun Zhang, Jia Meng, Zhiyuan Zhu

items.title: Characteristics and Applications of Chemosensors for Biometric and Microclimate Measurements in AI Astronaut Suits: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: Background: Astronauts operating in extravehicular activity (EVA) and intravehicular activity (IVA) suits are exposed to a closed, thermally demanding microenvironment in which sweat accumulation, hydration status, skin-barrier disturbance, optical-signal interference, and changes in oxygen-carrying capacity can affect health, comfort, and task performance. This review therefore evaluates five sensing modalities—humidity, pH, sebum, melanin, and hemoglobin—not as general cosmetic sensors, but according to their potential roles in AI-enabled astronaut-suit monitoring. Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted using multidisciplinary scholarly databases and publisher platforms. From 1036 initially identified records, 187 full texts were screened, 135 reports were assessed for eligibility, and 93 studies were included. Studies were organized into humidity (n = 22), pH (n = 20), sebum (n = 16), melanin (n = 20), and hemoglobin (n = 15) categories and comparatively evaluated for sensing principle, quantitative performance, calibration requirements, wearability, environmental robustness, and relevance to astronaut-suit integration. Results: Humidity and pH sensing are currently the most directly compatible with textile or skin-interfaced suit architectures because they can provide continuous information on the local microclimate and sweat/skin chemistry. Hemoglobin sensing is promising for trend monitoring of oxygen-carrying status but requires careful optical calibration for pigmentation, motion, perfusion, and pressure effects. Melanin sensing is primarily valuable as a calibration and radiation/optical-context variable rather than as an acute physiological alarm, whereas continuous sebum sensing remains comparatively immature for operational spacesuit use. Edge artificial intelligence (AI) can support multimodal sensor fusion, artifact rejection, personalized baselines, anomaly detection, and tiered alerts without implying stand-alone disease diagnosis. Conclusions: The five modalities have different levels of technological readiness for astronaut suits. Near-term research should prioritize humidity, pH, and optical hemoglobin trend monitoring, while treating melanin as a correction/context variable and sebum as an exploratory skin-barrier marker. Translation to EVA/IVA use requires standardized calibration, low-power edge processing, long-duration biocompatibility, resistance to sweat, pressure, motion and thermal cycling, and validation in suited analog environments before flight deployment.
items.authors: HyeRee Han

items.title: Topology-Guided ACO–YOLOv8n: A Metaheuristic-Driven Hyperparameter Optimization Framework for Blood Cell Detection and Classification
items.abstract: Automated blood-cell detection can support microscopic analysis, but detector performance depends strongly on the training configuration. This study investigates a topology-guided Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) strategy for jointly selecting 21 hyperparameters of YOLOv8n without modifying its architecture. This study uses 614 images from BCCD and LISC, with 5138 available annotations for red blood cells (RBCs), white blood cells (WBCs), and platelets. Random Search, Standard ACO, and topology-guided ACO were compared within the same discretized search space and with a maximum of 600 unique candidate evaluations per run. Across five reported runs, topology-guided ACO reached a mean best validation mAP@0.5 of 96.8±1.2%, compared with 94.3±1.6% for Standard ACO and 91.6±2.2% for Random Search. The selected detector achieved 94.4% precision, 93.3% recall, 95.8% mAP@0.5, and 62.3% mAP@0.5:0.95 on the reported held-out evaluation. Because LISC provides WBC-specific annotations rather than complete three-class labels, source-specific interpretation is required. The present contribution is therefore methodological: this study assesses whether transition-based search information can improve systematic hyperparameter selection for lightweight microscopic object detection.
items.authors: Fernando Rodrigues Trindade Ferreira, Loena Marins do Couto, Eliana dos Santos Paiao Pereira

items.title: Where the Protection of a Ship Hydrogen Fuel Cell Room Boundary Actually Resides: Fire-Resistance Rating, Shutdown Speed and Flame Detection
items.abstract: The International Maritime Organization (IMO) circular MSC.1/Circ.1647 requires a ship’s fuel cell space to be bounded by “A-60” divisions and permits equivalent-safety alternatives without defining equivalence. This study proposes a framework that reads boundary rating, fire exposure and shutdown response as interacting protection layers. A full-bore rupture of an in-service vessel’s 10 mm, 0.8 MPa line gives a 4.75 MW source term. The boundary is loaded with prescribed fluxes of 50–250 kW/m2, not a predicted fire field. A one-dimensional wall model, calibrated on one test series and checked against seven independent tests, was run over 60 cases of grade, shutdown time and exposure. At 250 kW/m2, the modelled A-60 column exceeds the 140 and 180 °C rise limits after about 24 and 40 min. Resolved spatially, the local limit is still exceeded. Shutdown speed sets what the boundary contributes: A-30 and A-15 stay within an insulation-only A-60 benchmark if isolation occurs within 102–103 s, against 1.8–5.1 s from component data. This is one building block of an equivalence case, not A-60 or system-level equivalence: integrity, reliability and explosion are not assessed. MSC.1/Circ.1701 calls for detectors suitable for hydrogen fires. Hydrogen-capable detectors exist, but the cited route through the Fire Safety Systems (FSS) Code to EN 54-10 supplies no harmonized hydrogen test fire.
items.authors: Jae-Young Choi

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Cardiac Magnetic Resonance in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Diagnosis, Phenotypic Characterization, and Risk Prediction
items.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a genetically and phenotypically heterogeneous myocardial disease associated with a broad spectrum of clinical outcomes, including heart failure, atrial fibrillation, ventricular arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) plays a central role in the comprehensive assessment of HCM by enabling integrated evaluation of myocardial morphology, ventricular and atrial function, tissue characterization, myocardial deformation, and longitudinal disease progression within a single comprehensive imaging modality. However, conventional CMR interpretation remains limited by manual post-processing, interobserver variability, sequence-dependent measurements, and reliance on a relatively restricted set of predefined imaging parameters. These limitations may hinder the full exploitation of the rich multidimensional information contained in CMR datasets. Artificial intelligence (AI) approaches, particularly machine learning and deep learning, together with radiomics-based quantitative image analysis, provide new opportunities to extend the diagnostic and prognostic value of CMR to extract high-dimensional and quantitative information from cine imaging, late gadolinium enhancement, parametric mapping, and feature-tracking-based deformation analysis. Emerging evidence suggests that AI-enhanced CMR may facilitate automated image analysis, improve diagnostic classification, support differentiation of HCM from phenocopies, enable tissue- and deformation-based phenotypic characterization, and enhance individualized risk prediction. Although several studies have included independent or external testing, many remain retrospective, rely on selected populations or internal validation, and lack prospective assessment of clinical utility. High discrimination performance should not be interpreted as established clinical utility, because calibration, decision-curve analysis, clinically relevant thresholds, and prospective clinical impact remain insufficiently evaluated. In addition, interpretability and clinical generalizability remain important challenges for translation into routine practice. This review summarizes the current role of CMR in HCM and discusses emerging applications, methodological challenges, and future directions of AI-enhanced CMR for diagnosis, phenotypic characterization, and risk stratification.
items.authors: Yu-Jie Xiang, Yu-Cong Zheng, Ju Han, Qian-Mo Wei, Ting Yang, Rui Li
items.title_zh: 人工智能增强的心脏磁共振在肥厚型心肌病中的应用
items.summary_zh: 肥厚型心肌病（HCM）是一种遗传和表型异质性的心肌疾病，临床结果包括心力衰竭、房颤、室性心律失常和猝死。心脏磁共振（CMR）在HCM的综合评估中发挥着核心作用，能够在单一成像模式下评估心肌形态、心室和心房功能、组织特征、心肌变形及疾病进展。然而，传统CMR解读受限于手动后处理、观察者间变异、序列依赖性测量及预定义成像参数的限制，影响了CMR数据集的全面利用。人工智能（AI）方法，特别是机器学习和深度学习，结合放射组学的定量图像分析，为提取高维和定量信息提供了新机会。新兴证据表明，AI增强的CMR可能促进图像分析的自动化。

items.title: FedLCD: A Federated Learning Framework with Layer-Wise Consistency Detection
items.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple clients to collaboratively train a global model without sharing raw data, but it is vulnerable to Byzantine attacks, in which malicious clients upload manipulated model updates to disrupt training or degrade model accuracy. Existing Byzantine-robust aggregation methods typically operate at the whole-model level, making them less effective against partial-layer attacks and causing potentially useful information from unaffected layers to be discarded. To address this, we propose a Federated Learning framework with Layer-wise Consistency Detection (FedLCD). Specifically, we design a layer-wise Byzantine robust aggregation algorithm that detects malicious updates by computing pairwise cosine similarities at the granularity of individual layers, and retains only those with higher average similarity. This design filters malicious updates while preserving benign information from unaffected layers. Theoretical analysis confirms that FedLCD achieves a convergence rate of O(1/T), where T denotes the total number of communication rounds. This rate matches that of standard FedAvg, while FedLCD guarantees Byzantine robustness when benign clients constitute the majority. Extensive experiments on the CIFAR-10 dataset demonstrate that FedLCD achieves accuracy comparable to or higher than existing baselines across various Byzantine attack scenarios, while maintaining robust detection performance, particularly under partial-layer attacks.
items.authors: Xukai Cui, Hui Wang

items.title: Dendrometric Data from a Tropical Arboretum as a Teaching Dataset and Baseline for Living Collection Monitoring
items.abstract: Living collections in botanical gardens play important roles in conservation, research, and education, but their potential to generate interpretable biological information for teaching and management is often underused. This study reports a teaching experience based on dendrometric data from the arboretum of the Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden in a graduate course on applied statistics. The course combined R programming with a problem-oriented pedagogical approach, using a census dataset of 4621 individuals with DBH ≥ 10 cm as a common object of investigation. The dataset served as a common framework for linking statistical procedures, from exploratory analysis to model-based approaches, with botanical interpretation and management-oriented questions. Analytical outputs showed that taxonomic abundance, dominated by Arecaceae and Fabaceae, did not always correspond to structural dominance measured by total basal area. In addition, height–DBH models fitted for Roystonea and Carapa highlighted interspecific and between-bed variation within the arboretum. Student submissions reproduced and adapted the analytical workflows, while instructor feedback identified difficulties in regression interpretation and model diagnostics. Overall, the experience illustrates how dendrometric data from a living collection can be incorporated into applied statistics teaching while also providing information for collection assessment and future monitoring.
items.authors: Jorge Makhlouta Alonso, Lucas Costa Monteiro Lopes, Luisa Ridolph Tostes Braga, Juliana Cabral, Mylena Cabrini, Ángelo D. Plata-Castro
items.category_raw: Journal of Zoological and Botanical Gardens

items.title: Ripening Dynamics of Artisanal and Semi-Industrial Sjenica White Cow Cheese in Brine: An NIR Spectroscopy and PCA Approach
items.abstract: This study evaluated the quality dynamics of artisanal (A) and semi-industrial (S-I) Sjenica white-brined cheese during 60-day ripening and assessed the agreement between a commercial near-infrared (NIR IR) spectroscopy calibration and reference methods for process monitoring. The reference methods showed that cheese type significantly affected proteins (p = 0.002), pH (p = 0.001), titratable acidity (p = 0.001), and fat-in-dry-matter (FDM; p = 0.038). The S-I cheese demonstrated superior hygiene under mandatory HACCP principles (E. coli max 1.73 log CFU/g vs. 3.72 log CFU/g in A). Ripening time significantly altered the color and texture profile analysis (TPA) parameters (p 0.05). Principal component analysis (PCA) completely discriminated both cheese types at day 60, based on CVS color (86.27% variance) and textural attributes (87.08% variance). Sensory evaluation showed that assessors could discriminate between the two cheese types, while both maintained high overall acceptance. Deming regression and Bland–Altman analysis revealed poor quantitative agreement, with NIR systematically underestimating dry matter (−2.49 g/100 g), fat (−1.88 g/100 g), FDM (−1.80 g/100 g), protein (−1.04 g/100 g), and NaCl (−0.40 g/100 g). Overall, the results demonstrate that the production system significantly affects the physicochemical, microbiological, textural, and color characteristics of Sjenica white-brined cheese during ripening, while both the S-I and A cheeses retain high sensory acceptance.
items.authors: Vladimir S. Kurćubić, Matija D. Munjić, Slaviša Stajić, Sanja Đurđević, Marko Dmitrić, Saša Živković

items.title: FisherShield: Sequential D-Optimal Anti-Rewards for Deployment-Time Reward Privacy in Reinforcement Learning
